This game was incredibly overhyped and in my opinion, below average. While it's not a terrible game, it's frankly boring, with repetitive shooting gameplay between cutscenes. Towards the middle of Chapter 4, I found myself wishing I was already finished with it. I really had to force myself to get to the end.
That's not to say that I didn't find any good qualities in this game. Stylistically, I liked the cinematic visuals. There were even summaries at the beginning of each chapter, making me feel like I'm watching a TV show. The plot made some sense of the supernatural phenomena, but never came together for me. I didn't know what was really going on most of the time. The soundtrack was nice; I wish we heard more varied tracks throughout the game rather than the same two atmospheric tracks while walking everywhere. Voice acting was decent, but I didn't like Alan's voice very much in comparison to the other characters' voices. Something about the delivery seemed hollow.
Gameplay is where things turned sour. I actually don't mind linear games, but each puzzle for plot advancement was too simple; the answers were quite literally laid out along Alan's path. Each encounter with dark entities relied on jump scares, and fighting got incredibly stale. I did have some intense moments, but most of the running and shooting was a bunch of hoopla that didn't contribute any substance to the story.
Furthermore, my experience was negatively impacted by buggy controls. For example, the run and dodge button are the same, leading Alan to frequently dodge when there aren't any enemies around. Alan already has the worst stamina ever (seriously man... go do some cardio) so I don't need him wasting his breath. Another issue that drove me mad was that the camera kept resetting to the default position with Alan on the right side of the screen. l prefer Alan on the left, but the POV reset after every checkpoint and cutscene, even after getting out of a car! Lastly, something about the game physics looked really ragdoll-like. Not only was the fluid animation hard on the eyes, but it also made controlling Alan difficult, as he was zigzagging like a sidewinder across the screen.

As a port I was expecting there to be a lot of problems with this game. But it seems to have been ported well, as  I never once crashed or glitched the entire time I played this game.
As for the game itself...
If I had to describe this game to someone deciding whether or not to buy it, I would say:
"Did you enjoy Resident Evil 4? Because this game is a lot like that, except you care about the main character much more, the plot actually matters, and this game is much creepier".
What makes this game is the story. It is engaging, creepy, pop referential, and served up as episodes (as if it was a tv show you were watching). You -need- Alan Wake to succeed. You want to find every manuscript page if only to get a little warning about what is coming.
The sound design is excellent. Having a surround system I was able to hear the enemy approach giving me just enough warning, to dodge an Axe swing and run. The game is sometimes so quiet the only sound is your own breathing. Like I said, the game is very effective at being creepy.
The graphics themselves are great. This game has some of the nicest water I've ever seen in a game. The volumetric fog is nice, and the shafts of light you run to as you are chased look gorgeous. The only thing graphically, I wish they had worked on in the porting process is the character textures, as they are the only thing in the game (to me) that looked like it came directly from a launch 360 title.
The game mechanics are well done. I never felt hindered by the button arrangement, and the items that you need to interact with and use are straightforward. They say that the best game mechanics are the ones you just don't notice, and that holds true here.
I heavily recommend this game.
Edit (11-26-16): After all this time I still can't recommend this game enough. It makes me a little sad that games like Alan Wake are so rare.

I rarely have time to play games, and when I do its main purpose it to clear my head - something I can pick up and leave at any time. This game sucked me in... not immediately... but after a while.
First I installed it becasue I had it sitting unplaid at the top of my Steam library and it had decent reviews.  But it was not until the second session maybe 2-3 hours into the game I got really engaged.
I only have time to play when the wife and kids are sleeping and after all work backlog has been cleard. So my Alan Wake experience took place for a couple of hours around midninght for a about a week. Lights out, headphones on.  A setting I can recommend.
More than once I stayed awake longer than initially intended just to play to the end of the chapter...
Sometimes the story is a bit slow and much of the fighting is repetitive.
Overall the game is predictable, but in the details the experience is often unexpected and unique.
The game design keep my interest long enough for me to forget about the controls that bothered me initially - and quite soon the controls actually feel very smooth. Rather than perfect combat control I feel as if I am directing a movie. Timing light boosts and headshots to trigger showmotion effects and explosions to make my own visual cinematic experience maximized.
I should also say that it is probably possible to play this game with keyboard and mouse - but a Xbox controller I consider a requirement for this game.
To some extent I think taking the role of a movie director/actor is quite a good analogy for this experience. There is a pretty linear but well written story. I control how specific details are acted out and push the story forward. The linearity of the story was not a problem for me. Given the events taking place I had no urge to roam around, explore, chat with game characters, take on side missions etc.. I just wanted to rush forward on my mission, no time to enjoy scenery or look back. That is also why I find some of the elements in the game a bit too slow. I would like to have the found manuscript pages read to me while still moving too keep the tempo up. The NighSprings episodes could have been removed or reduced to situations where it would be natural to watch some TV (the cut schene eposide with the recorded talkshow is a good example on where it made sense to watch).
If you have not played this game already I do recommend it. For me it was a unique experince. I urge you to bring your imagination and help push the story pace a little bit. If you explore too much and linger when you should run you risk getting bored.  When you use up all your batteries and you just have a few rounds of ammo and you are trying to outrun most danges while dealing with the unavoidable obstacles that comes in your way - that is when it starts to get exiting.
10/10. Would stare at again.

A decent shoot-em up that plays like an unreal tournament single player game. You run around the map holding the fire button fragging either aliens or alien teleporters with an occassional boss showing up. You collect data points from dead aliens to upgrade the super soldier/robot known as the enforcer with stat boosts and new weapons that can be upgraded as well. Your only company is the lispy scientist who created you in the threadbare story. With some more game mechanics like precision aiming(the ability to look up and down) and more involved melee or platforming this game could have been a lot more engrossing, but with a simple A.I., a loose game balance with power-ups and weapons spawning randomly around you, and little strategy to use besides circle strafing it feels like it would be more at home at an arcade. The game entertained me more towards the last half of the five hour campaign when I became a powerful killing machine; bunny hopping around the map at lighting speed, chopping up the dozens of onscreen enemies with a spinning sword or shocking them with chain lightning,and blowing them to pieces with a cluster of rockets. It was worth the couple of dollars I paid for it. (The game ran perfectly for me after I turned off dynamic lighting and changed the compatibility to windoows xp)  7/10

I tweaked some settings and installed a re-shade and the game looks pretty good now.  Is it how I think a game releasing in 2016 should look?  Not even close. I'm not sure why they chose to use just FXAA (and a terrible implementation at that) for anti-aliasing and provided no other option.  And to top it all off you can only knock it down too Low.  You can't completely turn it off.  This is the source of the blurry graphics.  That's all FXAA does, is it uses blurring to fix jaggies on the screen.
PROS:
•	Great story so far.
•	Amazing soundtrack.
•	Top notch acting.
•	They nailed the mindset for the time period.
CONS:
•	Poor frame rate.
•	Graphics look like they would run on an Xbox 360 or PS3.  This is definitely different than     the game play that has been shown for months.
•	Control scheme is a little weird, but seems to better with the new patch.
•	Still suffers from frame rate issues, even with the patch to unlock it.
Do I recommend this game?  Yes, I absolutely do based on the Pros outlined above.  If the game didn’t have a good story, I wouldn’t be able to recommend it in its current state.

If you want to reshade the game to make it look better, here are the instructions which should help.
A quick ReShade preset that basically saturates some of the colors and adds sharpness. The Mafia 3 PC port is a giant mess right now, so this should at least make things a little bit better.
Install Instructions (Kinda complicated, don't blame me) :
1. Download ReShade 3.0 from here:

2. Install it to the Mafia 3 game directory and select "Direct3D 10+" as the library. Install the reshade-shaders that it asks you to as well.
3. Go through the ReShade in-game tutorial.
4. Download the We Wuz Colorful preset. You can find it by doing a Google search.  I can't link it here because the Steam filter just removes it. Paste the preset into your Mafia 3 game folder.
5. Go back to your Mafia 3 game folder, open dxgi.ini and add this line to the file under the [GENERAL] section: PresetFiles= E:\Games\Steam\SteamApps\common\Mafia III\WeWuzColorful.ini
6. You may want to change the file path above, but once you're done, save the file.
FINAL STEP: Press Shift+F2 in-game and select the We Wuz Colorful preset. You can select it from the dropdown menu under the "Home" tab.
I am using the following settings in-game  to help out a bit with the blurriness as well as inconsistent frame rate with the new patch:
Depth of Field - OFF
FOV - 75
Motion Blur - OFF
Anti-Aliasing - LOW
Volumetric Effects - Low
Reflection Quality - Low
V-Sync - ON
FPS - Unlimited
These settings allow me to run the game at a solid 60FPS with pretty good visual quality.
I also went into the NVidia Control Panel and enabled AA there and set the mode to Override any application setting.

While I missed the original Wasteland I got to play every game in the Fallout series. I believe that this game is a worthy successor, albeit not as good as the early Fallouts. It has the same perspective as Fallout 1 and 2, but is now using a 3D engine. The game is a fair bit more combat heavy compared to Fallout 2, but unlike Fallout Tactics has a far deeper role-play element to it.
+ Character creation is quite deep with plenty of attributes, skills, and derived stats. You get to create four characters at the start of the game and up to three more NPCs can join your group at a time. There are enough skills to make you want to create specialized characters for different purposes. There are skills for using different types of weapons, social skills, ability to perform certain actions such as lockpicking, safecracking, using computers, medical skills, etc.
+ Combat is turn-based and has a feel very similar to the early Fallout games except that you get to control a party instead of just one character. NPCs that join your group will sometimes choose to do their own thing if you do not have a character with high enough leadership. You get a certain number of action points to perform actions during a character's turn such as moving, using one of the weapon's firing modes or an item, reloading, and so on. Cover exists and increases both aim and defense of a character in it. When and how often characters get to move depends on their combat initiative.
+ Game is long and completing it with all of the sidequests can easily take 60 hours. There are plenty of different locations to explore and while there are radioactive walls that prevent you from going to certain places before you are supposed to in the story line you generally get to decide where do you want to go.
+ Story and writing are both solid. A lot of quests have multiple solutions and in a number of cases social skills can help avoid confrontation. Decisions you make will affect the ending and the ending itself will clearly show the results of your actions with slides explaining what will happen to every place you have visited.
+ Great ambient soundtrack from the same composer who created music for Fallout 1 and 2 as well as Planescape: Torment and a number of other games.
+ While overall graphical quality is quite poor by today's standards and character models especially could use an improvement, I feel like the designers and artists have made the most out of a kickstarter budget.
- Most of the loot in the game is completely random and changes on reload encouraging save scumming. It is completely possible to crack a well-protected safe only to find a few bullets in it while a game reload could give you a nice weapon instead. Furthermore most of the loot is broken down into tiers based on location or your place in the story line so there are often points in the game when you know your party is equipped with best equipment possible until you progress further making looting until that point completely unexciting and even becoming tedious with how plentiful containers are. Also a number of items that are marked as junk end up having a purpose in some of the quests.
- Some balancing issues make certain weapon types completely useless throughout the game. If you choose wrongly in the beginning you will feel screwed later on.
- Due to how plentiful combat is higher difficulty levels require very specific character builds to make the most out of combat initiative and action points in order to progress. If you want to create a role-play party my advice is to stick to the default difficulty level.
- The game still had plenty of bugs upon release, especially in the second half of the game. The very last few areas also feel like they have been a bit rushed, but at least the game ending is satisfying.

I've just finished all parts of the story and can finally come to a conclusion.
+ The core combat gameplay is still great, with very welcome new features
+ Nemesis system is even more terrific than before
+ Sieges are fun
+ The first three acts are great
+ Graphics are nice and smooth
- The final act is quite repetitive. Also, I would have liked some kind of final boss or just something different at the end. Having said that, I still played all the way through
- Pacing issues. Your enemies likes to present themselves when you meet on the battlefield, freezing the action for a few seconds. This is cool in the beginning, but a nightmare during sieges since it kills the flow and disorients you in the chaos
Honestly, the microtransactions option seems completely meaningless. It was clearly an after-thought.
I did not spend any real money in the market store and still had over 70.000 in game coins at the end, with nothing to spend on. As for what you can spend on:
- Followers: You can get them just by dominating enemies, which is also fun
- Gear: The legendary sets are pretty useless, I hardly ever used any set bonueses, so gear isn't a concern. You'll get it just by playing. Which again, is more fun
- Boosts: For example a boost to XP. Since enemies scale to your level, and you'll pretty quickly get enough ability points to max out what you need, getting XP faster seems pretty meaningless. Actually, having a high XP rate in the final act could make it harder since you'll leave your old followers behind faster
I enjoyed my time with the game and look forward to content expansions/DLC.
Highly recommended.

The Witcher 2 is probably the most mature game I have played in many years. I originally bought the release day version and I must say that 2.0 makes the game more accessible and harder at the same time; both for the better I assure you.
The environments are dark, gritty and real and the themes are based around murder, deceit, betrayal and of course, mature content.
The gameplay is hack and slash third person with an assortment of rpg elements and a massive character chart which allows you the choice of mage, warrior or alchemist trees to choose from, all with their own pros and cons.
I must warn you, however, this game can kick your♥♥♥♥♥on Easy if you don't pay attention.
If you love replayability and an engrossing story, you will find them both here in a deluxe package with multiple branching story lines that require you to play through the game many times to see them all.
The Witcher 2 is heavily action oriented and you have to think and prepare before battles instead of blindly entering combat situations. You cannot turtle and pop potions mid combat, you must prepare and drink potions while meditating outside of combat. Potions heal over time or cause damage over time effects etc.
If you are an achievement fiend you will be welcomed to one exceptionally hard achievement to obtain: Madman. This calls you to play the game with save disabled, the game saves for you and if you die it deletes your save. You also die rather easy on this difficulty, but it's just an option for hardcore fans.
There are 3 mini-games of sorts to play to take a break from exploration and questing:
- Arm Wrestling
- Dice Poker
- Fist Fighting
All of which allow you to increase your oren supply (money).
If you have a powerful rig and want to play one of the best RPGs in as long as I can remember, pick up The Witcher 2.
And.. When you get bored, you can step up in to the Arena and test your ultimate mettle.

To date, one of the most boring and generic shooters I've ever played.
Loyal fan of the XCOM franchise?  Want another high-quality TBS?  Maybe an interesting tactical spinoff involving flight simulation or RTS elements?  AH HAHAHAHHAA... no.  Get out.  That's right, screw you.  And you.  Screw all of you, and myself, SCREW EVERYTHING!
Three enemies (some kamikaze droid, the sectoid, and what I'm guessing was supposed to be a chryssalid) are spammed at the same reactionless drone that does random crap like touching civilians to beam them up to the enterprise or killing the same transporters.  Yes, every map, every objective-- it's all the same.  Three weapons total that you can't switch in and out of but instead just get whatever you picked up last and roll with it, three enemies types constantly spammed at you, two possible objectives.  Zero variety whatsoever.
Also, its graphics... I know it's an old game, but were they even trying?  The animations themselves are absolute garbage, everything in the world feels static and bolted down.  Unlike Half-Life, Unreal, or any other "classic," the environments feel like nothing more than cardboard cutouts spread along a graph.
Then we get the annoying announcer.  Judging from the repetitive gibbing of Sectoids I guessed this wasn't a kids game, but I was probably wrong.  The announcer is the same poorly acted scientist that makes sure to compliment you in a childish way every time you shoot your gun at a transporter that you were supposed to take down.
I wish I could say ONE good thing about the game, on the fact alone that it has the X-COM name carelessly stapled onto it.  But no, that only makes me hate it more; this game KILLED X-Com to begin with, and it has NOTHING going for it.  It fails to be an RTS at all, it fails to lack ANY kind of cohesive thought, and worst of all, it can't even pull off its shooter mechanics competently.  It's a thoroughly lifeless MDK clone that deserves to be buried in a landfill and covered up.
Final verdict: 3/10.  Generic, worthless, low-budget shooter 'game.'  I've seen better in free unity games.

Currently writing this with 20 hours on record, and I feel like I can accurately review this game. First off, this is my review, meaning that this is my opinion on different aspects on the game, so there's no reason to get upset if you disagree with something I write. Now, before we get into the pros/cons I want you all to know that this game is heavily story driven, there are nowhere near as many things to do free roaming like ther was in Mafia II. So if you're expecting a good free roam, maybe GTA will be better for you. Also, the decisions you make in the story do have an impact, so think before you choose.
Now onto the pros and cons.
Talking with contacts can be repetitive as the camera is stationary and characters cycle through a small list of preset animations.
No character customization, your outfit is set and can only sometimes vary depending on the mission.
This is not as free roamy as Mafia II was, there are stores to rob that net you very little cash (not even worth robbing). There are no gun stores to buy weapons,

Car crash damage system is a lot more forgiving than Mafia II, a head on collision at 100+mph will not kill you (even on hard)
Money system - Lose half the money you have on you when you die (can get it stored so you don't lose it on death). The money is only used for upgrades/buying a weapon you currently don't have equiped.
The hard difficulty is not that hard, with decent aim this game is fairly easy.
No long 30fps capped (Wasn't a big problem to begin with)
Great story
Good graphics
Driving feels nice
Soundtrack is amazing
Damage system vs. enemies is rewarding (one shot headshots)
Decisions have an impact on how things can go
Overall, Mafia III is a good game, it may not be as good as a free roamer Mafia II was, but it is still a good looking Mafia game with a great story and good graphics.
Would recommend if you like a good story, 8/10

With over 440 hours on this game, I believe it is time to make a proper review of this game! Playing since its Open Beta 37, the game has changed handfold. With a great community and amazing devs, Hi-Rez seems to do their best to here what the community wants. One issue I had with the game came about a reason patch- OB44. Do not be discouraged to play based off other reviews due to the patch! The developers have done their best so far to go hand and hand with what the community wants and has really improved the current state of the game. Improving new player experience by providing essential handouts in currencies, Paladins has never been more fun. Having a multitude of options for customization in champions design and play style, there is something out there for everyone! I will continue to invest time on this amazing game and I hope that you too will give it a chance like I did! See you in the realm!
I will now break the game down into different components.
Free to Play: This game has remained free to play throughout the time I have played. While the game took an interesting turn with the addition of essence, a third currency that is used to create cards and legendaries, I am still surprised with how Hi-Rez has handled the feedback from its community. While essence in the beginning was a **** show for incoming and current players, recent hotfixes have fixed the issue to a point where you can obtain what you want and what you need. Achievements, chests, champion mastery and much more are only some of the many ways to obtain this currency. They even hinted at the addition of disenchanting cards in order to have essence when needed. In order to get coins, the currency used to purchase champions or chests, you just have to play the game! Each day you log in you get a bonus which consists of coins and day 6 and 7 crystals too. Crystals are used for skins in the game and other neat chests. Further, you obtain coins at the end of everygame. Finally, you may also obtained coins from your 3 first wins of the day which total to over 1300 coins a day (3 wins per day). With the additions the game has every patch, it seems more friendly to those who can't afford to pay for games. You do not need to spend money in order to be successful in this game.
Diversity in Playstyle: This game seems to have something for every playstyle you can imagine. You have a turrent placing dwarf who mans the frontline while also having the chance to play the winter witch known as Evie to kill the backline on her flying staff! Every corner you look you may see something you can get into. Blasters and Hitscans alike, there is a multitude of ways to play each champion. Within each champ, you have a loadout system. This loadout system allows you to take 5 cards of your choice available to the champion to customize your playstyle. The addition of champion legendary's has improved the diversity eightfold. The card system allows you to counter your opponents. Have 4 cards in each category, Blue, Red, Green, and Yellow, you can go anyway you want. If you see a frontline, you can choose wrecker to deal more damage to shields. You may choose haven to take less damage or veteran to heal more out of combat. This system allows you to play different from anyone else on your team.
Community: The Paladins community is on that I am proud to be apart of. With patches going out at least twice a month, we see many issues being resolved due to the support from the developers and other employees at Hi-Rez. While patch previews are always nice, it's on every social site including forums that our voices are heard. With the implimentation of the new currency, there was a vast majority of community feedback. It didn't even take a week for Hi-Rez to respond and actually add in fixations to alleviate the feel of such a hard grind. This was done through decreasing costs of legendarys and increasing the amount of essence you may obtain. As for the play base, you will meet lots of interesting people. While every community has your salty players, the majority of players that I have met are nice and welcoming.
Gamemodes: Paladins currently has 4 casual gamemode, a competitive mode, and training area. The 4 casual modes are: Siege, Payload, PVE, and Survival. Lets break each of these gamemodes down. Siege is a gamemode where you capture an objective in the middle of the map and attempt to push it to the enemies capture area. The score of this goes to whoever hits four points first. Payload is similar to siege. In this gamemode, you either start on offense or defense. You then have a certain period of time to either defend or push if you are on offense. The sides then switch at the end of the timer and those who defended must now push past the point to where the other team had gotten in the time they achieved it in. PVE is the next gamemode which is often renamed to the name of theme. This week was 5 Skye's, a flank champion that goes in stealth, named Hide N Seek. This gamemode switches often and consists of a fun player vs. entity type play. The final and newest gamemode in the casual setting is Survival. Survival is a gamemode that goes to 5 points, with each round counting as either a win or loss. The idea of this mode is to kill off every other enemey member on the team. They do not respawn during the round. Note that each team has 5 members. This in my opinion is the fastest gamemode. The Competitive mode is one where you can really show your skill. Competitive is also where you can place on leaderboards and achieve a champion border. While the system may not be in its prime, I must say it is fun. With in this mode, you have a 5v5 siege type play. The next set of gamemodes is the training grounds. This is where you will play for your first five levels of play. The training grounds is where you can play against bots to familiarize yourself with champions, maps, cards, and even gamemodes. This mode has siege, paylod, survival, training where you play against stationary bots (Only you are in the little map) and the tutorial. The tutorial provides basic knowledge to those enetering into the game. To wrap up this section, it is key to note that the time to recieve a match varies for each play, you aren't garaunteed 10 second queues every day. It's estimated time is 2 minutes to 5 minutes depending on the gamemode.
This wraps up my review! I will add information as I feel needed to adress the game as it evolves.

If you're a fan of the original Wasteland, the long-awaited sequel hits just about all the right notes you'd hope for. It builds upon the original's style, writing, skill systems and combat in a completely logical way, without getting "too modern". It's also chock-full to the brim with references to the original, both in dialog and in the locations you visit (the whole first half of the game is basically a love-letter to the fans, as a matter of fact). So if you're coming into it from the same nostalgia-fueled background as me, you'll probably enjoy the game.
As for everyone else, I am really not so sure. The game is good, but far from perfect. The biggest issue is probably that the combat can get to be a bit simplistic and tedious after a while. Although there are elements of strategy to it, you almost never need to do anything "outside of the box" to successfully win a battle. The story is OK, but nothing you haven't seen before - a post-apocalyptic wasteland threatened by a megalomaniacal antagonist... yadda, yadda, yadda. The writing is good overall, striking a nice balance between serious and playful, though some of the dialogue ends up being a bit cheesy (especially towards the end). Two other big issues are the pace and length of the game. It really takes a while to get rolling. This is partly due to the aforementioned tedium in combat, but mostly because of the sheer size of the game. It becomes pretty obvious after a while that the developers just decided "screw it, this is our one chance to do this, and by god, let's go all out"... and "all out" they most certainly did. They threw everything they thought of in there, plus an extra kitchen sink. On one hand, that's admirable and I completely understand it. But I also just ended up feeling that maybe they should have scaled back their ambition just a tad, which would have allowed more time to tighten up and polish the experience overall. There are quite a few bugs in the game, at least as it initially launched. Thankfully, there was nothing completely game-breaking that I found, but there were definitely some bugs in various quests and dialogue options, and a few other glitches that popped up here and there. Finally, I also felt that the skill and weapon systems weren't quite balanced properly. After completing the game, it became kind of obvious that some of my skill, attribute and weapon investments were more or less useless. Again, not the end of the world, but the game could definitely use some additional balance in its systems.
Overall though, none of these minor issues greatly affected my personal appreciation and enjoyment of the game. I backed this Kickstarter project on day one, and don't regret it for a second. That said, I am also pretty forgiving when it comes to these sorts of things, especially when I know what a labor of love the project was for Brian Fargo and his team. So while I do recommend it overall, I would suggest it primarily for fans of old-school turn-based RPG/tactical-type games. Casual players, or those on the fence should probably check out some gameplay videos of the combat, in particular, to see if it's up your alley. If so, and if you are willing to look past a few minor flaws, definitely give Wasteland 2 a shot.

After the game launching with a 30 fps lock, blurry images, low res textures, which was bad enough and not standard for 2016, they now released a patch to fix this. At least the FPS lock.
Great, right? Kinda.
The game, in most parts, runs at 60 fps steady. But every so often it dips in frames. Sometimes to 50, then to 40.
Plus they didn't fix the Alt - Tabbing issue which leaves your mouse pointer on the screen. So I had no choice than to play with a controller, if I didn't wanna have to restart over and over again.
Pro:
- story seems to be a fine thing
- likeable characters
- interesting setting and behavior of the people (the whole mafia/racism thing - "truly historical")
- Stealth gameplay is somewhat satisfying (I'm a big stealth genre fan)
- Gunplay also doesn't feel too bad, I especially like how enemies react to your shots
For example you give them a load of shotgun in the chest, then they'll actually hold their chest and tumble if not die instantly.
Cons:
- fps, like I said, are dipping. Even, after quite some time now, if it's not too often and everywhere.
- crashes, 2 so far
- colors are washed out (Which is fixable by applying a sweetfx reshade)
- a lot of clipping through objects when interacting with them, for example opening and closing (car)doors, or lifting up gates etc.
Regarding the cutscenes, the characters' eyes point into more than one direction more often, even if only slightly off.
- upscaled low res textures
- the sound design is something which you would indeed find on a console.
When the tires are going wild and you hear that squeeching, it mostly comes from the right side, at other points mostly from the left, only slightly using the other ear. No clue what 2K thought when they designed it like that. The sound doesn't appear immersive at all. Also sounds more like it happens behind you.
PC is able to use 7.1 surround sound, where this is purely 2.1. Also due to the consoles only being able to do that, which they ported over to the PC.
The gun sounds are also something which you'd find if you google for open source gun sounds.
____________________________________________________
Conclusion:
This is a very poor port to grab a quick buck beforehand. If they will even fix this mess entirely is uncertain. Let's be honest. Players who are used to quality, which should be a standard on PC, know that this is wrong. We all expected a masterpiece by 2K. Especially when it comes to the Mafia series. They didn't deliver. Not at all.
The right thing to do would've been to delay the PC version. If necessary even by a month or two.
Kudos to the people who could even play it blurry and in 30 fps, I can't. Still no reason to be an imbecilic butt about it. If you are okay with that kind of quality, good for you. But many people are not.
Right now I can't recommend it. If they ever fix it, sure, go for it. The gameplay is actually pretty fun and it has an interesting story. If you feel "Vengeance" can be a good story.
And for people crying about "Don't play on a toaster, go get a proper PC, you mongo".
Specs:
- Windows 10 Pro 64 bit
- i7 6700k stock clock
- GTX 1080 OC
- 32 gb DDR4 ram
- Every single driver up to date including bios
- Nvidia control panel -> maximum performance preferred
- Using Xbox One controller

Honestly, this game is far better than I expected. There's something to be said about taking a formula that works, and then just giving more of it, which is exactly what this is. If you liked the first game, you'll like this one. If you didn't like the first game, nothing that this game does will change your mind. The fact that this game also doesn't run out of things you can do means that there's more to be done in the late game, and additions like pit fights where you can trains your orcs to be stronger are a plus. I can't say there's anything wrong with this game in my mind.
As for the loot boxes, I think they're fine in this game. You can easily complete the game without ever using one, or ever buying one, and indeed you probably shouldn't until you're max level anyway. The ones you buy with in game currency that you earn are fine as well, because you'll earn so much money from melting down equipment that it will never be a problem. You also get things that allow you to custom make orcs as you want, which is a great plus.
I think the major negative for me is that while the various places are cool, navigating them can be a chore, and there aren't nearly enough voices and the like for how many orcs they want to create. I also think there's a bit of a flaw with the adaptation system, because you'll end up with orcs that cannot be killed because they'll adapt to everything that used to be able to harm them. A rarity, but it's happened and it's a problem.
The way I see it, if you enjoyed the first game, you'll enjoy this one. If you didn't like the first game, it's not going to convert you. But it's a good game, and fun to play.

I played and enjoyed Shadow of Mordor, and heck, I played and enjoyed Shadow of War too. But SoW just doesn't have the staying power of the first game, despite their efforts to artificially extend it with a loot grind and the constant need to build up forces to take down and keep fortresses. In fact... I'd say it's this artificial grind that really takes it down a peg.
The Nemesis system still works as a compelling and fun game, but there's just too much of it here -- too much prepwork, too much setup, too much you have to do to take over too many forts. Eventually you run out of new and interesting things happening and it's just a grind of same-y activities.
Add on top of that a story that's really, REALLY weak compared to the first game, on the level of terrible and incoherent LOTR fanfiction, and well... there's just nothing here that keeps me coming back. I'm sure as heck not paying real world money for more orcs to make the grind less grindy, either; I'd feel like a sucker.
All in all, I guess it's an okay game if you get it in a deep sale. But seriously, set your expectations bar nice 'n low, particularly if you're into the fantasy of a Middle-Earth story. SoW does not deliver there.

Your objective is to protect your steaks at all costs from several types of dinosaurs and send them home once and for all. Go Home Dinosaurs! is a simple tower defense game with 3 different worlds. Each world has around 20 levels with different paths and while some of them might prove a challenge it’s all up about finding a decent strategy in order to complete the level. As you advance in the game you will unlock different cards that gives you other types of defenses, some are used to slow down the dinos while others can put them at the starting point or even make them smaller and therefore, weaker.
The game is pretty much violence free and the bright colours are inviting if you want to play this game side by side with a younger player. In order to promote their own creativity and their decision making skills. The strategy in which tools to choose as well finding the best alternative when spending your coconuts to buy more allies can be a good incentive to play and there’s a decent amount of levels and hours to be spent specially considering the low price (if discounted).
By the end of each world you will have a final Boss. Each boss is bigger and while slow, he doesn’t stop. Right before your enemies reach your precious steaks you have two sets of dinomite
that will prevent them from reaching them, however you will lose one steak. If you no longer have this final defense with you it’s game over and in the final bosses this won’t stop them. I finished all the levels while repeating some of them for a perfect level (or because I was failing them) in around 10 hours and I had a fun time with the game. I believe it’s a good choice to play between those heavy AAA titles or just for a quick-short distraction.

I've been between negative and postitive reviews for this game now for some time. The longest I've left mine on Negative has been about 2 years. Trust me, I've wanted to love this game but in the state it was I couldnt... however. NATURAL SELECTION 2 IS BACK BABY! The game is finally at a state again where it's back to the top. I've posted reviews before that were a run down of the content and why it's good or bad but this time I'm gonna focus on game state and community state
Balance is simply at the best it has been. The new MG is powerful but costly, Onos can be taken down easily by a skilled team unless backed by an equally skilled team and the same with EXO's. The flow of the game is perfect now as well, with the option to slowly creep through with a steamroll style siege or to keep throwing nonupgraded troops into the meat grinder for commanders. When troops follow orders, the commanders can have a blast enjoying the tactics they can employ.
The ground combat is where it has always needed to be. Sure guys like me who love automatic rifles still think the AR is underpowered but that's the point. It's good in groups and solo not so much. The before mentions MG is the weapon for thse fans of throwing as much lead down range and reducing hostiles to a mush and it does that job insanely well. Not only this, new animations added to the base load out make them feel weighty, I can't wait for new animations for weapons to come out that move them all to the same level.
Now onto the community. For me personally it's still not as good as NS2's early days but it is getting much better. Gone are the days of being two minutes in and having one team give up and wave the white flag instantly. I've seen more gameplay in one night (the night I'm reviewing) than compared to the week I quit, when you would have a team giving up in two seconds because the other team rushed well and got more res or something along those lines.
The only downsides, some members of the community that are underage for the game love filling comms with spam about 'I FOUND A GLITCH' when in reality they're just sitting on a ledge and CoD gaming has ingrainded that in their mind as a glitch or you get people giving bad info over comms. Try to resist muting people if possible in game but I understand myself they can be frustrating. Hearing a kid after dying say something along the lines of inaudiable screaming and Onos and not give the position of the Onos is frustrating but they might give a tid bit that manages to turn the tide (somehow).
Finally, as a finishing point, LISTEN TO THE COMMANDER AND FIGHT TO THE END!

Go Home Dinosaurs a tower defense game where you play a gopher having a barbeque where Dinos then invade in an attempt to take your food.
Visually the game is bright and has a cartoonish childish look to it that soon grows tiresome to look at. The gameplay here is what kills it. It is incredibly slow to play. Unlike most tower defense games now there is no speed up button to advance gameplay forward at a faster pace. So because of this you are forced to trudge through slow moving enemies advancing forward. You also can not upgrade the towers you do build and are forced to find places to put them since they all take up different amounts of spaces and angles.
You also control the main character himself who can go around throwing coconuts at the enemy. The main problem with this game though is just the lack of fun I found myself not having while playing it. Between the slow gameplay and the fact that the game provided little challenge I just found myself growing bored too quickly with not much in game to keep me wanting to advance into the further stages.
Overall there are hundreds and thousands of better tower defense games out there one could play. This one is lacking gameplay features and fun factor while being made for a younger crowd. Even on a Steam sale I just can't recommend this.

Natural Selection 2 is a near-perfect asymmetrical multiplayer game that integrates the real-time strategy and first-person shooter genres into one package. In Natural Selection 2, there are two teams: the marines, and the aliens. The marines work kind of like your typical first-person shooter. They are, however, led by a commander who can drop health and ammo for the marines as well as placing structures around the map for them to build on their quest for victory. The aliens work a little differently; they tend to fight more effectively in close quarters situations, unlike the marines who can shoot from a distance. The alien players can also evolve into more advanced life forms whom each have their own advantages and disadvantages. Just like the marines, the aliens have a commander. The alien commander works much more independently than the marine commander; however, the alien commander can still provide a lot of support for his team with the structues that he or she builds and the upgrade paths that he or she chooses. The asymmetrical gameplay along with the combination of two outstanding game genres means that there is never really a dull moment, as every match can be interesting in its own way. I definitely recommend that you atleast give Natural Selection 2 a chance.

X-com Enforcer has a reputation of being bad. A bad shooter, a bad use of the X-com IP, and aging badly. However, for this review I will assume you've got it in the X-com Complete Pack rather than spending money on it (Please don't do that, it's not worth 5 Euro/Dollar/monopoly monies in my opinion)
As such, I will actually recommend you play it, after all, you have it from the complete pack so the only thing you can lose out on is time.
It has a lot of bad, and yes, the reputation is kind of deserved. After X-com Interceptor has you beating aliens in space, there really wasn't much else to do in the X-com story. So we're not really getting a story here.
The story is: You're a robot. You wake up. Aliens are attacking. Go kill aliens. And...That's about it. There does seem to be an idea of a story in there but it's kinda hidden.
Simple, but it works. It's slow to start, but you'll eventually unlock bigger guns, the ability to go faster than many projectiles and even more guns, and even more big guns. Did I mention you go fast and have guns? I think I did. Taken as a continuation of the X-com franchise, it fails. Hard. But if you take it as just an X-com based shooter you get as a bonus with the rest of the X-com pack it is less painful, and at times it becomes fun. After a while it becomes an amusing shooter where you slaughter entire hordes of aliens while flying from one end of the room to the other launching spinning disks with blades attached to them. There's the standard (For the time) hidden secrets to find, big levels in which you can explore a whole lot, and a lot of aliens to shoot at.
It also takes a little from bullet hell games, as your bonus points(And I think maybe super speed too) resets when you get hit. You won't die from just one quick hit, but you will find yourself actually trying to dodge things so you can keep going fast.
It doesn't make the game great. But being completely honest, I wouldn't say it's awful and bad either. Don't take it as a hardcore serious game, take it as a casual amusing shooter narrated by an amusing scientist who seems to enjoy watching his creation(You) wreck the alien invaders.
It's not good, but I wouldn't call it bad either. And since it's in the X-com pack you may as well give it a go.
At the least, play a few levels before you decide whether it sucks or not. It might surprise you

If you're looking for a game review of the wonderful game crashlands, you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

I actually wasnt expecting this game to be a thing. I got a a lot of X-COM games in a humble bundle, and I never expected one of them to be a third-person shooter. And a fun one at that. The gameplay is simple, and that works in its favor like you wouldn't believe. All you have to do is run with WASD, shoot and turn with the mouse, and press space to jump. That is all, and it works beautifuly. The game consists of 38 missions, which have a few different styles of completion. It could get repetitive if not for the gameplay and some fun levels thrown in here and there. As far as weapons go, there are only as many as you collect and research, as all weapons and power-ups are collectable. So on to enemies. There are plenty of types of enemies, and when bosses start showing up as regualar enemies, you see just how far you've come. The story is the weakest point, as it is basically there to string together the levels. The voice acting is great, the game sounds pretty good, but there is a lack of soundtrack, though I suppose it is made up for due to the insane amount of shooting you will do. My only major gripe with the game is that since enemies just run towards you, it can force you into a corner, and with bigger enemies, that basically means death.
My final score: 7/10
It was a fun little journey that I think you should play, but thats it. I have no strong feelings toward replaying it like other games, but its still fun, for at least one time around, and with different skins and neat weapons, there is some more fun to be had.

This game reminds me a lot of a game that goes by the name Shadow of Mordor. Both Mafia 3 and Shadow of Mordor are tales of revenge that contain very similar missions throughout the entire games. Most of which include the player absolutely annihilating massive amounts of enemies either in stealth or full blown rage mode combat in order to draw out a boss enemy that they must face off against in order to gain control of an area (Mafia 3) or weaken Sauron's army (Shadow of Mordor). After doing so the player will rinse and repeat until facing off against the final enemy of the game and then boom. That's that. Now I'm not saying either game is bad, I actually love both games (however Mafia 3 a little more). However if both games are so similar why did Shadow of Mordor recieve such high praise while Mafia 3 is getting bagged on by at least half of the reviews out there on steam. Well let's start with what both games get right in my opinion.
.Great story
.Great characters
.Fantastic combat
.Great sound designs
.Fantastic character motivations
.Soundtracks are great
.Both look pretty good
.Deep perk and upgrade systems
.Fantastic voice acting
.Plenty of content
.Hateable enemies
.Badass main characters
Now as for what sets each game apart. Mafia 3 is clearly a different game. Different time frame. Different characters. Different weapons. The works. But the components are almost identical to Shadow of Mordor as far as your goals and the mission structures. Now I know a lot of people are saying the game has crap textures, bugs, and crashes but the game is far from unplayable (at least for me since i have yet to experience a single crash). The bugs dont break the game and neither do the textures although they are dissapointing. Everyone will tell you that due to these problems you should stear completely clear of this game and in my opinion doing so would simply deprive you of a really good time simply because occasionally the textures look kinda bad. People are also saying the missions are all exactly the same thing over and over and ya they kinda are. You go from place to place and kill a whole bunch of dudes and perform one of several different tasks such as an interrogation (either by knife to the throat or driving like a madman with them in the passenger seat) which to me feels super badass, assassinating a sort of mini boss special target (he has what seems to be slightly more health but I'm not sure), destroying enemy supplies, or robbing that location. Sure the bulk of the missions are the same, but seeing as how the combat is so damn fun what with the shotguns, handguns, rocket launchers, grenade launcher, LMG, rifles, automatic weapons, grenades, molotovs, distraction devices, car bombs, combat finishers, tactical vests, and so many upgrades and unlocks and more to come in dlc is the best. I don't see why people aren't rating this game like Shadow of Mordor it's the same formula there. Fantastic combat but mission design is the same thing over and over. Not really a bad thing if most of it is kickass combat combined with a kickass story, cool♥♥♥♥♥time frame, and interesting mechanics and unlike shadow of mordor there are so many upgrade paths in this game you can miss whole trees in a single playthrough so it adds to the replay value.
To sum it all up. Is Mafia 3 a perfect game? Is it just like Mafia 2? Does it change the player's life and make them question what reality is? No of course not. Does everyone expect it to be and do those things? Yes of course they do. Look Mafia 3 has problems and some missing and loved features from Mafia 2 and the world feels a little empty at times but it is definitely worth the money. I got 30 plus hours so far of nothing but fun and that's worth the price to me, and since the story is so good I felt so disgusted with myself after the game was over I mean come on Lincoln Clay is a criminal he does bad things but I was also so excited to kill the Marcanos all over again I restarted it immediately. I just hope in the next Mafia game they up the variety a bit, include some randomly generated mission design in order to add that real sense of taking down the mob in your own way as advertised, and don't half♥♥♥♥♥the outfit and car customization. Cause come on the witcher 3 is only $50 and gives us hundreds upon hundreds of hours of content. We need more and higher quality content.
P.S. people will tell you the driving is bad, but it's not, it's just not GTA V. I think it's really fun but takes some getting used to cause it's new. Also, the collectables are playboys, who doesn't want to collect some of those.

Nuclear Throne is a frantic post-apocalyptic rogue-like shooter bullet hell set in a universe inhabited by mutants and monsters. Made by the same developers who made games such as Super Crate Box and Luftrausers, Nuclear Throne is yet another notch on the belt of great games by Vlambeer.
Nuclear Throne sports pixel art 2D graphics, with each world being unique and completely different. The setting of the game differs between contrasting enviornments such as a desert wasteland and a frozen city. There are many different types of enemies which all look unique as well as menacing, as well as bosses in certain areas in each playthrough, each with completely differing looks related to their enviornment (my favorite is Big Dog). From bugs to robots, from rats to crystals, Nuclear Throne has a wide variety of odds and ends from all corners of fiction.
Nuclear Throne has very nice adventurous music that really helps set the tone of the game. You don't want to listen to boring orchestral music as you fight your way through nuclear wastelands since the rhythm and speed of the music doesn't match the frantic bullet hell style of Nuclear Throne. For the first couple playthroughs of Nuclear Throne, you'll be hearing a lot of the same music because every Area uses one or two different tracks. If you spend a lot of time in say, the first Area, you'll be hearing a lot of the same music, but as you progress deeper and deeper towards the end, you'll hear all sorts of music made by the wonderful composer "Jukio Kuabee Kalio".
Nuclear Throne is a frantic roguelike bullet-hell game that keeps you on your toes and the edge of your seat. One mistake can very well be your last mistake in a playthrough. If you get yourself into a sticky situation, surrounded by enemies, it may very well be your chance to say goodbye to that playthrough. There are many different types of playable characters, with my favourite being "Crystal". Every character has different abilities that you can use with your right mouse button. For example, Crystal can shield himself for a short period, deflecting some shots back at the shooter. As I mentioned before, some areas have their own boss. For example the first Area, the desert, has Big Bandit, who shoots a machine gun and dashes through walls. The further you get into the game, you unlock chances to unlock a Crown, an item that alters the flow of the game that also bears consequences.
The storyline of the game is mainly told to you through small snippets of exposition in the load screens. If you are looking for a deeper take of the Nuclear Throne storyline, you'll have to go to the Nuclear Throne wikia and look at the trivia for characters or bosses. I would like the story aspect of Nuclear Throne so much more if there was little bits of exposition, say, after you defeat a boss. I would really love to know the backstory for Big Dog, my favorite boss in Nuclear Throne.
Overall, I really enjoy playing Nuclear Throne. You can easily pick up a game and play for a few minutes, but you could also easily find yourself into a 30 minute or longer playthrough. If you are a fan of bullet hell or roguelike games, then I think you'd enjoy playing Nuclear Throne, however, if you are looking for a game with a deep story, then Nuclear Throne most likely isn't for you (unless you can swallow the storyline aspect and just enjoy the explosions and bullets). I can definitely see myself playing Nuclear Throne to completion more and more in the near future.

I'm a huge fallout fan, so this game was highly anticipated for me. I tried playing the classic fallout games a few times, but unfortunately their age made the games far too slow and painful to progress through despite their amazing visual style and overall presentation. I picked up Wasteland 2 to fill that experience I always wanted, but unfortunately it just couldn't do it. Overall, the game is very unpolished, and just doesn't have the fit and finish I would expect from a game that's been in development for nearly three years.
Incoming gripe-fest: I can't say too much on the story or progression yet, as I'm not too far into it, but I feel like the game keeps you in areas far longer than you should be in. The Ag center quest took me nearly SIX hours in total, and I don't feel like much was accomplished in that time. The quest system is fairly ambiguous as there are no map markers or anything to even send you in the general direction of a task. I've had bugs make me reload a save from nearly hours earlier just for it to happen again(pathfinding is wonky). The lack of lore is another thing that pains me. The game doesn't go too far into what's going on in the world other than forcing DESERT RANGERS! down your throat for the first hour. Scavenging is weird: there are SO MANY obvious loot crates just sitting around for no apparent reason other than to give you ammo- there is so much ammo that it is never a problem in the slightest. And on the off chance you actually find a hidden safe, for the most part it is RNG, so it is likely you will just find .38 ammo over and over again.
The game does have its merits though despite being quite janky. There is a LOT to do, and for content-per-dollar, I'd say you get a lot out of it. So if you're looking for a game where there is tons to do and you can play it for hours on end, this is a good choice. However, if you're like me and enjoy games with a higher quality standard, you should steer clear-at least until the game is well patched. The game is definitely a fallout fan's paradise in concept, but it just can't live up to it for so many reasons. I could rant all day, but in the end the only thing that matters is: How big of a Fallout fan are you?

Short version: Your enjoyment of this will very much depend on whether you enjoyed Fallout (1/2). If you haven't played them yet, play them instead.
I loved Fallout, so this ticked all of my nostalgia boxes. And really nostalgia is what this game is about. It's a top down post-apocalyptic cRPG with all the party building, xp grinding, side quest hunting goodness you could want. The different areas are mostly interesting. The side quests have multiple ways to resolve or screw up and don't always have a happy ending and often the game provides you with a choice of two (or three) equally bad outcomes. It's also rammed full of geek references
All in all it's hugely enjoyable.
But. It's not perfect. It's almost too caught up in nostalgia and could have done with some modern thinking applied to some of the mechanics. It's not particularly intuitive to start with and the lack of a decent in game tutorial will mean a lot of trial and error at the beginning. A few mechanics are clunky; for example, when you find a trap on a box you still have to explicitly use your demolitions skill to remove it as clicking the box with your demolitions expert will cause him to happily ignore the danger and open it anyway.
The camera thing, while pretty is a little pointless. I never found a situation where I wanted the view anything other than as high as possible and missing things due to not having the screen rotated the right way grates a little.
The first major location you hit will be one of two. Ag Center or Highpool. I hit Ag Center and it was long and tedious. It's not a great introduction to the game and may well result in people dropping the game at this point. Which would be a shame as it immediately improves 10-fold on moving on.
The second half of the game is hugely unfinished. Side quests can be completely bypassed by doing something slightly different and people will talk to you as though you were asked to perform the task and failed it. Then you'll find the side quest later on than you were supposed to, complete it (all the while being told it was a shame you couldn't resolve it)  and everything will flip to the "completed" state. It's as though inXile provided many paths to find/avoid/complete quests but didn't account for it in the dialog.
Nothing is insurmountable though and, with the odd little issue you can get through pretty much all the content. If you can put up with this, it's a blast.
It is, however, expensive. It's priced on a par with big AAA games. And while you can't say they're released bug free, they are generally a lot more polished than this is. I got it through Kickstarter and that was a perfectly acceptable price to pay for it. £30 though is too much.

if you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting
- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper
- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces
Make the Ravioli filling.
- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Make the Ravioli dough.
- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor.
Fill the Ravioli shells.
- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together.
Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.
- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.
Cook the Ravioli.
- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates
Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

This game is a mixed bag. I usually don't write pros and cons reviews, but for this I think it's the best way to get the point across as I'm not sure how I feel about it to be honest. I've enjoyed my time so far, but it's starting to feel like I'm not going to finish the game. This is at best a qualified recommendation so if you see something in the con list thats a deal breaker I'd stay away.
PROS
* Word Design - The city they built looks and feels great, lots of intersting people and stuff going around all the time.
* Music - Some of the best music I've seen in a game from the likes of Creedence, Cash, Stones, The Animals, Presley, Ramones, Hendrix, etc.
* Voice acting is on point - Major, minor and random NPCs are all voiced very well.
* Racism & bigotry - Weird thing to put in a pros list, but it adds a lot of realism to the world and the racists are all at your mercy.
* Lots of Guns, cars, upgrades and stuff to get
* A few interesting and well made characters.
* The shooting feels satisfying at least with a mouse.
* Field of View Slider
PC PORT CONS
* Frames Per Second - 30fps lock has been patched out, but I only get 36fps post patch, so thats no good. At least its stable for me.
* Crashes - I've never quit the game intentionally, it crashes whenever it feels I need a break.
* UI and Menus - They have not properly ported menus and UI to PC. Things are clunky as hell. Settings in the launcher are missing and some are ignored, the main menu has no settings option.
* The controls - pre patch the controls were made by a crazy person who has never seen a keyboard. I spent a long time fixing it, then they patched the game and changed all the controls, even my own settings. The new controls were better than the old ones, but still not good and since they overwrote every setting I had made I had no idea how to do a bunch of stuff so I had to redo all my settings.
* The game does not support extra mouse buttons or rebinding of the mouse wheel. It also has issues with knowing what keys you can set to multiple actions (like when in a car vs. on foot) some keys can't be set to multiple things even though they would never overlap and others can be set to multiple things, but they cause the game to do weird stuff it isn't supposed to.
GAME CONS
* Story - The game starts out strong, but quickly turns into a by the numbers revenge story without any strong characters to interact with.
* Lack of Music - When you're not in a car or near a radio the game gives you no access to its amazing soundtrack. The only music outside of this is some boring suspense tracks that play when you're in a firefight. I understand that it wouldn't be realistic to have a walkman or radio with you, but the result is that the game is quiet a lot of the time and thats no fun.
* The mechanic for taking over the city is a step down from previous games in the genre. It's just not fun and its getting to be a hassle.
* Once you unlock a silenced pistol theres not really any need for further upgrades. The game has gotten very easy, I just headshot all the guards and waltz through the place without any issues.
* The graphics are sub par. This game looks a lot like a last gen open world game, the textures are poor, animations are stilted, models are clunky, faces look strange most of the time, physics wig out often, even in cutscenes.
* This looks, feels and plays like a last gen open world game. Its like they failed to see all the things GTA5 got right and kept at it like they were making an Xbox 360 game.
* The game play loop of taking over districts is monotonous and boring. Its the same thing over and over again for ever single district. Start the mission, talk to NPCs to spawn objectives, kill some guys, destory some stuff, force out the boss, revisit a location you've already been, kill boss. Doing that twice unlocks a story mission for the district. There are 13 or so districts.
As I said I'm having some very mixed feelings about this game. When it works I'm enjoying myself, but every time it crashes I really don't feel like restarting it again. Its a qualified recommendation at best. I'd wait for a deep sale at least. Theres plenty of stuff worth your time here, but it does not feel like it justifies its high price tag.

This is what a Kickstarter project should be like.  They got their support, they took their time developing it, they had it in early access beta for a while, and then they released it when they felt it was finished.
Is it perfect?  No.  But what is?
Two of the things that people complain about with new games is that they are unfinished, or buggy, so lets start there.
Do I feel it was actually finished when they released it?  Yes.  Sure, it has some bugs and some tweaks were necessary, but that is relatively minor, the kind of thing that you expect in patches.
Is it a buggy mess?  No.  A few small bugs, the most severe I've seen is an annoying camera freeze bug that seems to be caused if you try to move the camera while the AI is moving (can't swear to that as the cause though).  Overall, haven't felt it was particulalry buggy, nothing game breaking.
One of the stated goals of the game was to recreate the essense of the original Wasteland.  In this regard I think it succeeded admitably.
The game has a quirky sense of humour that is quite fun, its got a really foul mouth (it has a mature rating for a reason), its got decisions for which there is no best solution, and sometimes the solutions are all bad, its got an interesting story line, the AI gives a good fight (maybe not the best, but decent), some of the fights require you to think about unconventional ways to handle the enemy, and its BIG.  There is a lot of play here in even one run through (mind you I actually read all the stuff that it prints out, so that can add to it).
Graphics wise its not bad, perhaps a little dated.  I find that too often graphics are focused on at the cost of gameplay, so I'd rather they go that way anyway.  Its not a first person game, its isometric view, so that may not be to the liking of some.  For the old school Fallout fans that didn't like the FPS style of Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas, this game may be more to their liking.
Audio isn't bad.  Most dialog isn't voice acted which is unfortunate, but they didn't want to spend money too much money there, so I can forgive it.  Some of the dialog does have Voice Acting though, and its generally been good quality, the sick woman on the radio was heart wremching.  Music is appropriate, a lot of it from the old Fallout games.
If you can't handle reading too much, and are over 18, you should either be checked for ADD, or take a remedial reading course.  Until then, you probably won't like all the reading in this game.
UI is functional, although note that sometimes the terrain gets in the way of your clicking on a spot to move, rotate the camera to get a different angle and you should be okay.  The UI can be moved around to your hearts content, although I haven't bothered with that myself.
Gameplay is good, a few things could be better, but its overall pretty solid.
Combat is interesting and varied, as stated the AI can give a good fight
Story is good and fairly interesting.  RPG aspects arem't bad, but could have been better - I've noticed several times I wish I had more dialog options.  One recent conversation with one of the big bad guys had obvious logic flaws I wanted to jump on, but there wasn't an option for it (although you can type in words, so maybe it was a hidden option, hm).
Overall a good game in the style of the old Fallout 1 and 2, with a direct connection to the original Wasteland (as opposed to the 'spiritual' connection that F1 and F2 had).
I'd give it an overall 8/10.

This game is great and one of the rare must-plays of an RPG fan. Consequences are treated realistically, and sometimes (read: sometimes) you will have to make important ethical decisions that will screw certain factions over in favor of other ones. The companions have interesting dialogue that makes it hard to hate them, and more often than not, you will find yourself genuinely moved. Protips for best ending: Chaos is almost never good. Invest in Smart♥♥♥♥♥and Kiss♥♥♥♥♥skills.
It's to be noted
That being said, there are two major gameplay flaws. Number one is the enemy move range. When the enemy moves, they, more often than not, will move halfway across the map in order to reach you, stand out in the open exposed like an idiot, or both. I admit, the obscene move may be so they can get to you, because without it they likely would be taking 2-3 turns to get into range. But, I fought most of my fights in an old British-style line formation, because the enemies didn't let me get a chance to get into cover! And no, the player characters can't move that fast.
Number two is the allied units' AI. Like the enemies, they will move obscene distances to get within range of the target, but when a friendly sniper tries to run up, out of your units' move and attack range, to melee an opponent that can kill him/her in one hit when he still has ammo in his clip, you know something's wrong with the AI. If you don't want to see allies die, my advice would be to not recruit them. (This applies to random people you meet on your adventures that want to temporarily aid you, not recruitable party members that count towards your party limits. With minor exceptions, they should remain under control.) This, however, is a minor flaw, as friendly NPCs are rare.
Don't get discouraged, though. I love this game, its multiple paths and otherwise tight combat MECHANICS are good. Tactics is an important part of the game, and positioning before a fight can have many benefits. The ending slideshow bugs have been largely fixed, and the game runs well.
