This game is HUGE and AWESOME! If you explore thoroughly and do everything you can, the game will take at least 70 hours. And if you enjoyed Fallout 1 and 2 then you will almost assuredly enjoy this.
But the real reason to play this, and something I don't see discussed much for some reason, are the choices you get to make throughout the game. I've played a lot of games where you are given quests and different ways to resolve them, but this game blows all of them out of the water. Almost all main quests and most side quests have 2, sometimes even 3, different ways to resolve them. And it isn't just a simple resolution with a different reward, characters and sometimes places change based on your decisions. Almost right at the beginning of the game you are given the choice to save one of two towns (or neither) and both places have their own unique recruitable NPC and quests. Not to mention the ever present option of "kill everyone you meet".
In fact, there are unique dialogues put into the game if you choose to kill indiscriminately. For fun I decided to save my game then kill everyone in the mayor's office of the town I saved. Afterwards some anonymous citizen radios Ranger Citadel and snitched on me, so Vargas radios me asking if it's true and I'm given a choice of admitting it or playing dumb. If you play dumb he tells you to go check it out, if you admit it he asks you why and then gives you a free pass this time. I'm pretty sure if I had continued my murdering ways Vargas would send after me the elite squad I met at RC who handle "problem rangers". I reloaded though.
It's not uncommon to go to a town and there be some kind of conflict going on. You pretty much always have the option of siding with one side or the other (or neither), but more than that there are usually different ways to solve it for either side. If you have high enough speech skills you can usually make it easier and/or more diplomatic, or do what the leader wants you to do (like eliminate the opposition instead of finding peace). Although, since this is the wasteland, few people are entirely "good". Almost everyone is bad in their own way, though not always entirely malicious. Sometimes the bad stuff they do is to try to help others, so is bringing them down truly the best choice for that town in the long term?
What really impresses me is not just the incredible amount of quests and their multiple ways to solve them, but all the little touches made based on your choice. In one town there was a guy about to be executed and I had noticed a pre-dug grave for him. After I managed to free him I decided to go back and re-examine the grave, and there was new text saying someone had taken a dump on the gravestone. I love it.
Yes there are some bugs, including quest-breaking ones. But when you understand the mind-boggling amount of connectivity everything has based on quests and the many different ways to do them, then I think you can forgive the relatively few bugs there are currently in the game. And don't worry, the devs are working on fixing them!
In closing, there is an extraordinary amount of replayability in this game. If you love the ability to make choices and see those choices have a real impact on the world around you, then you simply cannot pass this game up. Buy now, no need to wait for a sale!

EDIT: I just beat the game so I decided to reformat the review and add any final thoughts
I never got around to playing Mafia 1 but I loved everything about Mafia 2 back in the day. The gritty realism, the somewhat unique story, and all the small mechanics that made the world feel so real and different from the other sandbox games at the time. If I had to choose right now, I would probably play it over GTA 4. Because of this, I got relatively excited for this iteration. I avoided every trailer, gameplay video, and blog post to not get my hopes up so that I could have an ubiased and uninformed play through this game. But after only a day of playing I have realized that this is a poor mans GTA for a rich mans price.
Pros:
- Story: The beginning, ending, and some of the story missions in between are very well done and will motivate some people to get through the repetitiveness of the game
- Setting: I don't remember any games that take place in the racist South during the 60s, playing as a black man on top of that just sweatens the deal
- Soundtrack: Every time I play a game like Fallout, Mafia or GTA I love the soundtrack. This game is no different. However, it is a let down that there are only three radio stations to choose from
- Characters: The personality for each main and side character is unique and very well done. And their voice acting is top notch. I wasn't suprised to see the long list of voice actors in the credits because no one sounds identical
- Cutscenes: Every time a cutscene starts I have to sit back and just appreciate how good they look. Other than some small shadow and clipping issues, the character models and facial animations are amazingly done. However, this is also a negative because once you get back into the game it brings home how ugly it is
- Story Missions: The only interesting and unique missions are the story missions which take place after taking over a district. There are around 12 of these missions (not all of them are good) with boring filler missions in between each one
Cons:
- Graphics: This game is ugly. The intro cutscene got me excited to delve into a nice looking game, but it is obvious that this is a console port once you actually start playing. It's almost comparable to a mid gen PS3 game. Where are the GTA 5 level graphics that are shown in the cutscenes? I found that the only time this game looks good is at very specific times of the day, and at night. For about 95% of the day, the sun is blindingly bright and washes everything out
- Pop in: This ties into the graphics. Cars and objects pop into view about 50 yards ahead of you, which makes driving really fast in the oncoming lane very dangerous. The pop in is even more evident in the rearview mirror. A wall of brown chases you and swallows everything 50 yards behind you
- Audio: Everything is cranked up to the max. No matter how far away someone is yelling from you, it sounds like they are right next to you. This makes it very difficult to track down the last guy you have to kill
- Driving: I don't even know what happened here. I've tried both driving modes and simulation mode is the most playable, but they both feel like you're driving an arcadey tank that can just plow through any car. I can hit an oncoming car at 100mph and take no damage but slightly nudge a stationary vehicle and almost die
- Missions: There are four different types of missions that are repeated throughout the entire game. It's either: kill/interrogate this person or steal/destroy something. And all of the racket boss missions reuse the same buildings so there are no more collectibles or money stacks to find and pick up after the first visit
- AI: I can't remember the last game that had AI this stupid. They can't see more than two feet infront of them so every mission leads to me running around stealth killing everyone without ever getting caught. And if you get bored of that and want to shoot some people, have fun with enemies that run at you in the open or poke their head out of the same cover until you shoot them. And once you get a silenced weapon the game becomes a joke. You can clear out an entire warehouse without being careful and no one will notice. Two enemies were next to each other talking and I killed one and the other guy kept talking while he took his gun out and walked around for a bit. No reaction to his friend being shot in the head right infront of him
- Cops: Are cops even in this game? Throughout the entire game I only had to deal with them when the story forced it. I have driven through red lights, in the oncoming lane, going 100mph, right infront of a police station and gotten nothing more than a little police awareness bar. I've also gone on a massacre and killed everyone in an area and nothing came from it. Witnesses to a crime will run past a cop to get to a phone booth instead of just telling the officer that's walking by
- Customization: I thought I hadn't gotten far enough into the game yet, but no, there is absolutely no customization. There isn't a clothing store or garage in site so you're stuck with Lincoln's army jacket, and car upgrades are purely performance and not cosmetic
- Weather: The skybox rivals that of old N64 games and the rain is ugly. The most obvious and possibly the ugliest part of the game is that the time of day changes in waves instead of gradually. If you're driving fast enough you can actually race the time change and stay on the line between morning and afternoon. It is very distracting when it's bright out and then suddenly a wave of darkness comes over everything
- FPS: Before the patch, I was holding a consistent 30fps. But since changing it to 60fps I have been bouncing between 24-39fps. My rig is fully capable of running a game like this at max settings at over 60fps. Be upfront with your costumers and tell them that you haven't optimized the game to run at 60fps, instead of leading us on like this
- The Interviews: The idea of having present day interviews with characters from the game was very interesting. But they didn't know when to stop. Between every mission they felt like they had to have a short interview cutscene, which really breaks the immersion of the game. And there were some parts of the game where I was thinking how the hell I was going to pull the mission off. But then you are promptly interrupted by an interview that spoils the entire mission and that everything went to plan. From the very beginning of the game you already know what happens to Lincoln and Sal because of what Father James says in his interviews
Overall:
This game is a huge disapointment. It has its ups and down like any game but its ups don't carry it very far. I miss the days of Mafia 2 with all its little details that showed how much the devs cared. Cars had fuel, you could shop at or rob every open store, stores closed for a day if the employees were killed, cops punished you for breaking traffic laws, cops kept track of your license plate and clothing so that you had to change them, and every mission was vital
to the story and didn't feel like a filler side mission. The thing about this game is that it does nothing new. The story, while enjoyable, is very predictable. And every game mechanic that is present or missing has been done 100 times better before. The Godfather 2, which is a 7 year old game, accomplished more than this game. Wait until a huge patch comes out, or until the game is at most $30. Hangar 13 and 2K, thank you for treating a huge demographic as second class citizens with this abysmal and lazy port

An all-round good sequel to shadow of mordor.  Its not radically different and the only ways in which it is different is that it takes what it had in SOM and improves it, especially the nemesis system. In SOM i never really experinced the nemesis system to its full extent because hardly anyone ever came back when i killed them and very few uruks encountered me twice(not to blow my own trumpet but talion is OP). In SOW however this happened loads i had captains appearing everywhere and each one had a different line to say to me (well, most of the time, bards always said "The singers song will never end" and then promptly lost their heads) about how they hated me for something that had happened to them or another orc. I had one olog who I got from a loot crate(I know, I know) who on his first mission for me caved in one guys head and decided that because that uruks bodily fluids were now all over his face they were now blood brothers and he promptly betrayed me and killed me. I sought revenge and i followed him to the nearest fortress and put a massive hole in his stomach, end of story, except not really (I cant believe I just quoted a poem from my english exam). Later I was wandering around when BAM, ambush, no problem(ologs may be a new enemy for SOW but they're actually really easy to kill since you can dodge every single attack with relative ease), this time I detached his head from his body and thought that has to be it, he cant come back from that. Now, this game has necromancy allowing some uruks
to bring back the dead, and yep, you guessed it, this guy came back. Now this was my first real experience of what this nemesis system had to offer. Ur-Heku drake slayer, who i just beheaded, is stood in front of me except now he looks different, his face is mishapen and he has stitches all over his body to show he's been through a rough time (courtesy of me) and his name has now changed to Ur-Heku the Stitch to reflect his condition. Now thats cool. I immediately wanted to control this guy again except when I branded him he had iron will so I couldnt so I ended up killing him anyway. It is at this point that I travel to another region (this game is huge and has 5!!!) and during the loading screen a tip came up and said that shaming has a chance to remove the iron will effect. Consider me annoyed. Very annoyed
Now, I mentioned the fact the that there are 5 regions (cirith ungol, gorgoroth, nurnen, seregost and minas ithil/morgul) all of which look realy nice and each one different from the others. Gorgoroth has lots of fire and volcanic land, nurnen is more green and natural and seregost is icy and cold. I cant fault how these regions look but what i can fault is the amount of content in these regions. In my opinion the maps may be bigger than in SOM but they dont feel as though they have as much to do in them, this may be because they are spread over a bigger area or there may just be the same / less amount of missions and artifacts as in the first game. Because of this i didnt really feel like continuing to play like i did with SOM because i dont like just wandering around aimlessly, i have to have something to aim for and i very quickly collected all the artifacts and shelob memories(which results in a pretty cool cutscene) leaving me with not much to do.
The campaign is ok. It didnt really feel as though it had any drive or particular reason as to why you were doing what you were doing. It was more a series of short stories that have been brought together in an attempt to make a bigger story when to be honest none of them really gave anything to the overall plot. Although they were enjoyable for the most part in the late game the missions started to get a bit repetetive with just find so and so and kill them missions or some such similar thing.
The endgame in this is a lot better than in SOM. Although the "final" fight with sauron is definitely better than the QTE from SOM i still didnt find it challenging enough to be a final boss, the nazgul in minas ithil right at the begining of the game were more challenging and I died quite a few times but with sauron I killed him first time and it didnt feel very rewarding especially since I didnt get the proper ending. To get the proper ending I had to complete the Shadow Wars which involves a series of 10 stages in which you defend the fortresses in each region with more being attacked each stage. This was a bit of a slog and towards the end I started to get a bit bored of it but i was determined to get the proper ending. I got the proper ending but it was a very predictable ending for all the hard work i just put in but it was a good cutscene at least.
Ok. The biggest problem this game has in almost everyone elses opinions are the microtransactions. I dont see them as that big a deal since they are completely optional and you're not really pressured into buying them. I did buy a couple of war chests to see what difference it made and in my opinion it didnt make any noticeably huge difference it just gave me a few cool looking orcs. Ranks dont affect the game that much in my experince, to me its more of a rock, paper, scissors situation with certain traits being a lot more effective against others and levels giving orcs higher health but otherwise legendary orcs just get a few more traits which doesnt neccessarily make much difference at all.
Overall i'd say it was a decent game well worth the money with a ok storyline, decent loot system and a completely awesome nemesis system.

So, there was a lot of ♥♥♥♥♥torm involving this game. However, let me tell you one thing: It's not as much of a problem as you might think. It does set a dangerous sign for us players who - if we pay for this stuff, we will get more of it. It's inevitable. So don't buy these lootboxes or I will fight you on the side of the street!
Lets get to the game itself tho: It starts a bit slow in my opinion. But when you are finally able to control your character, it's getting really fun. It plays almost exactly like shadow of mordor, just smoother. The parcour is way better now because you can dash up walls which makes climbing superfast, the combat system is extremely well done and very fun even tho sometimes you might get a problem with targeting enemies. In this game, Talion is also able to find and equip weapons and armor found by killing captains or solving quests. Higher level gear has special properties which you can unlock by solving a mini-quest like "kill 2 orc captains with executions". The highest level gear also has sets which greatly impact your playstyle. The vengance set, for example (my favourite by far) enables you to execute enemies without wrath but at the cost of 40% hp. You can further improve your gear by adding gemstones to it, enhancing its ability with lifesteal, more damage or more XP. So - there is PLENTY of stuff to do, its almost overloaded, but never gets confusing.
The highlight of the game are the fortress battles. Those are fun and impressive as ♥♥♥♥. Taking out the warchiefs or let your own captains infiltrate the fortress, and then taking it over - its insanely fun. There are tons of upgrades you can buy for your fortresses or attacking army, and they all have impact. If the enemy fortress has wooden walls, a fire war graug can greatly increase your chances of taking the fortress. However, once you get a hang of the game, you can pretty much solo any fortress in the game which makes it slightly boring.
Then we have one big point: Captain and Boss Battles. Those are fun and impressive as ♥♥♥♥ now. Bosses actually feel like bosses, and captains are finally a challenge. Captains now have four types of weakness: Mortally vulnerable (instantkill), fear (runs away and can be dominated instantly), dazed (gets stunned) and not-immune to (basically normal). So, there still are enemies which can be instakilled by stealth or explosions, but there are also next to unfair enemies which are just brutally hard to beat.
I can't go further into the game without missing something. It's an extensive game and it is worth your money. The Story is pretty nice too, nothing absolutly great, but it's servable. However, the final cutscene is locked behind ~20 fortress battles - something i wasn't willing to go through yet. In the beginning, these battles are fun as ♥♥♥♥. Later on, they become tedious.
Go get the game if you liked the previous game. It's great and worth 60 bucks (NOT MORE!). If you didn't play the previous one, pick up that first, it's really cheap and maybe you can get shadow of war cheaper when it goes on sale.

The John Wick Weapon is pretty solid overall. If at anything, it's decent offering slight more powerful weapons then the close counterparts.
The Contractor Pistol is pretty similar to most other pistols but I think it is alot closer to the Crosskill pistol. Decent damage but a really small ammo pool making headshots an essential on anything above Overkill. However, the pistol makes you feel like a badass. The reload animation, the sound, the incredibly awesome model. It's really nice and really professional. This is also the Heckler & Koch P30L pistol John uses in the movie which is nice.
The Desertfox Sniper Rifle is generally solid. It's the one weapon that feels like a direct side grade to the R93 (Sniper Pack), Mosin Nagant (Historical Pack), or Platypus Sniper Rifle (Base Game). However, if Silencer Killer aced, the Sniper gets about 3.6 more damage then the Platypus. It's not bad but it's not good either. It can be used as a good dodge sniper rifle as it has a concealment of 19. However, it's decent none the less. This is the same sniper John Wick used when raiding Viggo's compound which is the DTA Stealth Recon Scout.
The Jackal SMG seems like a sidegrade, but that's where you are wrong. While offering some inferior stats, this gun offers a tight bullet spread compare to the Krinkov (Base Game), Swedish K (Transport Heists), and the CB 805R (Biker Heists) making if far superior if fired full auto or even in single shot. It also has a wide variety of customization similar to the Krinkov. It offers an interesting forgrip with intergrated flashlight and laser which is something not seen before in the game. Plus it's the UMP-45, who can pass up that bad boy. This SMG, while not used by Wick in the movie, it is used by one of Viggo's bodyguard in the compound.
The Throwing Knife just straight up sucks. Offer 1100 damage, it's nothing exciting. The Javelin has 7500 damage making it superior in every sense. This is almost a sidegrade.
The Mask are pretty nice I guess except for Daisy which is really really nice and I'm glad she got to be mentioned in the pack being as she is Wick's entire motivation in the movie.
Overall the pack feels almost like a reskin pack but it's not because each gun offers a superior aspect to it's other counterparts. Personally, the pack is worth it if you are willing to pay 5 dollars for a good sniper and a good smg. Though, some better weapons could have been added.

TLDR: Siberian Logging Simulator 2014
Pros:
Best mud and offroad simulation, period.
Excellent models of Soviet-era trucks, suspension and gearboxes all respond in a realistic way
Optimization: On Intel chips, this game can run with basically any graphics set, even integrated.
Cons:
No cockpit pov (though stated by the developers will be added in the future)
That wouldn't be much of an issue except for:
The current camera is the most ♥♥♥♥tarded one I have seen in a game, ever. It's almost as frustrating trying to look at what you're about to run into as getting stuck in the mud is.
Lack of diversity on missions and game modes. Currently hauling lumber from point A to B is the only thing to do on the map, though between the mud, crossing rivers, and running out of gas, you can sink two hours into completing a map easily.
Ultimately, it was worth $30 for me because I've been watching this game for a long time.  If you're looking for a thought-provoking story (or a mindelss one), it doesn't exist in this game. If you're looking for flashy 10,000 point combos and click-to-win type scenarios, this isn't one.
IF however, you have an interest in big trucks, off-roading, exploration, logistics, and physic simulation, all of those things are in this game. The developers have made it clear that this game will be updated and expanded in the future, and though it will never be GTA in the forests of Siberia, it can certainly occupy a space on the "Frustration Porn" section of your games library, alongside Kerbal Space Program and QWOP.

An excellent and engaging experience for fans of science/engineering themed games as well as fans of space and rocketry. I would also recommend the extensive array of mods available as they can really add to the experience of KSP.

The story is really thoughtful and the main carrying point of the game. Think of it like Gone Home, Finding Ethan Carter, or any other story driven game. You aren't playing the game, more or less you want to watch the movie that is this game.
That being said the story is really well integrated into the actual game itself, novel transcripts found throughout the world cleverly explain the story in more depth.
SPOILER:
The gameplay itself is where this game falls short, it's repetive for the most part and while original, isn't exactly great. It consists of flashing a light in many different ways on an enemy, then shooting them. The aiming isn't exactly precise by any means and the third person shoulder view means it will play kind of like Resident Evil 4...except worse.
That being said it's not particuarly difficult outside of a few things, the game itself is carried on the premise of the story like said earlier. The story at times may seem creepy and scary, and there are some jump scares but it's more of a thriller than a horror. The characters are actually very interesting and mold pretty well together, it's a game that's a movie that requires you to think about what it's telling you. If that makes any sense.
The graphics despite being a relatively old game, held up extremely well on the PC version, it's actually one of the more impressive games I've seen despite the textures clearly lacking the scenery and details create some impressive visuals. It may not have the sharpness of next gen games, but it really doesn't need it. Also the performance for this game is rock solid, very easy for my PC to run it, very stable no frame dips or stutters despite being as pretty as it is. I was definitely impressed by the graphics of this game even for an old game.
If it's $2.50 (the price @ Winter Sale 2014) definitely get it!

To sum it up. If you like older RPGs like the Baldurs Gates, Fallout 1 and 2, Arcanum or even the oringinal Wasteland, GO GET IT, DONT WAIT FOR ANY SALE! I would not consider this a horror video game, but rather a game inspired by horror books. The story and voice acting are superb, the environment incredibly vivid. The world is highly detailed, withthe environment looking incredibly realistic! If you dont care too much about graphics, this will still capture your attention. Enough about graphics, what about gameplay and story? The narration of the game through Alan Wake himself makes the whole game truly feel like you are reading a book, in a good way! The entire game I felt immersed with my surroundings and the events being told, and was always compelled to continue on to learn what happens next. I wont go into a lot of detail, but I would give the story a 10/10. The gameplay is fairly unique, with the idea of "fighting with light." Unlike many games involving shooting, you cant just run and gun, thats not what this game is about, in fact running and gunning will just get you killed and ruins the experience anyway. Instead, as yout ravel in the woods or elsewhere, you need to strip the enemies of the Darkness by shining your flashlight on them for a while. Once the Darkness is taken from them, leaving them vulnerable, it's time to fire away. But it can be easy to run out of ammo, so sometimes it is better to just run away and dodge their attacks. the gameplay would be a 8/10 for me, with some minor refinements needed. Overall, if you want something fresh and a thrilling experience, this is definitely the game for you!

EDIT: I just beat the game so I decided to reformat the review and add any final thoughts
I never got around to playing Mafia 1 but I loved everything about Mafia 2 back in the day. The gritty realism, the somewhat unique story, and all the small mechanics that made the world feel so real and different from the other sandbox games at the time. If I had to choose right now, I would probably play it over GTA 4. Because of this, I got relatively excited for this iteration. I avoided every trailer, gameplay video, and blog post to not get my hopes up so that I could have an ubiased and uninformed play through this game. But after only a day of playing I have realized that this is a poor mans GTA for a rich mans price.
Pros:
- Story: The beginning, ending, and some of the story missions in between are very well done and will motivate some people to get through the repetitiveness of the game
- Setting: I don't remember any games that take place in the racist South during the 60s, playing as a black man on top of that just sweatens the deal
- Soundtrack: Every time I play a game like Fallout, Mafia or GTA I love the soundtrack. This game is no different. However, it is a let down that there are only three radio stations to choose from
- Characters: The personality for each main and side character is unique and very well done. And their voice acting is top notch. I wasn't suprised to see the long list of voice actors in the credits because no one sounds identical
- Cutscenes: Every time a cutscene starts I have to sit back and just appreciate how good they look. Other than some small shadow and clipping issues, the character models and facial animations are amazingly done. However, this is also a negative because once you get back into the game it brings home how ugly it is
- Story Missions: The only interesting and unique missions are the story missions which take place after taking over a district. There are around 12 of these missions (not all of them are good) with boring filler missions in between each one
Cons:
- Graphics: This game is ugly. The intro cutscene got me excited to delve into a nice looking game, but it is obvious that this is a console port once you actually start playing. It's almost comparable to a mid gen PS3 game. Where are the GTA 5 level graphics that are shown in the cutscenes? I found that the only time this game looks good is at very specific times of the day, and at night. For about 95% of the day, the sun is blindingly bright and washes everything out
- Pop in: This ties into the graphics. Cars and objects pop into view about 50 yards ahead of you, which makes driving really fast in the oncoming lane very dangerous. The pop in is even more evident in the rearview mirror. A wall of brown chases you and swallows everything 50 yards behind you
- Audio: Everything is cranked up to the max. No matter how far away someone is yelling from you, it sounds like they are right next to you. This makes it very difficult to track down the last guy you have to kill
- Driving: I don't even know what happened here. I've tried both driving modes and simulation mode is the most playable, but they both feel like you're driving an arcadey tank that can just plow through any car. I can hit an oncoming car at 100mph and take no damage but slightly nudge a stationary vehicle and almost die
- Missions: There are four different types of missions that are repeated throughout the entire game. It's either: kill/interrogate this person or steal/destroy something. And all of the racket boss missions reuse the same buildings so there are no more collectibles or money stacks to find and pick up after the first visit
- AI: I can't remember the last game that had AI this stupid. They can't see more than two feet infront of them so every mission leads to me running around stealth killing everyone without ever getting caught. And if you get bored of that and want to shoot some people, have fun with enemies that run at you in the open or poke their head out of the same cover until you shoot them. And once you get a silenced weapon the game becomes a joke. You can clear out an entire warehouse without being careful and no one will notice. Two enemies were next to each other talking and I killed one and the other guy kept talking while he took his gun out and walked around for a bit. No reaction to his friend being shot in the head right infront of him
- Cops: Are cops even in this game? Throughout the entire game I only had to deal with them when the story forced it. I have driven through red lights, in the oncoming lane, going 100mph, right infront of a police station and gotten nothing more than a little police awareness bar. I've also gone on a massacre and killed everyone in an area and nothing came from it. Witnesses to a crime will run past a cop to get to a phone booth instead of just telling the officer that's walking by
- Customization: I thought I hadn't gotten far enough into the game yet, but no, there is absolutely no customization. There isn't a clothing store or garage in site so you're stuck with Lincoln's army jacket, and car upgrades are purely performance and not cosmetic
- Weather: The skybox rivals that of old N64 games and the rain is ugly. The most obvious and possibly the ugliest part of the game is that the time of day changes in waves instead of gradually. If you're driving fast enough you can actually race the time change and stay on the line between morning and afternoon. It is very distracting when it's bright out and then suddenly a wave of darkness comes over everything
- FPS: Before the patch, I was holding a consistent 30fps. But since changing it to 60fps I have been bouncing between 24-39fps. My rig is fully capable of running a game like this at max settings at over 60fps. Be upfront with your costumers and tell them that you haven't optimized the game to run at 60fps, instead of leading us on like this
- The Interviews: The idea of having present day interviews with characters from the game was very interesting. But they didn't know when to stop. Between every mission they felt like they had to have a short interview cutscene, which really breaks the immersion of the game. And there were some parts of the game where I was thinking how the hell I was going to pull the mission off. But then you are promptly interrupted by an interview that spoils the entire mission and that everything went to plan. From the very beginning of the game you already know what happens to Lincoln and Sal because of what Father James says in his interviews
Overall:
This game is a huge disapointment. It has its ups and down like any game but its ups don't carry it very far. I miss the days of Mafia 2 with all its little details that showed how much the devs cared. Cars had fuel, you could shop at or rob every open store, stores closed for a day if the employees were killed, cops punished you for breaking traffic laws, cops kept track of your license plate and clothing so that you had to change them, and every mission was vital
to the story and didn't feel like a filler side mission. The thing about this game is that it does nothing new. The story, while enjoyable, is very predictable. And every game mechanic that is present or missing has been done 100 times better before. The Godfather 2, which is a 7 year old game, accomplished more than this game. Wait until a huge patch comes out, or until the game is at most $30. Hangar 13 and 2K, thank you for treating a huge demographic as second class citizens with this abysmal and lazy port

Civilization 3 is the third installement in the popular turn-based strategy series and personally my favorite.
First of all this title still holds up tremendously well nowadays, it runs on newer operation systems and you can tweak the resolution in a file making the game really great to play. There aren't any issues at all.
Civ3 is not as complex as Civ4 and doesn't have such intricate indepth mechanics but still manages to keep the player busy, you have to manage several aspects of your empire. The more streamlined gameplay makes this Civilization my favorite, it's easy to understand but yet very hard to master. You get down the basics really fast but in order to be good at it, you need some serious practise. There are tons of different civilizations to choose from and many different scenarios. The included expansion offer even more content. The AI is really good and easily challenge you, even on lower difficulties.
The visuals are also nicely presented, the 2d sprites look good and have a more realistic touch. The soundtrack and soundassets are also amazing and do a great job immersing yourself into the game.
Overall this is just an well designed game and incredibly enjoyable. I recommend this game a lot.

Much has been written about “Game Feel”, yet it’s still a nebulous and largely indefinable concept. On the surface, Nuclear Throne isn’t special. Top-down, rogue-lite shooters are abundant on Steam these days, and it doesn’t ostensibly do much to distinguish itself. But Nuclear Throne simply FEELS wonderful to play – a combination of tight controls, punchy sound effects, an energetically grimy soundtrack, and a satisfying gameplay loop establish Nuclear Throne as the best of its genre.
At times, the RNG can generate level layouts that border on unfair, but spawning in an unfortunate location and blasting your way out of imminent doom is awfully satisfying. Yes, certain weapon drops can make your run much easier, but no weapon build is truly unplayable (save for the Disc Gun, maybe). Progression is measured not through unlockables but by your increasing skill level, and very few games have made incremental success feel as gratifying to me as Nuclear Throne. The game is brutally difficult, so it’s definitely not for everyone. For anyone who enjoys the challenge of mastering a game’s nuances through repetition and practice, I highly recommend Nuclear Throne. Its seemingly simple components combine to induce a state of Flow in me the way few games ever have.

Great game! And if you were wondering, this is NOT a pay 2 win game! There is a shop in the main menu, but the only things you can buy are badges and skins which are only cosmetic features for your soldier. They do not help you gain an unfair advantage unlike most free 2 play FPS games. Every gun you cam get is earned through getting kills, which award you with in-game cash to buy better guns. My tip to get more kills in this game is to: 1. By a SPAS-12 shotgun at the very start of the match -> 2. Kill enough dudes until you can afford the AK-47 -> 3. After you buy the AK, kill more dudes until you can afford the maximum 100 point body armor. 4. Now that you have the basic needs, you can continue killing until you can afford an AWP or LMG -> 5. Repeat same steps in next match. This tactic works best for me and it's helped me improve my game a lot (With this strategy, I get over a 2 KD average each match). Another piece of advice is to just hip fire, don't bother aiming down the sights unless you are holding down a choke point or using a sniper rifle. Spraying and praying will kill people ALOT better/faster than ADSing. Trust me. Oh. Also, if you meet some good/skilled players along the way, ask them to friend request you. If you have a massive team of good players, you will just rekt the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of ALL the noobs that try to fight back. Overall, this game is really worth a try. Like most reviews I've seen, this game is like a CS and CoD hybrid. So, is you're a fan of either these games, chances are, this game will be a ton of fun for you. But, if you don't like it, just delete it and no harm is done. Besides, the game is only like 200 MB, so it doesn't take up much space anyway. That's about it for what I have to say. Have fun!

This is a pretty awesome game.
You play as either an Alien or as a Marine. Marines like to use guns, Aliens like to nom Marines and are faster.
Both sides have a commander who builds structures for the team and play this FPS as an RTS instead. They use resources from resource points that they've built on or gotten team-mates to build on. These then are used to get more tech and upgrades for everyone else.
Everyone else also gets resources from their controlled resource points. Aliens use them to evolve into different Aliens (and to place structures as Gorge) such as rhinos (Onos), whilst Marines use them to get different guns and jetpacks and mechs.
So your goal is to eliminate all the enemy players by either destroying their respawn buildings and/or command structures. To do this hold more resource points so you get upgrades faster, and go destroy enemy buildings / people with better weapons/aliens so that the enemy team loses their resources.
Have fun nomming people/shooting things/bossing people around!

Ah, Kerbal Space Program. No dout one of the best, if not the best games I have ever played. And im sure that the big "Overwhelmingly Positive" sign on the overall ratings is already making you want to buy it. So, without furtherado, lets get into rating it.
I believe I can give a fairly accurate review, at the period that im writing this I have played around 50 Hourse of KSP.
Im sure your wondering what all the fuss over KSP is about (if you havent already watched a video). Well, ill put it simply: The gameplay is absolutely phenomanal. And im sure everyone who has played the game will agree. KSP is a Space Simulation Sandbox Physics game, where you get to construct your very own spacecraft using a wide variety of parts. The building system is drag & drop, and there are 2 classes of things to construct: Spacecraft, or Planes (Also can be Spaceplanes). Once you finish constructing your wonderful craft, you can explore the solar system, and kerbin (earth). You get to drive your spacecraft, organize manuevers, set up experiments, etc.
There are three modes in KSP: Carreer, Sandbox and Science (Classic Carreer).
In carreer mode, you do as said above. However, you have to worry about money, science and reputation. Money is pretty self explanitory, but I bet your asking "Whats science?". Well, science is what you earn after completing an experiment. Different experiments in different places yeild different amounts of science. Science can be used in carreer mode to research a wide variety of technologies to add on to your spacecrafts & planes. Reputation is what you earn by getting a kerbal safely back home. You can lose rep by a malfunction in space.. and that explosion.. I can still hear jebs little screams!
In Sandbox, you can construct whatever you wish without having to worry about Money, Rep & Science. You have every part unlocked, infinite funds, and ininite rep? Im not sure, never really checked.
In Science Mode, you get to play the original carreer, in which you only have to worry about science. Hence the name.
There are many planets to explore, and personally, I love to set up mini-bases on KSP's equivilent of mars (Duna)!
10/10

This isn't a bad pack for those who like concealment builds. Otherwise you can safely ignore this one. Maybe pick it up on sale though as it's far from essential.
The Desert Fox is the weapon I was most interested in, and is basically a straight upgrade over the Mosin Nagant. It has 5 more rounds in reserve and is much more concealable (A maximum of 20 with silencers and related skills). It's pretty competitive with the Patypus 70 and R93 if you equip the long barrel. Some people are complaining the magazine capacity isn't good for close quarters, which makes me wonder why they're bringing a bolt action sniper rifle to fight at close range in the first place.
EDIT: The Jackal is a more concealable CR 805. It's most comparable weapon is the Swedish K. At first I took the Jackal as being the superior weapon, but being fair, the Swedish K has slightly more concealment, has a higher base magazine capacity and more accuracy at the cost of less stability and less total ammo (by 10). I've never been a big fan of the Swedish K, but I am willing to conceed that it is at least equal, if not slightly better to the Jackal.
The Contractor pistol is probably the only weapon that's not very good. The LEO is a better concealment pistol considering it's extended magazine doesn't reduce concealment. I would not consider this a horror video game, but rather a game inspired by horror books. The story and voice acting are superb, the environment incredibly vivid. The world is highly detailed, withthe environment looking incredibly realistic! If you dont care too much about graphics, this will still capture your attention. Enough about graphics, what about gameplay and story? The narration of the game through Alan Wake himself makes the whole game truly feel like you are reading a book, in a good way! The entire game I felt immersed with my surroundings and the events being told, and was always compelled to continue on to learn what happens next. I wont go into a lot of detail, but I would give the story a 10/10. The gameplay is fairly unique, with the idea of "fighting with light." Unlike many games involving shooting, you cant just run and gun, thats not what this game is about, in fact running and gunning will just get you killed and ruins the experience anyway. Instead, as yout ravel in the woods or elsewhere, you need to strip the enemies of the Darkness by shining your flashlight on them for a while. Once the Darkness is taken from them, leaving them vulnerable, it's time to fire away. But it can be easy to run out of ammo, so sometimes it is better to just run away and dodge their attacks. the gameplay would be a 8/10 for me, with some minor refinements needed. Overall, if you want something fresh and a thrilling experience, this is definitely the game for you!

The graphics are amazing in this game, allowing for countless opportunities to take snapshots of the beautiful rural scenery both in light and dark - but even if they weren't, there would still be much to be enjoyed through the narrative that one becomes intrigued and lost in. I cannot overstate enough the narrative genius that is communicated through this game.
There is only one negative that I would have to say about this game, and that is the driving - which can often feel sluggish and untamable. However, this does not in any way detract from the game's overall ability to impress.

After finishing the game (70 Hours) here is my verdict.
Gameplay/
Gameplay is one of the most aspects that drive my judjment towrd any game, the more solid the gameplay and polished the more i invest my self with it.
The battle system doesn't offer much of creativity or presenting a new ideas, compering it to XCOM Enemy Unknown which has a simillar battle system, though the latter is better in that aspect.
The AI in this game is highly underdeveloped, enemies with ranged weapons would charge towrd you despite that it will hinder thier accuracy and hit chances and they don't seem to use the environment In their favor that much, like cover for instance.
The difficulty spikes seems to be absent most of the time regarding that you know what you're doing. I have't encounter any impossible situation that hinderd my progress. All of the hard encouters is doable with a will excuted strategy ofcurse.
Nice and will implemented skills system that add a decent and rich experiance.
_____
Graphics and Sounds/
I don't usually mind graphics in games too much, but I do agree it gives a nice boost to the game experiance.
Graphicly the game is not emprassive at all, varrying between a poor characters design and a moderate enviroment design.
yet there is some nice areas that have some depth on them.
The sounds generally is fairly good, but the game lack variety in the soundtrack department.
_____
Story and Writting/
Likable strory with some nice twists and a bold and brilliant writting.The strongest features in this game is the writting and it's quist line.
The game Intelligently combine decision making with your team's skills to progress through the game, making every playthrough a different experince.
It sometimes present a deep and philosophical ideas but somehow faild to present it properly.
_____
The technical side
Unfortunately the game doesn't excel technically, starting with massive frame drop and graphical glitches.
In the first half of the game the frame rate average at ~90 FPS then drop dramatically in the second half at average of ~35 FPS (680 GTX OC).
A lot of the time the game won't responds to mouse ckicks when initiating skills command.

Phenomenal, just what I had expected and more.
After 50 hours I have finally beaten the game and that with skipping some side quests mainly in the second half of the game, Rarely does a game give you so many choices alot of which are tough moral choices that have very real effects on the game, every NPC except on is killable (The commander in Sante Fe), you can play the game in every way you can think of and killing everyone or betraying the rangers are legit options that you can make and they wont stop you from progressing in the game (they will make the game harder though and I am going to start a game where I am going to kill everyone right after I finish writing this) and dont think killing everyone doesnt have benefits, unlike in other games if you kill a marchant all of what he was selling is takeable.
Some people claim that the combat is the weak part of the game but I have to disagree, the combat feels great, it can get annoying sometimes with some extremely hard fights and with some enemies being able to run completely insane distances.
The story is well writen and there is not a single "bad guy" that fights you because you are evil no one is really bad or good, most of the people in the game are in the grey area, they are all driven by ideology,religion or another motivation and even stories of tiny side quests often have interesting plots and twists.
Everything you see is described in a log of sorts in the lower right side of the screen which adds to the over all immersion of the game
No game comes without flaws though, the game is often buggy mainly in the second half of the game, the game also lacks voice narration and has alot of text which resulted in me skipping alot of text, also alot of times when confronted with a moral question by a so called "bad guy" alot of times it felt to me like I can only say that I agree with him or something that sounds like "What you are doing is injust and we fight injustice" when I actually didn't really play the good guy, I was very much in the grey area, doing things the rangers don't approve of and even lieing to my command after killing civilians and often avoiding the peaceful solution and dealing with problems guns blazing and there was not really a good way to represent the fact that what the bad guy is doing has no benefit to me, at least in my opinion.
Over all this is a one of the best games that I have ever played, everything from the atmosphere to the gameplay is awesome.

I really wanted to love this game.  I backed this from the kickstarter, and I just can't.  It lets me down in so many ways, which became even more apparent having played its spiritual twin Divinity.  From the lack of realism to the let down on tactics, I regret having funded this game.  The orignal wasteland was truely gritty and edgy for its time.  This one can't seem to decide to take the step into adult themes, and follows old sterotypes and troupes that don't bring anything new to the post apocalyptic genre.
The tactics are a joke.  The game imposes penalties for having enemies near you if you have long guns.  As a result, enemies will run past entire groups of armed people to stand next to anyone with a sniper rifle.  The best tactic in almost every setting is to have everyone shoot at the closest enemy until it dies, then repeat over and over.  While some settings are obviously designed for more use of cover and crossfires, the enemies go agro from amazing distances, or are placed directly next to you effectivly nullifying any use of cover.  One of the most annoying things were the traps.  In divinity if your charactor sees a trap, they try not to step on it.  In wasteland, they can see a land mine and will run right over it.  In divinity, you can change the order and arrangement of your team to take advantage of diffrrent skills.  In wasteland they run in a large and random pack, which gets redistrubuted once you engage anyone, making any efforts to protect your snipers and advance your shotguns worthless.
The storyline tries to do some things that are new, but for the most part it felt like a bad remake of the orignal wasteland.  The enemies are the same, the locations are very similiar.  I can't think of any charactors in  it that would be at all notable.
I could go on and on, but at the end of the day it was a real let down for me.

My husband and I decided to play this game together. We took turns; he controlled Shay and I controlled Vella, and I would have to say that this worked out beautifully. I would recommend other couples try this, or perhaps parents with children (not super young children because it gets a bit scary at times).  You can switch back and forth between the two characters at any time, and when you finish one character’s story it automatically jumps to the other character.
We enjoyed the game itself. The artwork and voice acting were amazing. The puzzles were pretty doable for the most part. There was only one time we were both stuck, but there were a few times one of us was stuck and the other was able to jump in with suggestions. This made our experience all the more enjoyable. We also really liked being able to discuss our theories about how the two characters were going to intersect, and the surprise ending of part one made us glad we shared our theories because we were pretty far off the mark and it was nice to share the revelation with other person present.
All in all, I would recommend Broken Age as a game for anyone who likes adventure games or point and click games, or for anyone who loves a good story, but I would doubly recommend you play it with another person. It’s definitely a game that is better when shared.

Gameplay is smooth and casual. Puzzles are logical and consise. I didn't feel stuck or bored once which is a sign of a delicate balance for a quest. At first I missed a button to highlight active areas on the screen. I got used to it in Broken Sword and Deadalus's games. The biggest disappointment I had about Broken Age was "End of Act I. Act II coming soon!" caption after spectacular ending. Overall, highly recommended.

Nuclear Throne is one of the best games of its type; it has variety when it comes to characters, weapons, outcomes, and more, and it is difficult to the point of being awesome at some points, and with loads of replayability.
With characters, you can select ones with speed, with health, with blocking, and with other abilities depending on what you enjoy. You unlock characters as you play, so you have a reason to continue moving forward (aside from the 'just because i like to shoot.')
You have different weapon classes, with everything from arrows to shotguns to explosives represented, and you haveenough bullets to keep things interesting but also enough to progress without a terrible amount of conservation. I like that about a game like this; with a bit of aiming and a bit of luck, you can manage pretty well, and with a few character upgrades, you can do even better.
Speaking of which; through the collection of 'rads' via kills or random placement, you level up and gain abilities. At first this happens around every one or two boards, but later the pickings get a little more difficult due to the enemy type and your distancing. You can get things that allow more health, more bullets, kills giving health or bullets, and on and on. That makes it interesting, too, because it adds even more variety.
I have clocked about 30 hours of game time that Steam has counted and at least 30 more offline, and I have to say that the game keeps me coming back.

While it seemed ludicrous at the time to suggest that a man or even small group of men could evolve a dated FPS engine into an RTS interface without the hand of the divine, the origins of Natural Selection were eventually proven by the discovery of several missing download links. Even with the irrefutable proof we are now privilege to, there are still a few conservative philosophers that argue Natural Selection (and by extension Natural Selection 2) was created by God himself. Great thriller.
Alan Wake is a thriller/horror game created by Remedy (i.e the creators of the orignal max payne).
The story is one of the game's greatest strengths. You play as Alan who is a writer and recently moved away from the city, with his wife Alice, to the country town Brightfalls. Things aren't as they seem in the neighbourhood and you begin to search for you missing wife and unravel the secrets in the town. The story has plenty of twists and will definitely keep you guessing what will happen next, burrowing elments from 'Stephen King's' films. It is also broken into episodes so you can take a break from the game when you complete each one.
The gameplay has its strong and weak points. The game is basically linear with a limited area to explore and direct route that needs to be taken to reach the objective marker/checkpoint. Combat involves shining your flashlight on enemies until they become vulnerable to your bullets (you will know it when it happens). Furthermore, you have limited ammo and can only carry a couple of weapons. Enemies can come from anywhere that is darks, so you need to be aware of your surroundings. This helps to create a tense atmosphere as you juggle between managing ammo and using your flashlight. You generally won't have enough ammo to spare (especially when your surrounded) so you will be forced to run away to the next checkpoint. A negative point to this is when you're facing the flying objects (things possessed by shadows flying at you) which take alot of light to kill, difficult to dodge and inflict massive damage.
The graphics are good and definitely help set the atmosphere. The dark lighting helps to enforce gameplay and set a creepy experience for the player as you are forced to move carefully, flashing your light around you to look for enemies. The setting is  basically the woodlands of America which looks gorgeouse at times and really draws you into the world.
The sound is excellent. The soundtrack definitely fits with creating a spooky atmosphere for the player and is great at setting the mood. The voice acting is good as well, which helps make the characters interesting and relatable. Furthermore, you get the soundtrack for this game for free via the DLC which includes tracks from the band 'Poets of the Fall' (who sound great btw).
The DLC, 'The Writer' and 'The Signal' are also included in the game. Althoug both DLC do continue the story after the ending of the base game, they don't add much to it. Furthermore, some of the level designs and encounters aren't too well thought out.
I recommend this game to people who love horror/thriller games.

I'll List pros, cons and neutrals and give my conclusions at the end of the review. Maybe its just luck but I haven't experienced a single CTD and only very few fps drops (After the fps patch they seem to become more common, but still manageable) and one small freeze.
I'll update the review at each new patch or fix released.
Pros:
+ Catching story and interesting historical setting
+ Good voice acting and facial animations.
+ Great atmosphere and city. Makes you feel inside the game and the historical context
+ AMAZING soundtrack. 60's rock, blues, jazz and country all the way fitting perfectly with the overrall setting.
+ Interesting characters, rich dialogues and the plot seems consistent so far even if sometimes its feels rushed.
+ Impressive lightining effects even though there still some bugs and some people that dislike it.
+ Cinematic narrative. It feels like you are watching a documentary about your character life and impact on New Bordeaux crime scene.
Neutrals:
. Driving Mechanic. I personally like it, as it seems like real driving but I guess a lot of people will not think like me.
. Somewhat strange animations. (Getting into or out of cover, Lincoln running with a gun and pedestrians animations are particularly weird.)
. A not-so-free world. Even though you can just hang around the city without any specific objective there isnt much to do outside the missions and collectables (It seems there will be patches to fix this, wich reinforces my final conclusion)
. Racket System gets repetitive too soon.
. Cluttered UI. I can go past it, but it's really annoying sometimes.
. Textures are not high-ended and polished as one could expect from a 2016 AAA game but it doesn't mean they are ugly!
Cons:
- Grainy and often foggy graphics. (The fps patch released on 10/08 adress this, it looks much better now but still an issue)
- Step back from Mafia I and II. Shops, bars, clubs are useless even though they are marked on the map, policemen dont care if you are driving 120mph, cargoes dont get damaged etc. These small bits of realism that made the Mafia series unique are absent.
- Very restricted field of view (remember GTA 3 and VC? That the map loading was so slow that you could go to someplace before it was even loaded?) (10/09 Update: Fps update adress this as well, it looks reasonable now)
- Notable graphic quality drop from cutscenes to actual gameplay.
- FPS lock (30 fps in 2016? Seriously?!) (Even if now there is a patch for that it still a HUGE flaw for a pc game coming out with a 30fps lock)
- Bizarre night and day cycle. There's no in-game clock (at least I haven't seem one) and day/night cycles looks totally random for me.
- Bizarre control scheme (Why not use GTA scheme?) (I play on a controller btw, things seem shitier for keyboard users)
- Very Dumb AI. Enemies and NPC's both.
- Overral feeling that you are a playing a BETA and not a finished game. Especially because the next patches will bring things that should already be in the game (as outfit changing, street races, interactive shops etc)
Conclusions:
1) Mafia III is a consistent game with a lot of potencial. Maybe even GOTY potencial, but this pc release is the worst since Arkham Knight (maybe even messier than that one). It seems to me the game was about 80% finished at release date but they released it all the way. Maybe with the coming patches and fixes Mafia III comes up and fulfill all its potencial. So far I can't reccommend this game to anyone and my veredict is that Hangar 13 and 2K just went lazy after the good pre-release sales. Actually I would give it a 6/10 but it has potencial to hit as high as 9/10 or higher.
2) This game doesn't seem to fit the Mafia franchise. Dont get me wrong, Mafia III is a potencially awesome game, but it just seems to me that it doesnt fit the franchise at all! The tiny little details that made Mafia an unique and awesome series are lost. Mafia III feels more like a mix of GTA general idea with Shadow of Mordor mechanics and the complex LA Noire history than one of the Mafia games. And the change of perspective (though I can understand it as Lincoln Clay is perfect for the setting proposed) still bites me.
3) DONT PRE-PURCHASE!!! Pre-purchasing ANYTHING is just plain dumb. You are giving away your money in exchange for the promise of a product and NOT for the product itself. This is destructive to any kind of industry as the quality tends to drop as the profitability of that product is already guaranteed before the product even exists. And in my humble opinion this is exactly what happened with Mafia III. A game that was released rushedly and unfinished, with no concern to customer satisfaction as a healthy profit was already safe and sound way before the release date.
I would reccomend this game for people who enjoy strategy-based games. It exceeded my expectations by far on how large-scale this game is. Definately worth the little amount they are asking for it.

I wanted to love this game, sooooo much. I don't, but I like it. It's good, it's definitely worth playing, but this comes with some serious reservations.
First, the good: the range of options is nothing short of amazing. The return to the old model of some voice to augment mostly written dialogue clearly gave them huge amount of freedom, and I love the way the decisions *feel* like actual decisions, and not just "Good guy / Bad guy" inane dichotomy decisions. No decision ever feels like the ideal one, and that's both difficult to execute and brilliant when done properly. The writing, by and large, is top notch.
The bad: It's very easy to create characters who end up as basically trash, and you almost have to play through once to know what you're going to need. Both your skills and attributes are locked once you select them. Skills you can make up for if you learn quickly, but you attribute allocation is pretty much locked once you create a character. Specializing in skills is hugely important if you don't want to save scum your way through all of the unlockables, but without knowing what NPCs are going to become available you can end up with very annoying redundancies. Given that a significant number of the skills are basically "unlock X," it starts to feel sort of silly.
The worst part, unfortunately, is the combat. It feels old, and not in a good way. For any fight that isn't a faceroll, you'll want to position your team before engaging and get it the first shot, guaranteeing your team at least some of the initiatve. Problem is, doing this is clunky to say the least. On top of that, cover (fairly necessary to keep fights from just being a straight up numbers game) is sparse and spread far apart most of the time...far enough that it's generally impossible to have more than a couple of your team in decent position. This problem is exacerbated by the weapon group disparity--ARs and sniper rifles (and occasionally energy weapons) completely outclass other weapon groups, a gap that only gets wider as the game goes on (although I will admit that my hand-to-hand bruiser does well, circumstantially). Maybe this is because I'm playing on hard, but enemies seem to have double or triple the action points of characters, allowing them to run obscene distances in a single turn or fire twice as much as characters.
The game relies heavily on combat, and for the style if play it's going for I felt like it was Jagged Alliace II lite. It uses almost all of the same systems JA2 does, but with less depth, or like X-Com, but with worse map design (for combat purposes--they're beautiful).
To clarify, this isn't a complaint that it's too hard--I *like* hard--it's that it's boring. There simply aren't a lot of options in the course of fighting and some skill and weapon choices, it becomes clear as you progress, are simply superior.
Short version: Everything about this game feels brilliant--writing, world, the player choices--but the simple / punishing combat model enourages simplicity and min/maxing in a way that takes away from the rest of the game.
So, worth buying and playing, but (and this is the first time I think I've ever said this) play it on easy or normal. Because the fighting is bland and making it harder just makes it take longer to get to the parts of the game worth playing.

If you like fallout, fallout 2, or fallout tactics, you'll enjoy this game.  Set in a post apocalyptic world with limited resources, there is an emphasis on creating a diverse, yet focused, skill set among your initial team members, as well as recruiting needed skill sets from among the npc's you encounter along the way.  There's a surprising, and welcome, amount of choice and consequence, and often those consequences aren't felt until later in the game.  There are so many ways to play through the game, and so many different choices, it is easy to see that this game can easily be played through multiple times with different experiences.
Graphically, the unity engine delivers the needed aesthetics.  While the ui is solid, it sometimes does not quite flow the way you'd expect, but once you figure it out, you should be fine.  I would point out, however, that if you are a mouse clicker, and not one to use keyboard shortcuts, this game will definitely wear out your hands.  If you are an older gamer  (like I am), this could be a problem....I've learned to use my keyboard shortcuts.
The story is solidly written, and you can tell the developers and designers had fun putting this all together.  There are more than a few moments in the game that gave me a good laugh, and caused me to shake my head.  Some of the references in even the type of loot you can pick up made me laugh (I'm thinking of you, "bat♥♥♥♥♥♥quot;, lol)
The combat is a whole bunch of turn-based goodness.  Though not quite as varied as, say, Divinity: Original Sin, it makes intelligent use of the cover concept, and emphasizes tactics over "jumping in".  This portion of the game reminded me a lot of Fallout: Tactics (with turn-based: individual turned on), in this regard.  You also had to watch your ammo expenditure, and constantly evaluate whether or not the enemies you faced was worth the ammo, since ammo is a rare commodity - espeically for sniper rifles!  This is where your 'brawlers' become important.  Also, let's not forget weapon smithing.  This was a layer on combat that added a little extra spice, and I personally didnt' realize to what extent I could use this skill.  Weapon smithing definitely defines the concept of "success is when perparation meets opportunity." A sniper that doesn't jam and has longer range? Yes please.  A bladed weapon that is easier to swing, letting you swing it more often? No question.  These little differences have often been the difference of a battle in which i use way too many trauma kits (lol), and a solid win with using a some pain killers along the way.
Though the game was fun, like every game, it had its flaws.  My main issue with the game is that, while I enjoyed the 'old-school gamer' vibe, it should have brought a few more modern gameplay elements in.  For example, if you have a character in your party that has safecracking skill, and there's a safe, don't make me select that character, then activate their safecracking skill, and then click on the safe.  Instead, I would expect a little more intelligence from my game. When I hover over the safe (assuming its not trapped), my icon should change to the safecracking icon, and then the character in my party with the highest safecracking skill should automatically make the attempt.  Fewer clicks, and the immersion isn't necessarily broken because I already know who my 'safecracker' is!
In summary, this is a fun game full of choice, consequence, and quirky humor.  The turn based combat is pretty solid, with a respectable variety of enemies which you have to face.  "Old-school" gamers will like this game, and even some younger gamers who want to see what all us old farts miss from the days of yore.  Give it a shot, you might be surprised!

Edited 3/29/2016: Do not mistake the fact that I haven't logged in in a while as a negative sign. I feel like there's at least 10+ more hours to be had from it. I only stopped because the third biome became quite difficult in contrast to the previous two for me personally. This game is terrific and worthy of your hard earned money (and then some - I could easily see it doubling in price and still being worth it).
PROS:
+ Keybinds (they're a godsend and quality of life upgrade)
+ Ability to take in the rich graphical beauty in full view.
+ Infinite inventory
+ Instant teleportation across the map to allocated teleport pads you discover as you explore.
+ Humor (this can be a con or pro depending on the person)
+ An in-depth crafting system with plenty to collect for hoarders and plenty of options for all types of players.
+ Cloud sync so you can load your save file on any device if you have it on each and continue where you left off.
CONS:
- Can get tedious and repetitive if you're trying to min max your stats by rerolling gear repeatedly.
- Movement speed feels slow sometimes and finding that attribute on gear that is also good gear is going to be pretty tough.
- Not very forgiving for mistakes in dodging enemy attacks (however, you can absolutely play on a lesser difficulty setting when you create the game)
- Cannot change difficulty of your game on the fly.
Counting the hours I've spent playing on IOS, I'm probably close to 10+ hours in and I've barely scratched the surface of the game, it feels like. I was a little unsure about whether or not I'd like the PC version, but now I can honestly say it is, without a doubt, the BEST version of the game. Moreover, the price justification needed to be there, and it is.
One of the only flaws I found with the game was on mobile platforms - tapping to move kept my finger in the way of what's going on, making avoiding attacks from enemy creatures more of a pain than it needed to be. At least for me. But that completely goes away here.
The graphics are wonderful and the way this game has improved upon the concept of Don't Starve is incredible. Absolutely everything was done right. Infinite inventory, the crafting system, pets that you can evolve (with a clever little homage screen to pokemon for their evolution), exploration, teleportation, the list goes on and on. Gone are the days of hiking back to your base by foot, or worrying whether or not you have enough inventory space left or whether you should pick up X item. Gone are the days of hunger and medical stats dragging you down (at least so far in my excursions).
The price tag is a lot more than on mobile platforms, but the game is absolutely 100% the same. So if you're strapped for cash and okay living without keybinds to open your inventory/quest log/build menu/etc, it's worthy of your time on any platform. But for those just interested in the PC version, who may be on the fence, do yourself a favor and buy it. If you liked Don't Starve, you'll LOVE this just as much, if not more, depending on the person. I myself can easily see many many more hours of this one in my future. You get your money's worth, that's for sure.

-The difficulty is not too tough like other point and click games so it is not a frustrating game.

Con:
-Shay's story was horribly boring to me. While I did like the idea and some of the characters in it, I had to really push myself to play through it. I didn't really care too much about Shay, I just wanted to play as Vella.

The reason the score isn't higher is due to Shay's portion of the game being so boring when compared to the excitement in Vella's half of the game. All in all, this is a fairly solid point and click game that fans of the genre should experience!

Very obviously endgame content that has no susbstantial story implications but is purely there for gameplay. As I mention below, people who are complaining about "grindy" gameplay in Act IV are unaware that at this point you are already done with the game. All you get for completing Act IV is
. It's just like every other long-term grind achievement hidden in almost every game for fun...
REVIEW AS OF FINISHING THE MAIN STORY:
If you like Shadow of Mordor, you'll like Shadow of War. More of the same with lots of improvements. Talion, the player character, has more abilities with interesting upgrades that allow for more costumization of your playstyle. There are more maps and while they are smaller than each of the previous ones (though larger in total), they are less stale and more varied. The inclusion of fortresses and siege battles encourages more interaction with the Nemesis system, so your attack forces/garrisons are on top of their game. Orcs are more varied with distinct races/tribes/classes, have more unique attacks and traits (also the menu to discern this info is much better). The story is a step up from Shadow of Mordor with the final events being particularly surprising (to me at least), going so far as to have major gameplay consequences.
I actually have few gripes with the game as it stands. Talion looks less mature and more like a 08/15 superhero from generic comic universe number 674. Performance differs between the maps because of detail denstity (although granted, the game features dynamic resolution). Talion, like in the first game sometimes comes across as quite naive but I guess this is on purpose, him being a fairly held back no-nonsense hero looking to save his kind once and for all. Some Orcs come across as way to intelligent, some actually lecturing you on how to interact with certain gameplay elements (literal tutrials). I would have preferred having a something like a rogue Gondorian guerilla helping out here or even Celebrimbor.
Adressing some concerns of other reviewers/players:
A lot of people complain about the grind after you finish the main story. I don't know how one can overlook the obvious shortcomings of the limited use of the Nemesis system in Shadow of Mordor and not conclude that the "grind" after the main story has been included to prolong playtime and engage the player in the Nemesis system for longer. In Shadow of Mordor the challenge modes were a really shallow band-aid for the same problem. This is much better in my opinion. Now obviously, the extremely shoe-horned lootboxes are despicable in principle, but I'd ask why you'd even use them when you enjoy the Nemesis system enough to play after the story. It's literally paying to play less of the game. Also you'll never get that level 65 maniac destroying your♥♥♥♥♥from a lootbox when you are barely level 40-something.
Reused assets, especially Talion's combat animations are no surprise. They are very good. Why would you change that? And more have been on top. Especially Orc vs Orc animations are plentyful now (also consider Ologs, which have to have their own animations against every enemy type).

Really good game, I didn't care much for the ending.
The ability to redo choices after you ♥♥♥♥ed up is a really good mechanic, especially since most people (like me) would just save scum and do that anyway so this is just cutting out the middle man. That being said, I often felt like too many dialogue choices weren't clear from the snippet of text provided, a problem I see often in games where you can select dialogue. Still, a really great teen drama that has time travel involved, but I feel like while the mind♥♥♥♥ near the end was executed great, the final choice felt dumb. It reminds me very much of Mass Effect 3, where the game acts like all of your choices matter, only to go "surprise, pick an ending lol". At least in this case the endings are different, but there is no happy ending; both are downers, it just depends on which one will make you less depressed. And I dunno, while the game did deal with some real♥♥♥♥♥♥(especially suicide), I felt like your choices should've allowed a happy ending, or at least a happier ending. It's like, I do everything right, make everyone happy, and nope, things are ♥♥♥♥ed up no matter what. And yes I get that the game calls you out that you're just making everyone happy to make them like you, which...in a sense is true; usually in games if we pick the "better" option to make someone happier, it's so that they'll help us out in the future. It's just the way we expect games to play out. So while I guess it was smart to call that out, it did suck that the ending was going to be a downer no matter what you did throughout the game.
While I wish the time travel powers were explained, the game wasn't really about that; it was about the life of this girl and the people around her. Until, you know, the ending. But spoilers.
I still definitely recommend it for fans of story-based games, just don't be surprised if the ending pulls the rug from under your feet.

Kerbal Space Program is a game developed and published by Squad. Words alone cannot express how amazing Kerbal Space Program is!

Optionally, if you just like building rediculously large rockets and watching them explode with glorious comedy when they fail catastrophically because you forgot something, then this is also definitely for you!
Kerbal Space Program is challenging, fun, frustrating, mind boggling, huge, hilarious, complicated, deep, and just plain awesome and is one of the successful games that has come out of Steam Early Access and I wish the developers the best of luck for future expansions and projects to come!
