The John Wick Weapon pack could have been so much better, like the Sydeny Character pack it has good looks, but in the end it's just lacking so much compared to other weapon packs.
Also if you like playing with armour or just being a tank in general, skip this DLC, it offers nothing to you, this pack is aimed at Dodge Crit players.
The Contractor Pistol is the best weapon out of the pack and best looking, it has great damage, quite a bit of ammo, a great mag size and is very concealable, on it's own it is a great weapon, and with help with some mods, it will be a helpful sidearm for loud and stealth.
The Contractor is the first DLC pistol to have Akimbo versions! AND THEY SUCK! In nearly everyway, their stats are just crappier versions of the Crosskill Akimbos and their ammo pool is way too low to even have a fighting chance against the Bernetti 9 and Chimano 88, avoid this Akimbo Weapon at all costs.
The Sniper Rifle is pretty much an R93 with 1 less shot and is a lot more concealable, so if you used an R93 or use it often, you will feel right at home with this gun, and thanks to it's low concealment, it's a great dodge and crit option, overall it's a good weapon.
The Jackal SMG has simlar stats to the Krinkov and the CR 805B from the Biker Heists, and is pretty much your average High Damage low ammo SMG... until you build it for pure damage and mag size and realise it's a downgrade in everyway from a CR 805B when you build it in the same way. However the saving grace with for this weapon is that it's quite concealable and can be a good option for Crit and Dodge users, but for me, I'll stick with the Micro UZI and Vector.
Throwing Knfies... don't use them, they are a direct downgrade from the Throwing Axes from the Biker Heists.
"Why?" I hear you ask, well...
While you have 6 Knifes, they have a second delay on them until they are thrown, meaning if a guard spots you in Shadow Raid, by the time you draw a knife out to kill him, he's already shot the air, while the Throwing Axes have in instant throwing animation, and chances are due to it's high damage, kills the guard in one hit... so yea, give these sh**ty knifes the middle finger and throw them into the bin, they are total garbage.
While the Knfies do share the same damage as the Axes, that small delay prevents it from being useful for me.
*UPDATE* They changed it so they no longer have a delay when thrown, and while yes they are now a true upgrade to the Axes, I still find the Axes more fun since... well throwing Axes at enemies is much more satisfying then throwing a dinky knife at them.
The achievements are... odd... while I do often complain about some achievements being p*ss easy or too boring, my main issue is how oddly tied 2 achievements are... I mean why do I have to use a pistol only, in Firestarter, on Overkill to get a mask? Why not just "Kill X amount of cops with the pistol" or "Finish 15 heists while having the Contractor equipped"?
I also don't like the Knife achievement, not only it forces me to use them, but why in Murky Station? Why? Why not in just any stealth heist?
What do these 2 heists have to do with Wick? I mean with all the other Promo/Crossover DLC all their achievements made sence, why does this get Achievements that don't even fit the character or movie?
However killing 45 Russians with the Jackel does make sence since in the movie

But all of the achievements are alright, they won't be unlocked in one game and they will take some time to get done, so I'm happy with that at least.
The masks could have been better, Daisy is the best mask, while the others are meh, the patterns and materials are also decent.
Overall this Weapon pack is mediocre, the Biker Heists DLC does the exact same job as half of this DLC but better, while the other 2 weapons are the only ones worth picking up.
Get it on sale, it's lacking too much to be worth £3.99/$4.99, go grab another pack instead.

First of all: If you're like me, you will *not* like that game. I still recommend that game, because I see the potential for players who like this kind of game.
I'm scared of trying things without knowing the consequences, even in a game. I'm the kind of RPG player, that googles the possible outcomes of choosing one or another dialogue option, and then decides for the best possible outcome. This doesn't work in Kerbal Space Program. You need to experiment, try things, learn by failing, I don't like that at all.
So much to the reason why I will not continue playing it.
Now to the reasons why I recomment it anyway.
While building rocket ships by myself was scary, I really liked the tutorial missions. The Kerbals explaining stuff, letting you build the perfect rocket for the mission at hand, telling you how to steer it, after lift off, that was fun for me. I like the controls of building the rockets, I like the options one has to set it up so that it *wouldn't* crash into the planet, and somehow I still killed a Kerbal when I landed in a mountain range instead of sea level.
There are many parts to choose from, when building a rocket, very different parts also. All of them have their own properties, heavier but more fuel, smaller but more expensive, it's always a conflict of interests when building a new rocket. What should this rocket be able to do, and what is unnessecary stuff, that can be removed. At first there is no perfect rocket for any mission you get, there is very specialized rockets for each and every (type) of mission, and finding the right parts to build that rocket in a way that you accomplish the goals can be tedious but also fun.
So in the end I can't tell you anything about mid game or end game, just the beginning, which isn't something for me, but has potential for sandbox lovers!

WIP Review:
More guns! I love guns!
To be honest, this is mostly a sidegrade weapon DLC. And the issue is, OVK can't possibly appeal to everyone at once. You have people who cry "PAY TO WIN" if the gun beats the meta, and "reskin" if it doesn't. The thing here to remember though, is that this "reskin" is terrific, because of the UMP-45. And because the game gets more guns.
Each gun has a load of customization options. I haven't gotten to all of them yet, but I did mess around with the Jackal (UMP)
Yeah, the dang thing is huge. It also comes with all the mods unlocked and with the ability to throw on an intergrated flashlight, something I haven't seen with any other gun in the game.
The sniper has its own mods, but they're a little more... Condensed. A silenced barrel and a long barrel, as well as a short, are it's only offerings. But you can't really do much with a Sniper, to be honest.
I haven't gotten around to the pistol, but I do look forward to tinkering with it.
TL;DR: More guns with more customization means that we can find new ways to beat the enemy back. And I personally love that.
EDIT: After playing with the SMG and Sniper on OVK, I have come to the consensus that:
The sniper, while powerful, lacks the magazine capacity to be able to be used in prolonged engagements
The SMG is awesome.
EDIT 2: Contractor pistol has become my favorite pistol. The looks, the animations (aside from sprinting) the preformance... It's fire rate is a little low, but overall, it's one of my favorite pistols, and will probably be my go to from now on.

Game is decent but seems like it was rushed.  There are a lot of inconsistencies and annoying things left out that would have made the game much better.
The NPC pictures look weird and different than the game's text descriptions.  You will read about how ancient looking an NPC looks and the picture will be of a person in their mid-to-late 30's.  Stuff like that isn't too serious but it does break immersion a little.
The camera controls are annoying.  You will constantly miss things and have to re-search areas because the camera angle was wrong and a wall or something was obstructing your view.  I am not even talking about small things either... you could miss a giant door or anything because of this.  You can press the Z button to see outlines of interact able things but if you want to make sure you find everything you pretty much would have to hold it down the entire time which is unacceptable.  Small rooms are almost uninteractable because of this.   I don't understand why the developers didn't make it that walls go transparent when you get near them (like most other games like this one).  It seems like it would be a simple thing to do that would make the gameplay so much better.  Perhaps a future update will address this?
One of my characters has had a concussion effect for pretty much the entire game.  It tells me to go see a doctor but there are none to be found anywhere (or I keep missing them due to the way the overview camera works as explained earlier.)  Therefore she is suffering from lost attribute points and I seemingly cant do anything about it.  Annoying.
Your characters don't automatically level up.  You have to go through an unnecessarily lengthy radio call-in dialog every time someone has enough experience to level up.  Because your characters level up individually and at different times expect to do this frequently, almost after every battle encounter.  While we are on the topic of leveling up the character skill and inventory screens are very clunky and unintuitive.  An example of this is when you find a new weapon and want to compare it with a character's current weapon.  Since you have a primary and secondary equip slot you can only compare it to the currently equipped weapon.  To compare it to the weapon in the other slot you have to exit the inventory screen, switch to the other weapon slot, and re-enter the inventory screen.  Like most things I have pointed out this is more annoying than really game-breaking.
Ammo is pretty scarce IMHO.  You will go up against enemies that shower you with bullets but somehow only drop a few when they die.  Buying bullets is expensive as well.  Just a warning.
The worst problem with this game I have encountered so far is how enemies seem to have unlimited action points allowing them to move around at will every turn.  I had one enemy make it from a field, up a ladder, and right next to my sniper sitting on a building in a single turn which doesn't seem right at all.  It is really irritating to setup a nice ambush plan only to have your troops overwhelmed by melee enemies that make it 20-30 spaces in a single turn right next to your well-positioned team members.  It really spoils the whole battle mode IMHO.
I was going to give this game a thumbs-up overall but after actually typing out all this stuff I have changed my mind.  The decent story is overshadowed by a horde of minor annoyances and I have to give it a thumbs down until they address this stuff.

Nuclear Throne is one of the best games of its type; it has variety when it comes to characters, weapons, outcomes, and more, and it is difficult to the point of being awesome at some points, and with loads of replayability.
With characters, you can select ones with speed, with health, with blocking, and with other abilities depending on what you enjoy. You unlock characters as you play, so you have a reason to continue moving forward (aside from the 'just because i like to shoot.')
You have different weapon classes, with everything from arrows to shotguns to explosives represented, and you haveenough bullets to keep things interesting but also enough to progress without a terrible amount of conservation. I like that about a game like this; with a bit of aiming and a bit of luck, you can manage pretty well, and with a few character upgrades, you can do even better.
Speaking of which; through the collection of 'rads' via kills or random placement, you level up and gain abilities. At first this happens around every one or two boards, but later the pickings get a little more difficult due to the enemy type and your distancing. You can get things that allow more health, more bullets, kills giving health or bullets, and on and on. That makes it interesting, too, because it adds even more variety.
I have clocked about 30 hours of game time that Steam has counted and at least 30 more offline, and I have to say that the game keeps me coming back.

Okay, out of pure boredom, I decided to write a full review about every specific thing in the game.
If you just came here to know everything about the game before you buy it, I would highly recommend you to buy it, but I think I should head over to the cons before anything.
If you can relate to these things being bad, or unenjoyable, then you may need to reconsider buying this game.
- 8-bit (or 16-bit, whatever, OR 24-BIT, WHATEVER) graphics. If you dislike those kind of graphics, remember that the whole game is pixelated.
- Very difficult. If you’re a person who is overall bad at games, or like specific game styles, remember that everything in the game is very, very, VERY difficult, unforgiving, and did I mentioned that it’s difficult? You will die all the time and I mean it.
- Very fast-pasted. If you’re a casual gamer who enjoys gameplay that involves no stress at all, you should definitely reconsider buying this game.
- No multiplayer.
If none of the things I just mentioned don’t bother you, I would REALLY recommend you to play this game.
Okay, now when that is out of the way, let’s talk about specific aspects.
1. Gameplay
It has a top-down perspective. (Look at the screenshots if you don’t understand.) Where you kill people with melees and guns. You can throw them, too, which is unique compared to most games that feature guns. Throwing the guns at a person resorts in knocking them down, and you execute them by pressing the space bar. If you have no melee equipped, you will need to left-click a few times before you kill the enemy. But if you wait a short while, the enemy will get up, equip the nearest weapon he can see, and will try to attack you again. There are enemies that require weapons, such as dogs, fat guys, and dodgers.
Also, a very significant thing about the gameplay is that you get to choose a mask with different abilities. Want dogs not to attack you? Choose Ted. Want to make the enemies not hear the gunshots, and just kill them one-by-one? Choose Peter. Want to kill enemies just by throwing the guns? Choose Jake. You get the point.
2. Visuals
They’re 24-bit, but they’re very detailed for a pixelated game (especially the faces that appear whilst dialogue). And if you’re a fan of gore in videogames, then you will definitely enjoy this game, considering that this is one of the goriest games that I’ve ever played. Okay, I’m not too much of a gamer, but my point is that the game is gory, especially in the second game.
3. Story
Sorry, I can’t summarise the story chronologically in a few sentences, but it’s interesting, dark, mysterious, and confusing. Google search it if you want to. It won’t spoil anything, it’s hard to put the puzzle pieces together when playing the game. The first game has barely any story comparing to the sequel, and it constantly takes different roles and time periods.
4. Music
If you would ask anyone who has played Hotline Miami what stands out about this game, one of the first answers would be the music. It really gives you the atmosphere that the game takes place. In my opinion, Hotline Miami 2’s soundtrack is much better, but a lot of the songs used in the first game are very iconic and popular.

I'm comfortable with the hours I've put in, and that they returned the value of the product as purchased..
I do, however, have some
issues with the game.
This game is great fun during the first few levels, the difficulty feels fine, the weapons and character progression powers you acquire add both excellent depth, and good variety. The starting (and early-unlock) heroes are all interesting, and have enough variance in play to justify their existence. It's really a good experience all around.
After that, however, you begin to see the flaws. There's a whole progression system that only happens _after you've thoroughly beaten the game_. Nearly half of the heroes you can acquire are locked behind a run progressing beyond x stage. This is content that
will never see.
. There's a whole world of unlocking starter weapons that most players will never see.
The difficulty ramp is also quite large. The ice levels are filled with high-health enemies that move very quickly and do lots of damage. The boss for that stage isn't terribly difficult to kill, but surviving afterwords is something I've yet to accomplish. And that brings me to my second point:
The main flaw I have with this game is that the difficulty is unearned. There are either no invulnerability frames after being damaged, or the timing of them is so miniscule that it may as well not exist. This makes most deaths feel very unsatisfying. Some big, fast moving enemy does a charge attack in an unfriendly and open procedurally generated map, and it might kill you before you can react because it damages you multiple times very quickly. Cars can explode on the end-map portal opening and kill you. There are melee enemies that move very quickly, and strike for huge damage in a very large area. The maps can be way too open, giving you no time to dodge the myriad of threats around you. The norm is to feel cheated when you die.
The fact that the game is so punishing may not be all bad. It can force you to
but even outrageously punishing games like the souls series have permenant character progression, and enemies that are fair, when approached skillfully. I can get top 100 on dailies easily, but I have yet to get past the ice levels. Half of the characters are locked, and most of the post-game content is, and will be, forever locked. There's whole swaths of interesting weapons I'll never get to experience because they're only for people in the late-game levels. It's a bit sad really. Content designed for people skillfull and lucky enough to get that far that nobody who is unlucky will get to see.
Look, it's fun enough, but the brutal and generally luck-based difficulty really turns me off because of the things I'm missing out on. Maybe a game mode where all weapons are available at any point would make me happy. Maybe just a quarter second of invulnerability when damaged would make the game beatable to more than the select few. Maybe they don't want that. But maybe that's what holding the game back from being really excellent. I don't know, but that's my 2c.

For the full review, I'm going to break things down by mechanics and features. New players will also be able to learn some useful tips about the game, by reading this.
So, let's start with:
For starters, this game is pretty funny. It doesn't take itself seriously, and has jokes and humour littered througout. The thing is, it's all quite well done, and creates an enjoyable world to explore and discover. The characters you'll meet are often silly and entertaining, but not in any way that breaks immersion. Overall, it's very well done, and by doing the storyline quests and side quests, you unlock more recipes and ingredients to use to make your character even stronger.
The crafting system in the game is very well done. There are different crafting stations for different tiers of equipment and tools. There are a lot of similarities between this system and Starbound, however this one ups that by offering ideas that make it easier to craft. One of my favourite features of crafting is the ability to track a recipe. Click "Track" then you'll see what ingredients you'll need to craft that item. As you collect the ingredients, you'll see how much you have, and how much you still need, in order to make that item.
Recipes are another fun aspect of the game as you start with a bunch when you make a new station. You can also get new recipes from finishing quests. My favourite feature, however, is that you can get epic and legendary recipes from resource drops, mob drops, and fishing. It's very rewarding to kill an enemy and suddenly see a recipe box pop out. It could be anything from a new piece of furnature for your house to a legendary blueprint for a piece of equipment.
Crafting is this games' killer app, and it really is killer.
Exploration in Crashlands is very similar to Don't Starve. You start at your pod, and as you travel further out, your map gets filled in, block by block.
The further away you get, the more interesting (read:dreadly) the enemies become. Then again, the greater the risk, the greater the reward. There are lots of interesting places to discover, and NPC locations are littered everywhere, which results in gaining new quests, learning more about the planet you've crashed on, and of course, more recipes and lot.
It also helps that the art style in Crashlands is wonderfully colourful, with lots of glowy things that light up the world in a myriad of colours. Exploration is FUN FUN FUN in Crashlands.
At a certain point in the game, you're going to gain access to a hearth for cooking, and later, a fishing rod for fishing.
Unlike a lot of games that have fishing spots randomly appear in different places, fishing spots are permanent in Crashlands. That means you can place signs (assuming you've crafted some) at any spots you find, and come back to them every two hours. At one point, I was using signs to label sites on the map, but eventually the game one upped that by giving me a recipe for an item that creates fishing spots in any body of water I choose.
Let me remind you, fishing spots are pemanent, so these items were a Godsend, as fishing is not only very rewarding, it's also very enjoyable. Add to that the fact that you can also gain legendary items and recipes from fishing, and you have a system that will keep you coming back for more.
Fishing spot cooldowns will continue to count down, even when you're not playing the game, so long as you haven't left the game paused. Pausing the game and leaving it, unfortunately, also pauses timers. Bummer for sure, but this can be avoided by simply exiting the game when you walk away from it. The game saves everything automatically, so you won't lose anything by doing so.
As for cooking, when you use the hearth, you'll have a bunch of recipes for potions. Potions provide health, speed, resistences, etc. There are all sorts of boosts and benefits from potions, so you'll want to pursue that, when the hearth comes available.
Quick tip: There's a quest, not long after you get the hearth, that'll allow you to make really good health potions out of fish and stone. If you have a rod and a hearth, but not this recipe? Do some quests, it's worth it... so worth it.
Building is another great feature in this game. It's extremely simple to get some building supplies, then activate build mode which will allow you to click (or tap) anywhere on the screen to place that item.
Additionally, each building type is seperated into function. Floors have their own section, so it's easy to select that item set, choose a floor type, and just start pasting those floor tiles down the way you want.
Vegetation (farming... yes, this game TOTALLY has farming) is another section, and you can plant your seeds, and place potted plants which can both be harvested after a 15 minute cooldown.
Again, cooldowns will continue to count down while you're out of the game, so be sure to check back on your farms, from time to time.
Here is perhaps one of my favourite features of Crashlands, you can have pets! Pets serve two features. First, you can feed your pets to harvest resources from them. These resources can be used in certain recipes, and often come in really handy.
The second function, and perhaps the most important, you can take one of your pets out with you while you explore. They'll fight for you, while they keep you company. Additionally, they're invincible, so you don't need to worry about them getting killed by other baddies. They also don't need to be fed to stay aline, feeding is only something you do when you want to... milk them...
How about one more awesome point of keeping animals... Well, you can also unlock recipes for items that will cause your animals to permanently evolve into larger and more powerful versions. Each animal has multiple stages of growth, each one making them bigger, stronger, and look cooler, each time.
You should get an egg drop for each enemy type, shortly after you've crafted a station that can make that animal's nest.
Keeping animals is absolutely worth it, in this game.
There's loot... lots and lots of loot. When you kill creatures, fish, harvest resources, etc, you'll get showerd with items and materials. The key point here is that there is not traditional inventory with a sprawling list of things you have and don't have. The inventory system manages all of that for you, and there is NO LIMIT TO INVENTORY SPACE. As you pick things up, they will scroll by discreetly on the left, along with a number in brackets which indicates how many you have in total.
The inventory system in Crashlands is another one of those features that makes you wonder why it has taken so long for a developer to think of it. It's clean, efficient, simple to figure out, and cuts out all the mess of traditional inventory spaces.
As mentioned before, all enemies, resource points, and fishing have a chance of dropping some epic items, so there will be a lot of "OMG That's AWESOME" moments in your adventures with Crashlands.
Seems I'm at the word limit for this review, so let me just sum it up by saying, Crashlands is one hell of a good game. It aces its presentation, mechanics, sense of rewarding, and enjoyment. If you haven't purchased it yet, do yourself a favour and get in on the fun.

Shadow of War is another solid Middle-earth game, if you enjoyed Shadow of Mordor you will definitely enjoy this!
The story probably won't win any awards but it was good enough to keep me playing, however the combat is where the game is strongest. The Orc captains and warchiefs feel like more of a challenge compared to the first game, sometimes even adapting mid-fight to your stratigies. For example, if you keep vaulting over a captain to back-stab him, he will realise what you're doing and start to block your vault.
The betrayals and surprises from captains also keeps you on your toes, just as it looked like a battle was won, a captain would turn on me because I recently killed his blood-brother! Or when I've been knocked down and the enemy is about to deliver the killing blow, a friendly captain will jump in to save me at the last second.
The end portion of the game is where things take a weird turn however...It took me around 33 hours to complete the entire game (I left some of the collectables), the last 6-7 hours were very grindy BUT I didn't spend a penny of my own money on loot boxes (loot boxes contain "epic" or "legendary" Orc captains to add to your army).
Without spoiling anything, you need to have high-level Orcs in your army, and they need to upgraded a lot to make sure they're good enough to do the job.
I did however buy the basic loot boxes with money you earn in game, I found I had more than enough left over each time to upgrade the next army, but without those loot boxes I honestly would have given up on getting the "true" ending of the game (which you get after completing Act 4).
Overall I really enjoyed the game, if you're a fan of LOTR (or even if you're not) or you like the Batman Arkham series style of combat, I would highly recommend getting the game!

Garry's Mod is impossible to completely explore in a few hours. Sure it's a "simple" sandbox game based off half-life, but there is soooo much more than assets ripped from half-life. The workshop has an unimaginable amount of different content. Ranging from different maps, to nearly different games. If you like shooters, there's that. If you like building games, there's that. If you like doing random stupid stuff, there's plenty of that. I can't say Garry's Mod replicates these things perfectly, but the ability to do all these things in one game, with infinite customizability, makes this game just fanominal. I truely think this game fills the empty wants inside of us. I personally was annoyed by the lack of control you had in most games. In Garry's Mod, you have the ability to manipulate things in a way no game has ever made possible. Maybe this game isn't as fun to some as it is to me, but I think anyone can find lots of fun in this. Besides, it's really cheap, and it goes on sale for cheaper.

An asymmetical multiplayer-only FPS/RTS hybrid. Aliens vs. Marines, with the agile melee-only aliens trying to outwit, out-ambush, and out-rush the pea-shooter-toting Marines. Util Marines get Exos and stomp the snot out of aliens. Or, until Aliens get Onos and (literally) stomp the Marines so they fall down to be gored at the leisure of the Onos.
The balance needs a lot of work, as it is not okay to hard counter one OP unit with another when the rest of the game is (supposedly) soft counter. The loading times are excessive, and the voice volume is tied to the SFX volume. But, these things aside, it's a decent game that pushes the envelope and innovates, mostly for the better. It is very team-work focused, and a headset is pretty much required (which sadly many people don't understand). Having a competent commander is a must to win the match, but good luck convincing anyone to get in the chair!
6/10 for now, will bump it up to an 7 if they fix the loading times and work on the balance. Would have liked to see a couple different Marine classes, personally...

Let me tell you a story about my son, Karee "The Legend" Kerman.
Karee was just finishing astronaut training when the first "Mun Men" made their launch.  They made a rough attempt at landing their craft on the Mun and end up crashing, leaving two poor souls, Bill and Bob, stranded.  Their pod skipped across the lunar landscape as they came to realize they would never see home again.  Little did they know their comrades had prepared another rocket with a brave soul, Valentina, to come rescue them with a similar craft.  She rocketed off, carrying the hopes and dreams of their nation.  Valentina was able to land successfully, but way too far from Bill and Bob's original landing site, so she decided she would hover across the Mun to link up.  Valentina successfully hovered to Bill and Bob's pod, but she had used too much fuel trying to get over.  She too was now stranded...
When all hope was lost and nobody else wanted to go on another rescue mission, Karee volunteered to go alone.  He launched just two weeks after Bob and Bill had made their launch and not two days into his own career.  He navigated his craft into orbit around the Mun and landed just a few kilometers from the other two landing sites.  Perfect execution.  Bill, Bob, and Valentina then made the "Mun walk" of a lifetime by thrusting themselves to Karee's rescue craft.  All three boarded safely.  That was the easy part.  The rest depended on Karee's ability to pilot them back home.  He took off, sent them speeding low and fast around the Mun, and slingshot them towards home.  Karee then piloted them into the atmosphere.
I was so proud of my son Karee.  Finally, they were coming home safe... I went with the rescue team personally, saying -
"Karee, on my wayward son"

Unintentional running-scared-in-the-woods simulator. Overrated for sure, but worth a play-through.
Contains classic horror-tropes and cliches, some not so cleverly disguised, but for the most part the bigger tropes (killer birds, poltergeists & ax-murderers) are played on a somewhat satirical note. The story told is nothing groundbreaking or one you haven't necessarily heard before - but to it's credit, up until the final cut scenes, you won't be able to outright call the ending.
This game suffers from poor progression. The first chapter successfully reels the player in with flashes of climactic events yet to come. Anticipation builds, curiosity is piqued and then -- waiting ... waiting ... yep. The story comes to a practical halt, stringing you along with useless tidbits of information which have no greater meaning or impact as far as the plot goes. Alan Wake's saving grace is in the last two chapters, which reward the player's admirable patience with fulfilling and detailed sequences of events. Unfortunately, the transitions between chapters are blatant and without grace, reeking of inexperience in storytelling.
To break it down; Episode 1 is consistent throughout, and moderate in it's rhythm - to effect - as all stories must set the scene and establish some background. Then come Episodes 2-4; whereas a good narrative will lay down the brass tacks and drop some hints with substance, Alan Wake's narrative is merely a distraction, desperate to keep the player's interest by use of one-liners and random musings which make no contribution to the overall story arc. Finally, Episodes 5 & 6 pick up where the intensity of Episode 1 dropped off, the player finds themselves running through the woods once again, but this time with a purpose and a need to tie up all loose ends.
All in all, not a complete waste of time. Still, too lengthy a game for it's own story-telling purposes. Play it if you like cheesy horror flicks and you have time to kill. 6/10
TL;DR: decent story, poor execution, combat & game-play solely for purposes of lengthening the play time.

I just want to say I've only written one other review on another game in my 200+ collection of games which was Deus Ex: Human Revolution and it won't be as long as this one.
To begin, this game is something I did not think I would enjoy, boy was I wrong!  This game opened my mind to the Isometric strategic RPG genre of games and OMG i love it!  I beat this game in over 70+ hours of playtime including probably about 100 + save/reloads.  My first playthrough I picked 4 of the actual characters that you can actually begin with.  I spent about 10 - 20 hours and stopped at
I wasn't sure of why I wasn't catching up in the sense of skills on the easiest difficulty, some things were too hard or impossible to open and I couldn't understand it.  So, I looked online for an idea of what to do in my situation.  I found that certain things were easier to do if you made 4 custom characters.  You could plan your skills the way you want them and imo, in all cases there was an order to the skills being used that made them have a priority.  Lockpicking IMO had to be the most important.  The only problem with this skill usage correction is that it may detract from the game.  I enjoyed the game even after this skill customization.  I had 4 members of my team, with portraits available to be put inside the game from an outside source.  I had 4 members of my team, Arnold Schwarzenegger (heavyweaps, sub), George Clooney (sniper(just got done watching From Dusk till Dawn for the first time)), Daniel Craig (Assault Rifle), and Bruce Willis (shotgun) with the appropriate allotment of skills put into each of my team members.  All in all in order to cut this short, I enjoyed the game with much appreciation of all the work that they put into it, the upgrading of weapons and the awesome story definitely is what kept me going in this game.  i'm trying to think of different things that could have done to improve the experience but nothing comes to mind.  Certain bugs do occur, that may come to mind but it didn't stop me from finishing the game.
I give this game a 10/10 mainly because it is an awesome game and it makes me want to come back and play on the hardest difficulty.  Good job devs!

This game is unbelievably hit and miss...
The story and presentation are stunningly well done, it's a little generic but the delivery is impeccable. The shooting feels great and the setting has the potential to be gourgeous, that's the key word here, potential.
Pretty much everything feels almost solid, almost great, but not quite there yet. The city is beautiful but dead and plagued with graphical errors, glitchy citizens, awkward animations, a 20ft draw distance, the jankest weather cycle I think i've ever seen and so much more. The swamp is once again, beautiful but ruined by a terrible draw distance and odd glitches. The gun play is great, the AI is stupid. The melee combat is impactful, the animations are awkward and clunky. The visual design is stellar, it's ruined by a low framerate. Nothing is perfect and the only area where it truly excels is in the presentation of its story (The small amount of it that i have seen atleast).
Now aside from the big FPS problem and all the issues listed above the game is playable, very jumpy and annoying, but playable. The issues which make the game nearly unplayble for me are the filter, blur effects and glitches. The game has a p*ss filter which cannot be turned off, the filter is to make the game more 'thematic' as though you're viewing it through an old camera. This does make it feel somewhat more thematic due to the documentary style of delivery but honestly it isn't worth it, I'd rather just enjoy the period as it was. The blur is beyond frustrating if anything is more than 10 meters away it becomes incredibly blurry, text is unreadable, NPC faces become gelatinous blobs and gun fights are like a god damn earthquake. It feels as though the developers are trying their hardest to hide their lower res textures with obnoxious visual effects masquarading as 'style', it's  just bad.
The glitches are a whole thing on their own, cars pop through the ground and glide through you until you die, NPC's fall over for no reason and fling through walls when ever so much as touched in a car, the police walk on water (not kidding), take downs don't connect and sometimes enemies will just stand still and shoot at nothing. It's ridiculous and the game even crashed to desktop twice during just two hours of play.
Potential is coursing through Mafia III's veins, but raging type 2 diabetes and concrete surfing soft tops make sure you never bloody see it.
I'm not giving a rating with just two hours of play, don't buy it until it's confirmed that these problems are fixed.

While the game is good and all, there is a fair warning to be said. If the first half of the game (Arizona) is more or less complete and bug free (at least from my side, there are still a lot of bug for some people), the second half (California) is full of bugs, from minor to gamebreaking. In its current states, the second half of the game is what you expect from an early access, not a release.
In this state I can't recommend this game, which is sad considering how good it is in the first half, but the second half of the game can't be considered as finished. And you can blame the devs for it, since we asked to be able to test it, and they refused, arguing their QA team was working on it and it would be perfect.
Basically, the more you go toward the end, the more bugs you'll find, and the more likely you will encounter a game stopping bug.
Anyway, here the pros and cons of the whole game.
Pros :
-Lots of story. Expect a lot of talking. This is a hit or miss. Expect more talking than action, unless you shoot everything on sight.
-Background. Fallout/Wasteland and their universe are a hit or miss. If you like mad max, you'll like it.
-Humour, but not ridiculous. While there are a lot of easter eggs and jokes, mostly about 80' stuff, they are well done, and they are all logical in the universe. There is no joke for the sake to make a joke, as you would be able to see in fallout 2 (the Star Trek shuttle, broken dreams inn,...).
-Replayability. There is a LOT of endings and choices to be made. Ranging from small to big. And not only for the main quest, but for every area.
-Graphics. While it's VERY ugly when close, I find the game quite pretty from afar, and the places are really well done. I honestly enjoy it a lot.
-The possibility to build your own 4 rangers party (you'll be able to recruit 3 more NPC into your party, with their own moral compass etc...). It's basically like Icewind dale, or NWN2 Storm of Zehir for party creation. As for the NPC you can recruit, do not expect Bioware's interaction, they will leave or stay according to your action, and have something to say at various place in the world. Some of them are even granted small cutscene and special interaction, and can help you dealing with something special, but it's extremely rare.
Cons :
-Currently unfinished. And by that, I mean some area are missing triggers, some NPC are not even named (being generic NPC), and even some area are not done (casino being outside of the building, and an excuse about unfinished work inside for example).
-Full of bugs. Including gamestopping bug that prevent you from completing the game. Or less annoying, to complete an area.
-Combat system. While I like it, I wish we had a lot more cover and environment to use. So far, having a single place to take cover in a fight is quite rare. Being able to take cover with your entire team is extremely rare.
-RNG badly done. The game is basically inciting to savescumming if you want to open chests and whatnot. Only to find 10bullets inside a chest with 60% chance to open with the maximum skill. Why isn't it a straight check instead of some useless RNG ?
-Some choices not impacting the rest of the game. Granted, only really happened in the second part of the game which is unfinished, but it's still annoying to kill several patrol of some faction, having them calling everyone on radio to say how evil you are, and still being greeted like a hero in their HQ.
-Lack of weapon balance. Heavy weapons are useless, just like shotguns. While Assault Rifle and SMG are usefull for the entire game. And energy weapons being the best weapon for the mid/late game.
-Lack of variety in weaponsmithing. While you can mod your guns, the mod only increase in the bonus effect, not in variety. For example, scope only provide better range, nothing else. More choices would have been cool. Also, the heavy weapons can't be modded, making them even less interesting.
-Lack of stats balance. Some stats are useless, like luck, giving a chance to earn a small benefit, while another stat will provide the same bonus, with some others,  and is guaranteed. Also, combat initiative is a lot more interesting than action point, forcing you into a build, more than anything else.
-Traduction unfinished for any other languages than English. It's not a problem to me (playing in English), but it can be for you, if you are playing in German or French for example.
Once I'm able to finish the game, and the various side quests which are currently broken, I'll edit this review.

I think I was waiting for the fps fix in order to actually review the game, either way, let's start.
I want to just say that is amazing this game doesn't have Denuvo, that frankly would've been, for me, the final nail in the coffin.
But luckily 2k, or hangar 13 studios, maybe both seem commited enough to release a patch that actually fixes the framerate, and while the game does need a lot of optimization still, I can say that I can play the game at a steady 60fps for the most part with a single gtx 970, and some settings turn down, post processing too, turn to off, completely, simply because I don't like it.
So you probrably heard how good the story is, and it's true, the story it's frankly the biggest appeal for this game, it's frankly been the main drawing part of the Mafia series, ever since this one started, that's not to say the gameplay portions were bad, but they just weren't the main focus, you could tell right from the start, both the first Mafia as well as it's sequel are incredible experiences, they carry class, and elegance in their design, massive attention to detail, and care, more than anything, they're games with a lot of heart, right from the start in this third entry to the franchise I didn't know what to think at first, on one hand I understood some things as a little bit cheesy, while clearly after noticing the graphical quality, as well as the terrible feel that the controls had, I felt suddenly swept away, as if by some sort of force the franchice I knew and loved, the game I had play since I was a kid, only to then play the second entry as a teenager, and now playing this as an adult, had been struck by a bolt of lighting.
It's an understatement to say the first few hours of the game were dissapointing for a lot of reasons, the main one being the fact that the first couple of missions are being treated as very inclosed tutorials, eventually while getting every simple mechanic that the game presents, I really couldn't have avoided the feel of this game being a bit of a waste of time, I was upset after a while, seeing how the story seem to prepare a crucial moment, I knew, was coming, given the trailers, and the terrible way that the marketing deparment decided to handle which information got out for this game before it even released.
It wasn't until a few hours until the game open up to me, that being meant on the literal sense, as much as on the methaforical one. As soon as I was able to explore the city everything felt right, as if I could suddenly come and do as much as I wanted to do, but just like prior Mafia games the real motivating factor for me to keep playing was the story, as well as the follow up to the story, this one being presented through cutscenes that jump back and foward in time, being narrated for the most part as events that happened years prior to the filming, of what's supposed to be a documentary, documenting the events and crimes that you commit along the game.
There are times in which I feel as if this doesn't work at it's fullest, it's an original take on telling an interesting story, and the fact that everything feels so dynamic, I guess it's something that certainly gave liberties to the writers to shake as many different plot points, as well as add different interpretations from different characters you meet, there's never an spoiler in any of the presentations tho, the most that you'll be able to tell from the cutscenes is which characters have survived, and what was their take on what happens as you play, but on a future date, I feel tho as if the game sometimes it's a bit reiterative with certain aspects of the game which are obvious... Yes, I know you're trying to take revenge, I get it, stop repeating it for christ sake!
That being said there are other aspects that I disagree in the way their being told, for a game that prides itself so much in telling an "authentic representation of the time and place" I feel as if the game it's only choosing to tell certain things, I get it's about the Mafia, but there's more to human beings, even while talking about the ones that have to do with crime, than people deriving pride for murders, and women that they get. The rascism it's another problem that I have, for the most part the game treats it with maturity, but god, there are times in which I wonder if the developers ever took a mirror to themselves, Why is it that every irish person you see it's a drunk? Or why is it that the Hatians of all mobs have to be the ones dealing with pot, and trafficking people? This type of stereotypes are not even rare, they're common to this day and age, so it's strange to me that for a game that claims is portraying such an "authentic" view of the time and place, only reduces it's commentary against rascism in some cases by simply using the "N-word" there's more than that to those issues, and just like the game says it in the first screen that you see after starting the game, for a game that's trying to be respectful towards the people that have suffered this type of discrimination for it to pretty much reduce it sometimes to something so repetitive and dull, it seems as if anything they've tried to banalize certain aspects about the problems of rascism, and of the society, from back then, as well as from right now.
The gameplay and the general natural progress it's what really saves it for me, the more and more that i've played, the more and more that I like the game, I hated it for the first few hours, but eventually, after a while the game turns out to be a lot more complex that I thought it would be, and it kept going like that until this point.
I really like the way that the gunplay feels, theres a very particular gruesome satisfaction to it, like when you mallet a bunch of meat, or something, it's a game of course, and a bunch of the executions that are divided into three different ones at that are always brutal to commit, they are repetitive, and at this point they have become a bit annoying, but frankly I still turn and grin a bit for how brutal some of them are made to be.
Overall there really isn't that much to Mafia 3, I think seeing it for what it is, it was the first attempt for a new studio into making a sequel to a great franchise, and in that sense I believe they failed to accomplish that, I don't feel the elegance, the class, the beauty of the design of all the other Mafia games here, it goes beyond further than the issues that the game faced when it first launched two days ago, the game suffers more... Grave, issues, that no patch will be able to fix, I think as a Mafia game Mafia 3 fails, because it's incapable to even articulate as an idea what was exactly that made the first two Mafia games so incredible, and cherished by fans, this feels as a very strong attempt into making something that carries a certain level of identity from the originals, while still a game that desperately is trying to create it's own, even then there's something, something that still somehow connects it to the other games in a small way, in an almost unnoticeable way, while at the same time being able to create it's own thing.
And in that regard I do believe Mafia 3 succeds, if not as a Mafia game in it's entirety, then as a game that seems connected by an almost invisible layer to the other games.
While of course still being a fun "visceral" experience.
Even then tho, if you're not that interested, wait for more patches, and for a sale, as for me, I have to recommend it, there's something that keeps me coming back to this game.

Nuclear Throne is a special kind of game. The one that you always rage at but keep coming back to. Here are my thoughts on it.
Cons:
- The frames. It usually isn't too much of a problem for me but the frames being locked at 30 for a fast rogue like game was not a good choice.
- Balance. This goes for both types of this issue. The weapons or characters are either too weak or too strong or sometimes both. Weapons like the disc gun and the screwdriver become useless because they just don't give you any benefits. Characters like Crystal have no downsides whatsoever and end up being the go to which neglects the other characters.
- Difficulty. Difficulty is usually a good thing. A game needs challenge so playing it is meaningful but this game sometimes flips that whole thing over. For example, if you spawn in a level with enemies all around you right off the bat you cannot escape. This game needs lightning fast reflexes and is like hell in boss fights like Lil Hunter.
- Looping. As soon as you loop, you're ♥♥♥♥ed. Random enemies everywhere who instakill you. It's a cluster♥♥♥♥.
Pros
- The bosses. They are fun to fight and satisfying to beat since they give you new items. They also have cool designs and are very hard (for the most part).
- Weapons. So many of the weapons in this game are awesome and creative. You go from a revolver to a quadruple machinegun and you have a gatling nuke launcher at your disposal. That is some crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥
- Characters. They have their own unique perks that are useful, but are not overpowered except for a certain purple pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥
- Music. It's great and really fits with your kicking of♥♥♥♥♥ It can go from peaceful to intense and helps make the tone of mutants shooting things up greater.
Verdict? It's good. Not perfect and not spectacular but it is a good game. It requires patience and reflexes because this is an extremely unforgiving game that will kick you back to level 1-1 no matter if you've reached the throne or not.

Shadow of War is another solid Middle-earth game, if you enjoyed Shadow of Mordor you will definitely enjoy this!
The story probably won't win any awards but it was good enough to keep me playing, however the combat is where the game is strongest. The Orc captains and warchiefs feel like more of a challenge compared to the first game, sometimes even adapting mid-fight to your stratigies. For example, if you keep vaulting over a captain to back-stab him, he will realise what you're doing and start to block your vault.
The betrayals and surprises from captains also keeps you on your toes, just as it looked like a battle was won, a captain would turn on me because I recently killed his blood-brother! Or when I've been knocked down and the enemy is about to deliver the killing blow, a friendly captain will jump in to save me at the last second.
The end portion of the game is where things take a weird turn however...It took me around 33 hours to complete the entire game (I left some of the collectables), the last 6-7 hours were very grindy BUT I didn't spend a penny of my own money on loot boxes (loot boxes contain "epic" or "legendary" Orc captains to add to your army).
Without spoiling anything, you need to have high-level Orcs in your army, and they need to upgraded a lot to make sure they're good enough to do the job.
I did however buy the basic loot boxes with money you earn in game, I found I had more than enough left over each time to upgrade the next army, but without those loot boxes I honestly would have given up on getting the "true" ending of the game (which you get after completing Act 4).
Overall I really enjoyed the game, if you're a fan of LOTR (or even if you're not) or you like the Batman Arkham series style of combat, I would highly recommend getting the game!

Hi, I'm a huge fan of flight sims, but this was not what I expected out of a very well respected flight simulator. I have been flying on Flight Gear, an open source flight simulator that is totally free, and I decided to upgrade to a sim with a more reliable game engine and better graphics. I did some research and found that FSX: Steam edition is almost the same as the $100 version. So, after buying and downloading FSX:SE I booted up the game and saw a terrible thing... the plane was already running. I then closed the simulation and looked through the settings to find a "Start aircraft cold" setting. After looking through the menus and multiple online forums I found that I could only "Cold Start" an aircraft by turning off the aircraft and saving it in that state. So, I booted up FSX:SE in a 747 and I look up to the overhead panel to turn off the aircraft and hit the battery switch. And then again. And again. But the battery switch will not turn off. I try to hit other buttons on the overhead pannel, and then discover, to my dismay, that I can only turn on the external lights. I go through the rest of the plane and discover that I can only hit a scarce amount of buttons and switches on the aircraft. I then go throught multiple aircraft and discover how little buttons I can hit. Very dissapointed in this simulator, cough (just a game) cough, I refunded my money. Don't buy this simulator (I'm sorry game) if you like going through full aircraft checklists.

Let me tell you a story about my son, Karee "The Legend" Kerman.
Karee was just finishing astronaut training when the first "Mun Men" made their launch.  They made a rough attempt at landing their craft on the Mun and end up crashing, leaving two poor souls, Bill and Bob, stranded.  Their pod skipped across the lunar landscape as they came to realize they would never see home again.  Little did they know their comrades had prepared another rocket with a brave soul, Valentina, to come rescue them with a similar craft.  She rocketed off, carrying the hopes and dreams of their nation.  Valentina was able to land successfully, but way too far from Bill and Bob's original landing site, so she decided she would hover across the Mun to link up.  Valentina successfully hovered to Bill and Bob's pod, but she had used too much fuel trying to get over.  She too was now stranded...
When all hope was lost and nobody else wanted to go on another rescue mission, Karee volunteered to go alone.  He launched just two weeks after Bob and Bill had made their launch and not two days into his own career.  He navigated his craft into orbit around the Mun and landed just a few kilometers from the other two landing sites.  Perfect execution.  Bill, Bob, and Valentina then made the "Mun walk" of a lifetime by thrusting themselves to Karee's rescue craft.  All three boarded safely.  That was the easy part.  The rest depended on Karee's ability to pilot them back home.  He took off, sent them speeding low and fast around the Mun, and slingshot them towards home.  Karee then piloted them into the atmosphere.
I was so proud of my son Karee.  Finally, they were coming home safe... I went with the rescue team personally, saying -
"Karee, on my wayward son"

To be honest, I'm not a real fan of point and click adventures, I usually get frustrated when I have to say one specific thing to one person to get an item, and then proceed to another completely unrelated person, just to get a different item. That's my views on this genre anyway, but Broken Age did a great job of not really having a couple dozen steps to get anything done. The art style was interesting, and the music really helped define the characters and the situations they were placed in. My overall rave about this however is the ending. With this game being so early in development and very small in size (around 500Mbs download), it’s difficult to find anything positive to review about Warmode. It’s simply a Counter Strike clone with an ADS mechanic.
Many players have reported game breaking bugs, but I have yet to experience these bugs other than the audio cutting out and audio clues were being delayed when firing weapons from time to time.
The main concern with a game of any type being as small as this one is that it will likely find itself flooded with hackers and this should be the developer’s top priority if they wish to develop this game further. Just take a look at Warface.
With that said the map design is solid for the most part and a few maps have clearly been inspired by Counter Strike, one being a clear copy of Dust from Counter Strike but the spawn points need work, as spawn trapping is near impossible to avoid. Net code and servers that run this game seem solid, I experienced zero lag during the short time I played but keeping consistent high frame rates was difficult even with my PC being way above the recommended requirements.
With some performance, animation optimization and better textures this game could have a solid platform to grow, but this game does not bring any thing that sets it apart from the crap ton of F2P FPS games already found on Steam making it difficult to see why anyone would play this game over Counter Strike: Nexon Zombies or Dirty Bomb as they are also completely free of charge.

Well I have had this game for a couple weeks now and put 154 hours of my time (including nights when I left it running so I could avoid a queue wait in Archeage) in to it. Before you immediately discontinue reading my no life review please take in to consideration that a recent injury has basically locked me to my house and just today back to work with restrictions.
Alright on to the review. This game is definitely a great game if you ever played the original or even the fallout series. This game however is very different from the fallout series and let me tell you why. Warning there are spoilers on gameplay within the review but not actual events I will be making a guide soon that will give other spoilers.
In fallout I played as a melee fighter and could basically demolish my way through anything. In this however melee is mediocre throughout the entire story line becoming less effective each battle. Pistols are lots of shots but they aren't a great way to do damage imo, however if you can have your players controlled by the ai then let me tell you crits, large action points, and accuracy seem to be increased making them a mean opponent and sometimes trusty ally. Shotguns. Oh shotguns, well opponents with them will literally♥♥♥♥♥♥on your entire team dealing easily 70 damage to each later game when you spawn in to a battle. Otherwise if you use a shotgun be prepared to either get a lucky angle or you will have to move around so your shot is most effective or maybe just so it wont damage your team or allies. I don't recommend them and I barely used the shotgun  on my team. Rifles. Simple to say if you put your time in to it that it will be deadly just as it is for the opponent, not much difference here. Explosives. Well let me tell you that the expense for rockets can be worth it when you have a grouped up opponent but unless that is the case then you will only be looking at a lot of money wasted. P.S. grenades aren't worth the expense. Energy weapons. The first portion of the game these what seem like future tech weapons are comparitively just as bad if not worse then other low range, high ap, low damage weapons. However they immediately take a turn in the second portion of the game and easily become just as effective as rifles. Sniper rifles. These too are deadly and I would rank them right next to rifles the entire game with perhaps a little better quality than rifles the first portion of the game. And finally smgs. They are mediocre throughout the campaign and luckily are cheap to fuel compared to their damage. You may not kill fast but you will save some scrap while doing it.
Now let me say I probably put about 75 hours in to the story mode I actually finished. This is right around their 80+ mark and it is only because I didn't mingle with all of the side missions. That was extremely promising and I loved that aspect of the game. I also noted 4 different ways to end the game all with multiple turnouts based on your decisions for side quests and companions. This could be only a couple of ways however. Another thing I found interesting is that you can win the game at level one just as you can at whatever the max level may be. I beleive I only reached the low 30's. You may think you can't but I assure that if you finish the game you will understand what I mean. Wish there wasn't an end and it allowed you to do a free roam basically and allow you to finish side missions you avoided or something but oh well Ill just redo it and attempt to do everything possible.
The problems I have are the surprise encounters you face leaving your military based squad clumped in a lovely circle formation just perfect for that three burst shotgun and grenade to devour. Also saving should be a little less manipulative so it won't allow you to basically try until you succeed. I do think this should result in more successful roles and lower level locked doors, chests, etc... This would also make it possible to win when gambling. As of right now I promise you will never win while gambling it is rigged so you wont. This makes since though because people would just save gamble and save when they win and save gamble and load when they lose.
This game is great and if you are looking to find a game like fallout then try it out. It's worth it!

So I looked into Mafia III and when I found out that 2k refused to send out review copies lets me know that 2k had known that the "finished" copy of the game was no good enough to match what we expected for a game in development for 4+ years and realized it would suck thus explaining why their was no review copy sent out. Cons the game offers...

Wasteland 2 is perfect definition for term "mixed feelings". At best, it's just mediocre post-apocalyptic cRPG. At worst - it's game full of bugs, inconsistencies and bad design decisions. But for some strange reason, I couldn't stop playing it. So pick it on sale with 75% discount.
Pros:
- Story you may like, especially if you're a fan of Terminator/Mad Max movies. There's enough bandits and robots to kill.
- Most quests can be solve in more than one way. Or you can just shoot everyone.
- Music.
- Radio broadcasts are fun
- Some strange magic - I couldn't stop playing, despite all flaws (and there are many flaws)
- California - whole second part of the game is cool. Great factions, more interesting quests, etc. Unfortunately, more bugs too, and you first need to play 40h of boring Arizona. There's big chance you will never see Holywood.
Cons (long list):
- Bugs, bugs, bugs - broken quests, cutscenes not diplaying correctly, messed-up scripts (leading to broken quests) and more
- Game looks bad. Really, really bad. Fallout 2 looks better. Probably any game released last 10 years looks better. It's first game I wanted to quit while making character. And yes, I completely understand that graphic is not important.
- Massive FPS drops.
- Unresponsive UI - sometimes you need to click several times on button or on the ground to execute action (go somewhere, change or reload weapon etc.)
- Tactical, turn-based battles? Forget it. In most fights (many, many fights) you just need to shoot enemies while they come to you. You can't cover (because there are no covers), head shot is not valid option (because of massive penalties) and most enemies are just chargin on you. Shadowrun offers more tactical battles that Wasteland 2. So, Wasteland 2 is not Divinity: Original Sin, XCOM, Jagged Alliance 2. It's not even close.
- Pathfinding - if you want to move from one end of map to another, your team most probably will not be able to.
- Character development - there's nothing interesting in it. With each level you get some skill points, sometimes 1 attribue points. As you need all skills (or almost all), trying to create some unique builds is not an option. And there are no perks or anything that would allow you to create really unique ranger.

It's been a long time since a game has had me this hooked. I've always been a huge fan of Fallout 1/2, and while I enjoyed Fallout 3 and New Vegas, I felt that they always lacked a certain something when compared the originals. FO2 was adult-themed. It was nasty, dirty, gritty, dark, and more importantly it was REAL. Religious lunatics, extensive drug use, raiders, gambling, cannibalism, prostitution, dying villages, hunger, starvation, ghouls, and exploding whales.  It took almost 20 years, but finally Wasteland 2 comes around and they did it RIGHT.
First of all let me say that there is a LOT of content in this game. I've heard stories of 20 hours to finish the game. I'm almost 50 hours in and I still have a long ways to go on my first playthrough. Just when I thought the game was over, it threw a whole 'Please insert CD2' moment at me. Not only that, the game remains INTERESTING throughout. You are always finding new weapons, mods, enemies, etc that keep the game exciting. You know that feeling you get when you find you find a new, powerful weapon? Or a new piece of amor? Wasteland 2 manages to maintain that excitement throughout the majority of its playthrough, and that keeps you coming back for more.
Not to mention the writing, while at times a bit contrived or cheesy, is one of the best in the business these days. Sometimes it's hilarious, sometimes it's silly, sometimes it's interesting. Fallout 1/2 fans will feel right at home.
It's not perfect, in fact not near it. There are a lot of bugs in the game. There's been several times where I've had very random things occur. One time my characters would not enter a door to continue a quest line. Nothing happened when I clicked. I tried to reload from a previous save and try again and the same thing happened. I tried leaving the zone and coming back and that luckily fixed it. Unfortunately there are enough bugs like this to make Wasteland 2 frustrating at times. 5 hours or so into my playthrough, and I learned to get into the habit of saving, saving, saving. Doing this has kept the frustration down to a minimum.
The other cons are tolerable. The voice acting is here and there, sometimes feeling half-way finished. There are occasional typos. Sometimes the game does not give you enough direction on where to finish your quest, or alert you to certain items being important of unimportant. There are some balancing issues as well. Some of the environments can get old, and the combat itself can become very repetitive. There is also a ridiculous amount of repetitive looting. 95% of the time or so when you loot a chest, locker, cabinet, hole, or safe, you will find some ammo, some pants, and some junk. It would have been nice to get a more exciting loot system such as 'You beat this guy, take his key, and open his personal safe just to find a new 5.56mm pistol' or something.
Overall, however, the game is a blast and deserves much praise. It is games like this that can only be done right on PC, and it is games like this that a PC gamer can be proud of. I hope to all end that the positive sales figures allow this series to continue on. I would not hesitate for a second to order DLC or Wasteland 3.

Had this game for the last week or so, have dumped 14+ hours into it so far, which means it's time for me to stop being lazy and write a well-deserved review.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION:
This game plays similarly to the Don't Starve franchise, if you've ever played that or watched someone play it, but is vitally different in a lot of aspects.  You play as Flux, a purple suit of armor with no thumbs and an infinite inventory that manages itself.  Along with your trusty robot companion, you are plopped onto a foreign world via spaceship crash, and it's your job to survive, re-ascertain contact with the company you work for, and eventually get home (I think, if you have one).  The game is sort of a 2D sidescrollerish game, but the world is completely open, filled with lots of little things for you to loot, kill, and ultimately upgrade your housing, weapons, gear, and crafting stations.  There are literally HUNDREDS of items to harvest and collect and craft.  Combat takes some accurate timing and getting used to, but it's loads of fun.
PROS:
-Nice graphics, very nice art style
-Fun combat
-TONS of things to collect and craft
-Infinite, self-managing inventory
-Tools that equip themselves only when you need them, and disappear when you dont so they're not in the way
-Lots of content
-Building stuff, in addition to the aforementioned crafting
-Lots of different enemmies with varying attacks and variations of the species
-Pets made from killed enemies that help you in combat with active attacks and passive buffs
-Great music
-Addicting
-Cross platform saving with mobile
-No permadeath, if you die you can just walk to your gravemarker and pick up the stuff you lost
-Teleports all over the map for fast travel
CONS:
-I wish it wasn't such a pain to navigate between sections of the world like the Savanna and Bawg and then get back to your original house without making another one.
-I'm honestly trying so hard to find flaws - but godamn I love this game.
TL;DR:
This game only costs $15, and if I had known how much I would enjoy it, I would have paid $40.  It's amazingly fun, with humorous dialogues, fun gameplay, and very intuitive crafting and item collection/use.  I would HIGHLY recommend this game to anyone, even if you're new to games of this type.  I wasn't a huge fan of Don't Starve, but I love this game.  I wish I could high-five the devs and buy them beer.
Easily 9/10.
It is fun. Solid game. Yes.

Look. Nobody likes Loot Boxes. That was dumb. But was Shadow of War a good game?
Yes. It takes the Nemesis System and expands upon it. If you're playing at the Nemesis difficulty, you truly will find yourself invested-yet-frustrated as you try to make your armies work. It's basically Mordor, but with a little added complexity.
SoW's story is a lot more satisifying than Mordor, but that's not really saying much.
The real pride of the game remains playing off the Orcs you meet, fight, die to, and vow a personal vengence against. If you're the type of player who interally roleplays his character's motivations and monolouges it's easy to get lost in the endless sea of loveable Orcs.
The game shows it's weakness, however, when there is nothing left to conquer. I don't mean that literally, but rather once the dust of a new zone clears and the vast majority of the map is under the Bright Lord's Control. You don't feel like you made progress, gazing over seas of hostile orcs in a land in which every freakin' person on the map should be loyal to you. There is little to be done but dodge the now pointless orcs and collect artifacts and complete challenges before running off to the next zone. No advantage to staying, and little reward for complete dominion.
The controls are fine, through detection of when you are trying to flee up a wall or off a cliff is sometimes spotty, resulting in Talion waddling when he should be running. Combat is crisp and clean, and the impact of a rising combo meter feels rewarding, even on the highest difficulty.
The Lootboxes sour my personal opinion on the whole thing, and a part of me felt like merely buying the game was to enable the boxes.... But I am glad I did. It's more of Mordor, and it's a game I am enjoying playing. You don't have to buy the lootboxes to beat the game, thankfully.

Garry's Mod is impossible to completely explore in a few hours. Sure it's a "simple" sandbox game based off half-life, but there is soooo much more than assets ripped from half-life. If you like doing random stupid stuff, there's plenty of that. I can't say Garry's Mod replicates these things perfectly, but the ability to do all these things in one game, with infinite customizability, makes this game just fanominal. I truely think this game fills the empty wants inside of us. I personally was annoyed by the lack of control you had in most games. In Garry's Mod, you have the ability to manipulate things in a way no game has ever made possible. Maybe this game isn't as fun to some as it is to me, but I think anyone can find lots of fun in this. Besides, it's really cheap, and it goes on sale for cheaper.
