Took away aspects of strategy and made the nemisis system feel gimmicky. And unimportant.
But it wasn't too bad at all....
That was until I got to Shadow War...
I don't know many reviews that incorporate images to describe ones emotion, to visually display it for easier consumption and understanding.
But this is how Shadow Wars made me feel after several battles, but it still is not done;
A boring monotounous grind that I just want to be over with.
Oh, and the best damn part? You have to spend A LOT more Mithril than in the previous chapters of the game to defend your strongholds compared to assaulting them.
7500 for Metal Walls. And then hundreds more for other upgrades.
Otherwise you "enjoy" a significantly longer battle. Rather than a streamlined, efficient one.
Basically. Grind for a good while for currency and XP, or give up seeing the ending.
After playing and finishing Chapter 3, I genuinely thought that was gonna be the end..But, a 4th chapter, I was like "What? There's more?! AWEOMSE!." Nah. Shadow War. God damn Shadow War.
This shouldn't be in a game. The only reason it is here is to justify the fact they lied about the size of the game in comparison to the first game and blatantly misrepresented it's sheer size as a whole and arbitrarily increase the playtime. Which is just sad.
But, god damn it. Shadow War really does irritate me. I was considering the DLC, seeing as I got Shadow of War for free, basically, with my new GPU. But, nah. Not bothering with the grind.
DISCLAIMER: If you are happy with the grind. Dude. Go right, ahead. If you like grind, then this game is for you. And I will be entirely happy with the fact that people do like this game. But personally. I don't. And it is my right to hold that opinion just as it is your right to disagree with it. But do not comment going "Well HURR DURR I AM FINE WITH THE GRINNED SO UR OPIONION IS A STUPIT AND I AM RIUGHT AND U R WONRG". Because, seriously, we're on PC. We're supposed to be better than that. Better than blind loyatly and fanboyism. We're supposed to accept opinions and act like adults. Not insult people over them not liking your new favorite toy.
Other than that, I fully intend to finish it. But I don't think the average person could so in one burst.
I'll complete a stage of shadow war, maybe once every weeks so I can stretch it out and not have to play it all in one go. Or I'll watch the ending on YouTube if I get too bored.

This game is neat, but the one issue I've been having in plays of it is that it seems easy for the teams to become unbalanced. If one of the commanders isn't on top of things, or if your team isn't communicating very well and theirs is, you will get torn apart within a matter of minutes. I suppose that's true of all games, but in one where what the teams can bring to bear escalates on an RTS-style path, I just wish there were a way for a losing team to come back from losing more easily. That is, I wish the game had a bit more tug-of-war and didn't so much reward winning with more winning.
That said, one thing I do admire about it is that it is very hard for one person to dominate the game and make everyone else seem superfluous as in many FPS games.
I also dig the alien team mechanics a lot, and I like the option to play the RTS game as the commander; it's really fun if your team has some good communication going.
TLDR: Fun in a good server. Kind of 'eh' when you're being rolled.

Yes, attacking may result in you losing some orcs, but that is the same as attacking a fortress in the single player mode so there's no issue there.  Online vendettas are nice as I found I was running out of hostile orcs in my own game, so it was nice to be able to fight more orcs outside of the fortress.  The daily/weekly challenges can also add a bit of replayability while waiting for the DLCs to drop.  Only thing I would have like to seen was a way to manually defend a fortress after completing the shadow wars.
I personally enjoyed the story they crafted despite it being quite the reach from Tolkien's writings.  I loved the first game and this improved on those pieces in every way.  Luckily, loot boxes didn't ruin the experience for me, but I give props to those who stand by their convictions about not buying this game because they were included.

I'd personally recc. this game. People seem to make a uproar over the loot crates and the possibility of funds being moved stealthily past the passed director's family, however, the second point is unlikely and unproven. The loot crates on the other hand, they are very simple and they really cause no harm to the game's environment, they simply add more to do by encouraging you to save up currency to grow your army and test a little RNG to see what you get. The loot crates are bad to use early-game and are not gamebreaking in any way, the only thing that could be powerful about the loot crates themselves is the possibility of a legendary follower, in which case, even if you get one, it may not be a powerful follower. The loot crate system merely gives a little rng minigame to get rare followers imo, it causes no ingame or online difficulty. The most powerful orcs will always be those you train yourself, as you can use "tokens" and "Upgrades/commands/training orders" to increase follower strength and power.(you can also port orcs from your old game, shadow of mordor). The online siege is determined by the power of the fort and orcs you have, yes, but the biggest factors are player skill and the training and effort you put into countering, learning, and defeating your enemy with your own army, your own customized castle, and your own customized defenses. The combat in this game is very fun, however the more difficult defender classes with adapting traits and counters are quite agitating to fight. The brutality in the combat makes it entertaining, the first game felt similar to a god simulator at times, making your character very strong. In this game, however, your character is powerful, but some orcs can truly best you, over and over. Enjoy! The combat and system heirarchy is really fun, though i wish they added a bit to the hierachy of minas ithil itself. Lots more to do in this game! Also it stays true to a good amount of the lore! There's also way more interesting variation and classes in the orcs in this game, increasing the difficulty.

I cant recommend it yet. The Models need serious attention, and its clear that some areas received a lot of love and care in their construction and others are very much still Beta-Playtest blanks; and this is in the intro areas, Im talking about Citadel, Ag Center and Hightower.  Stat, loot and skill balancing needs work, and there's some very *very* clunky and poorly thought out UI choices, which Im unsure of whether they can blame that on Unity or not.
Considering the LOD that the Cenega XCOM games, and most recently the *actual* Xcom games recieved, the turn based combat here doesnt seem retro, it just seems amateurish. not being able to force 'combat mode' so you can properly position your people to spring ambushes is particularly awful if you're trying the higher difficulty levels.
Admittedly most of my gripes come down to mechanics; but the HardAss/KissAss/SmartAss mechanics ties directly into the players experience of the plot, and to split this out into three stats rather than a single Social check results in the player experiencing their characters as belligirent, smarmy or conniving caricatures, rather than intelligent people making choices.
I keep putting the hours in, hoping it'll turn around, but for now Im really rather disappointed: this comes across less like a sequel to wasteland, and more like the original wasteland creators haven't played or written a game since then; and then came out of hibernation, dug out UnityInANutshell and promised all us whippersnappers a good time.

. It is one of the most disappointing games I've played in years, with very few redeeming qualities.

Original story, set in a part of the world that isn't often explored in videogames. However, the story is conveyed entirely via cutscenes and only the first one has voiceovers; the remaining dozens do not. The cutscenes are mostly exposition, and the gameplay barely feels connected to the story.
Game ends on a cliffhanger promising a sequel or an expansion. Remains unclear if it'll happen.
Game it very, very short. A playthrough while watching the cutscenes is about 4-5 hours long. Replayability is almost non-existent.
The weapons and equipment variety is extremely low for an action-RPG. I changed gear a total of 5 times from start to finish.
Skills variety is low. Descriptions don't update past the first level, making it impossible to know what leveling a skill to the second and third level does before investing points.
Game difficulty is poorly balanced. Instead of fixing it, the developers added cheat codes to be invincible and skip levels...
Levels are very linear and exploration is not rewarded. There is no minimap.
It is rather obvious that the game wasn't developed by native English speakers, or translated by someone who had the skills to do so. In addition to numerous typos and grammar mistakes, sentences structure is often incorrect, making the story harder to follow. My favorite error is the game title: on Steam, it is called "Legends of Persia"; in-game, it is "Legend of Persia".
Graphics are dated and the aesthetics are bland and generic. Animations are sub-par.
Editor promised in the Key Features section is unavailable.

Coming at this as being my first foray into the MX vs. ATV series, I have to say that I find this game a mixed bag.
The game isn't bad. For a game from 2006 it's actually pretty decent, if nothing impressive visually. Controls work well with a 360 controller and even support both joysticks for camera rotation, something that older pre-Xinput games didn't always do, and the racing mechanics are solid enough.
All that said, even in 2006 there were better games you could have been spending your money on. The game looks and feels like a budget title even for the time, with the licensed soundtrack being the title's real high point. The AI rubber bands like nobody's business, a feature racing games still have a problem with, and the lack of real impact your bike or ATV has on the course makes for a game that just doesn't feel great to play. Combined with limited graphical and gameplay tuning options and you have an experienced that is easily surpassed by any number of titles both on and off Steam.
The price point isn't terrible, but feels like it is somewhat more than the game deserves given its limitations and the game's overall forgettable nature. On the plus side, the game runs fine first-boot on Windows 8.1 with a full suite of modern hardware, so if you do decide to take the plunge there is little in the way of configuration needed to get it to run, though widescreen support would have been nice to see.
Recommended, but only for the fact that those with some sense of nostalgia for it shouldn't be disappointed by this version or its ability to run. For newcomers, though? Look elsewhere.

I would love to recommend this game.
Unfortunately I cannot. It was advertised as a spiritual successor to Fallout 1 & 2 and sadly it is nowhere near the quality of these games.
Given the credentials of the creators of this game, the fundamental issues it has have been a major dissapointment to me.
I could look over the simple, passable if shallow combat system in what was supposed to be a crpg, but mostly is a tactical squad shooter.
But hopelessly shallow and illogical crpg mechanics I cannot forgive.
The attributes are very weak and have very little impact on gameplay, like maximum 10 Coordination gives +10 to hit - about as much as 1-2 ranks in the respective weapon skill. And less then what 1 weapon mod can give you...
Speaking about skills, this system is awfully shallow, with no connection between attributes and skills. Yes, your 1 Strenght wimp will be just as good at bashing doors open, as a 10 Strenght champion strongman. Or your 1 Charisma cavemen will talk just as smoothly as your 10 Charisma face. There is a large number of skills, many of which are redundant (medic and surgeon, lockpicking and safe cracking, perception and outdoorsman, to a lesser degree the separate combat skills for each weapon type).
Out of the attributes in the end only the derived stats Action Points and Combat Initiative really count.
There are no perks/traits/talents.
There is actually little incentive to keep levelling after the first 20 levels or so. As the skills check difficulty will invariably rise as the game goes on and only the highest skill ranks are worth anything,  you need to split the skill load between charcters. So on each level you get some more hp and some skill points, which you assign to the same skills you have chosen for each character at the beginning of the game. The levelling process could just as well be automated.
Oh and you get a stat point... every 10 levels.
There are no range accuracy modifiers, no aiming at and disabling different body parts.
Terrible, random loot. What's with the hordes of containers and safes! spread seeingly randomly all over the place? Was it raining safes in Arizona or something? That's beyond silly. Oh and when you finally diffuse that trap and beat that impossible lock guarding that chest/safe, you will certainly feel very rewarded when you find 5 bullets and a glass eye inside. Don't expect valuable stashes of old technology hidden by some bosses/factions/military organizations/research centers, not in this game, no. Only a handfull of bullets for you. Better buy your guns at the local vendor... oh and that power armor too.
Actually maybe don't. Armor... suffice to say it's horrible. In the end game it's much safer not to wear any...

Life is Strange strips most of the game away to focus on its characters and its narrative, and as a result it does these things so incredibly well. While some characters serve as generalisations of certain groups - geeks, jocks, hipsters, etc. - each of the games characters have amazing depth.
Max is lovable and her development into a strong person following her experiences is heartwarming. Each character minor or major has clearly defined personalities and each of thier actions are justified through a set of airtight characteristics, insofar as I never once said 'this character is unrealistic/no-one would ever do that.' One of the best characterised characters in gaming in my opinion is David, the ex-soldier who we see struggle with coming back to reality, and I as the player went from hating him to loving him so gradually that I didn't notice until it hit me like a frieght train. The fact that the extreme opposite is true for
characters stands as a testiment to this game's excellent characterisation.
Each major decision feels emotionally meaningful even on the rare occasion that they don't matter to the plot. As a result of these decisions Max grows as a person, as I felt myself growing as well. And I spent five minutes looking at the last choice. The friendship and love and hate in this story all feel genuine, to the point where its difficult for me to leave Arcadia Bay behind.
This game will remain an inspiration to me going forward. Absolutely stunning.

Pit fighting, also fun. Though after so many, you know what beats what and the surprise is taken out of it. Not all of the orc classes are balanced in pit fighting. Beast masters for example. They could have "epic skill: call graug" or "den mother" but never use it. Also, caragor mounts made pit fighting very dull. Half the time the orc would ride around in a big circle, while gangs fought gangs, and do nothing till every minion was dead.
I (unlike some) did enjoy the story. I know it's kind of dumb; certain aspects. I just liked it. Until it died at the end, which is where this review comes to the "do not buy this" section.
Act IV - The Shadow Wars
Sounds cool af right? Wrong. It may as well be named, "Act IV: Grind your @ss off with no more story or dialogue sans random orc encounters, OR pop out the wallets and buy your way to a half-@ssed cutscene.
They say the store and lootboxes aren't "necessary". They aren't lying, but they aren't being truthful either. The last act of the game is set up in such a way that it blatantly incentivizes purchasing. Because unless you do, then your only other option is to grind and grind and GRIND to get the orcs needed to defend/retake your fortresses.
Then, you have 10 stages. 20 fortress defenses. All of which play out the same. Kill siege beasts, kill warchiefs, your army either keeps bleeding and dying due to you not having the best orcs or best defenses, or they sit and jerk off inside impenetrable walls. Leaving you to hop down solo to kill a bit, climb back in for arrows and health, and repeat the process. 20 times....
It is so boring, and so disconnected from the flow of the first 3 acts, you feel as if it isn't the game you have been playing for 100+ hrs. It FEELS like a game+ mode, where you beat the game and then get the chance to screw around in the world for as long as you want.
I have to add a spoiler section for those that think they are gonna miss something by not playing this. Or ones not entirely convinced by the top reasons. So here goes.
You as Talion, with Celebrimbor, forge a new ring as powerful as Saurons. You then go on a nice journery of doing things. Not gonna spoil everything. You meet characters that literally have no relevance at the end. Humans that just up an leave like you never existed. A tree spirit that has the most interesting story, but disappears once you complete it. Then an elf assassin that has a big part to play in TWO scenes, and then you never know what happens to her.
Ratbag and Ranger, two orcs/olog are like your main story subbordinates but you never actually get to add them to the ranks of your army. Dumb. Bruz betrays you for no reason other than to betray you and show you it can happen. Felt forced.
Then...THEN, final battle time (or so you think, cause stupid Act IV comes after) you go to attack Baradur. To attack Sauron. Celebrimbor betrays you, gives the new ring to the elf assassin. You hate them both, want to kill them both. But guess what? You never get to interact with them again. Instead, you become a ring wraith, have a nice fight with the Witch King, take over Minas Morgal. Then Celebrimbor and Elf Assassin chick fight Sauron, they lose. Celebrimbor gets absorbed into Sauron and they say there is an internal war between them. Dunno. Never shows it, never get to find anything out.
Talion grinds with no story for about 20 hrs to fight 20 sieges, then it shows a recap of the LOTR movies where they add in Talions face on a wraith dragon, and show a light - presumably celebrimbor's spirit flying out of a dying sauron into mount doom. Whatever happens to the second ring and the elf assassin, no one knows. You just get a cut scene of Talion tossing his armor and weapons into a field, and walking off into the sunset.
Totally not worth the grind and all the money one has to put into it.
First 3 acts are fun. I enjoyed them. Last act and ending are BS though.
So I repeat, do NOT buy the game. Not worth it. Get it at a discount if anything.

Mountain is an interesting game to say the least. You have very minimal interaction with a mountain that is completely cut off from the rest of the world stranded in space. Despite only being able to move the camera and rearrange the space junk (That consists of horses, arrows, and trash cans) you find yourself attached to your mountain. The little comments that it writes giving the inanimate object a personality. Eventually you bond with mountain, realizing that there is more to mountain than your first thought. You bond over your mutual enjoyment of the weather. You help mountain rearrange its space junk, or treasures as you call them. Eventually an old music box is given to you from the space trash man and you begin to call it your precious. The voices whisper to you. They tell you how Mountain isn't has nice as it seems. But precious plays music that soothes you, it counsels the inner voices. But the inner voices start yelling instead of whispering to be heard over the voices. They tell you what mountain is planning. Mountain wants your precious. You know you can’t stop Mountain. In a futile attempt to halt the hand of fate you hit every key until it all stops and you have no control. A wild dwarf star approaches. In what feels like an eternity but is only a few seconds your friend is gone. Forever lost to the cold void of space. And you feel guilt. You mourn Mountain. This game took me through an emotional rollercoaster. All and all worth the dollar.

I’m not going to talk about the graphics issues (because i haven’t had any). What I will talk about is what people want to hear, the story, or rather, the boring, repetitive shallow story it has in gameplay built up around seemingly unconnected and boring cut scenes of an investigation into a CIA agent (nobody cares about).
Overall the game goes something like this. First a crazy character is introduced (stereotype), voodoo woman, drunk Irishman, rich old guy... Secondly you take out their underbosses by beating the guy with the shotgun, guy with the sniper, guy with the Molotov... Thirdly you give the territory to the crazy guy you spoke to earlier... Sounds repetitive? it is, this is the game in a nut shell and it doesn’t get any more interesting beyond the first "ward", feels very much like the gameplay of just cause 1,2,3.
In case your wondering, yes the first heist mission is the best in the game, it had detail, a genuine story and deepish characters, overall this is what the whole game should have been, they even managed it to an extent in Mafia 1 and 2 but its like they just gave up on 3 and focused on shoot them up arcade like action instead.
You cant buy property, fill up your car, buy clothes, change your hair or any of the small but very immersive details of the first games, it has got rid of all of them. Even the uniqueness of the second with the changing time periods is gone, replaced with mundane boring new Orleans which despite what the trailers say feels flat and dead (probably because you cant do anything in it when not on a mission).
Then we have the AI, or rather lack of it, the AI are terrible with a very strange hit algorithm, they go from no accuracy to pin point precision randomly hitting you with a full auto burst from the other side of the mission area then missing at point blank with a pistol. They also do the annoying kamikaze thing bad AI do by rushing you point blank seemingly suicidal which messes up your ability to aim and hit them in third person (I died multiple times due to this).
If I could describe this game in the way if feels it would be the illegitimate love child of LA Noire and Just cause... If your into that (mindless violence, empty world with a shallow story which had potential) you probably will like this game.
Overall 6/10.

Original review:
Enjoyed I and II, both great games. 5 hours in on III, and love it.
This is vastly improved on II, with far more story so far with some fantastic cuts scenes and much more to do in the open map than II, by a long shot.
I am suffering crashes the same as anyone else, I've had 3 in 5 hours, but it certainly hasn't ruined the game yet for me, and I'm sure the developers will patch and fix.
Some of the controls are a bit clunky, same as in II and the AI isn't fantastic, though I don't think it's as bad as some people are making out.
I honestly don't think the graphics are as bad as people are making out either, everything so far on my rig looks fantastic.
The sound tracks are just awesome, I'm really enjoying listening to some old 60's music, sometimes sit in the car waiting for a track to finish before getting out, great stuff.
Long and the short of it, if you liked Mafia II, you will love Mafia III, especially if you're like me and it's more about the story than the killing / driving etc.
Some might want to wait til the FPS and crashes are fixed, if that sort of thing really bothers you, but it's well worth the purchase imo.

I have simmed with FSX boxed for a long time now, and I just recently made the switch to SE, and I must say, I really enjoy having multiplayer back without worrying about LAN servers. SE allows you to hop into a lobby of your choice, or even create your own session for simming with friends.

Works with a ton of my joysticks, yokes, and even custom mapped switch panels
Fun with friends: FSX is great alone, but if your looking into SE, you probably want to fly with other pilots around the world! This is the main reason I picked up SE and I am very happy.
Cons:
Some public servers are pretty chaotic & uncontrolled. If you want a true flight experience, you must VATSIM or host your own server and invite your friends. The public servers are still fun!
OVERALL:
If you are reading this, and you enjoy aviation, avionics, ATC, airports, or if you want to be a pilot some day, this is a MUST HAVE! FSX is to pilot enthusiasts as Nascar is to racing fans! :)

Hello everyone and welcome to Goldswags guide to WARMODE.
WARMODE is a free-to-play first person shooter which was released on the Steam Store on 25 August 2015 after being greenlit by the community on the Steam Greenlight project earlier this year.
The graphics are quite ropey for 2015, but would have been considered good about 5 to 10 years ago, and the menu system looks like it was built in powerpoint by someone bored in an IT GCSE class, however the game is very much in early-access mode, as evidenced by the fact the file size for the game was only 250mb, and the developer has commented they are expecting to bring more out soon.
The game is supported financially by the fact you can buy masks and stickers as purely cosmetic items, with no impact on the gameplay itself, meaning so far the game is not pay to win.
You will see many reviews on steam calling this a mix between Counter Strike: Global Offensive and Call of Duty, and it is easy to see immediately why these comparisons are drawn.  The crosshair and shooting system will feel completely natural to anyone coming from a counter strike background, and even in my first game I realised I was getting easy kills and headshots because of this.  You can also right click to look down the sights of your gun, in the style of Call of Duty, however I found this actually made it more difficult for me to aim.
At the moment it is completely deathmatch style, with instant respawns after death, and no real objectives.  This means at times I was able to just do the worst thing every and camp the enemy spawn for minutes at a time.  I also found that spraying seemed just as effective has shooting in short bursts, as it appears each players hitbox is the size of your entire screen.
Despite all of this, dare I say it...I actually had a lot of fun playing this game.  The arcade style of the game and the easy pick and play nature of it has an unusual appeal.  Please don't confuse what I am saying here – this is NOT a good game, and I don't think it will be developing an e-sports game anytime soon – however it is just really fun.  I don't know why, I don't know how, but you will have to take my word for it and give it a try.
Also, if you can explain to me why grenades are more expensive than most high cost rifles please let me know.  I never saw one go off once, so I can only imagine it is because they have napalm like capabilities.  However, as you will see due to the unusual control layout I had no idea how to throw mine, and it took me so long to save up for that the game had already ended before I found out.  It's “G” by the way (I think).
Anyway, this is WARMODE, and I hope you enjoy it at least a little – I did.

Yargis is an old styled action space shooter. You meet the world of Yargis in front of the conflict and you're the only one who can sort it out.
You start the game as a beginner and learn how to control the ship and guns :) Your main task is to flight from the space and fight with the enemies. Throughout the missions you're challenged with flying through labirynths and completing the objectives in certain missions. It's not always about eliminating enemies, but sometimes you need to collect parts or survive the level. The levels in the Story mode are not very difficult but you need to upgrade your ship by buying new guns or armor from the money earned by completing levels. The offline mode is a little bit more challenging so you need to care about upgrades more than in story mode. It was designed to be the training mode for multiplayer so it's obvious.
I really enjoyed how the ships are controlled. At first I had some troubles with discovering how to brake the ship but the Space button on KB is really helpful. The way how the ships are behaving is really nice and feels realistic. For example if you fly close to planet, your ship is affected by it's gravity. Therefore if the planet grabs your ship, you need to use boost to counter the force of planet's gravity. I was very satisfied with the graphics. The details of space and planets are really fantastic.

NS2 is a unique blend of a RTS and a FPS. Two teams compete for resource nodes that will benefit players with upgrades and weapons. Depending on which team you are on, aliens or marines, the game will play dramatically different. Marines will play like a traditional FPS with weapons like shotguns, grenade launchers and flamethrowers, while aliens are more suited for close ranged combat needing to either bite or slash the enemy. Each team has a commander that can issue orders to their troops, construct buildings and research upgrades. The game engine is built from scratch and is still being tweaked and optimized - you will need a beefy computer to play comfortably. If you are looking for something different then the run-of-the-mill FPS team based game, I highly recommend checking out this game.

Yargis: Space melee is the debut title from Plazsoft. It is a top down Space action title.
*I was given this copy for review purposes*
Graphics
The Graphics in Yargis are Great for the feel of the game.  Brilliant explosions, beautifully drawn planets, and cratered asteroids.  Overall I was impressed with the graphics in Yargis.  8/10
Sound
The music has a nice “space theme” to it.  Explosions, lasers, missiles, all sorts of weaponry sound great and fit the game brilliantly. The sound in Yargis is top notch and it shows the developer has put alot into it.  Overall I was impressed with the sound in Yargis.   8/10
Overall Gaming Experience
Yargis missions mode are varied and done well.  Dogfighting being my particular favorite.  Racing not so much.  The controls are a bit hard to get used to as it feels like you are on oil.  The controls make the racing levels a bit harder for me as you bounce off the walls.  The boundaries are a little hard to spot sometimes on some levels.  The Multi player includes Capture the flag, deathmatch, and last man standing to name a few.  There are plenty of multiplayer choices.  However the player base is very low.  Single player however will keep you busy for hours with its varied modes as well.  Overall I was im pressed with Yargis and rate it a 7/10.  Wait for a sale though the price tag is a bit steep.

Hotline Miami is a top-down hack/slash mess of blood and plot. Its not a long game, its good for the price it has, and it has a good amount of replayability since different masks give different abilities and such. It's got a unique art style and theme to it that got me invested immediately, and I decided to sit through the game in one sitting because of it. There's a lot of good things to say about this title, but that doesn't mean there aren't bad things.
Its pretty challenging, and I love a challenge, but sometimes it felt as if the AI behaved unreasonably fast (ie, shooting at you the millisecond a door opens) or sometimes through walls. Besides that, I'd say its right where it should be for price, length, and playability, and its worth picking up if you're looking for something to sit through and experience.

A lot of people might disagree with me on this review, but I think this game is awesome. For many games, I would agree that when the same game mechanics are used in the sequel, it usually means that the developers were lazy and couldn't be bothered to polish it. For SoW, I think it works. The developers have taken the original gameplay, and managed to build on it. There are more skills and more opportunities. They have taken the core gameplay and improved.
It really pisses me off that people are complaining about the microtransactions. There is no reason to buy them, and there is no part in the story where they are necessary.
Personally, I think they did a brilliant job with the grinding in this game. So far, I haven't gotten bored from grinding (and I'm in Act IV, the grindiest act of the game).
The story in this game is a huge improvement from the first one. There are multiple quest lines, and the characters managed to grow on me (especially Bruz). I thoroughly enjoyed the questlines (although the Spirit Of Carnan quests were a little tedious) and when the ending came around,
It made me emotionally attached to the characters through good character development and great story development.
All in all, I think this game is brilliant. I think the nemesis system is brilliant, I think the story is brilliant, and I think the gameplay is brilliant.
I am very happy to recommend this game, and hope that others enjoy it like I have.

Pros:
- nemesis system is back and it's better than ever
- game runs well (at least on my system) and has an optional high-res texture pack
- the combat feels visceral and meaty, the brutality of kills is incredibly satisfying
- story while not great has some interesting turns
Cons:
- microtransactions in a full-price single player game
- gets samey around the 20h mark, most of the interesting bits are front-loaded
- the 'true' ending is locked behind a massive grind, probably to promote microtransactions
- lacks depth I'd expect from a sequel - the nemesis system, while being by far the best bit here, is just a slightly upgraded version of itself from the first game
- unskippable cutscenes of orks speaking to the PC - not a huge issue, but there really isn't any reason why they aren't
- much like Shadow of Mordor plays loose with the source material, Tolkien purists will suffer
In summary:
A mediocre game with an amazing system in it, I have to wonder how it would look and feel without the publishers' greed written all over it. I've had a decent amount of fun with it, but I can't recommend it, mostly becuase I'm disinclined to grind for another 10-20h to reach the end.

But then again folks, maybe if the story turns out to be a dissapointment too, this rate could change too... Mountain, a brilliant game of unprecedented architecture. The game is widely known as a so-called "Mountain Simulator," but it is so much more. I remember the day like it was yesterday, my wife had left me and I had nothing but a dollar, a laptop, and my Steam account. I drank so much back then, shot after shot, it did nothing. While drunk, I pulled out my phone and bought this game which is called Mountain. Once sober, I opened my computer to see that I used my last dollar to buy a stupid game. I was ashamed, this led to more drinking. It eventually led to more than the hard liquor. I stole Cocaine, Valium, and Vicodin. I was addicted. I didn't know what to do. I finally opened Mountain after a long line of Coke. Then it hit me. The game was speaking to me. Not literally, but almost telepathically. After a couple of weeks, I sobered up nicely, got a job, and finally lived in a place that I could call home. I owe everything to Mountain. I give it 0/5

Its very much a spiritual sequel to class Fallout games people might better know than the original Wasteland its self.
You can create 4 party memebers(also able to recruit upto two more as the story progresses) stats are all important and in a way you want to have every skill in your six man party as you loose out a lot missing any. Story is engaging but slow as you can do alot out side/along side the story and it is of the classic grand scale of the best isometric RPGs but that is an issue for some. It has Honey Badgers but they are unrealistic in so far as being killable, so a small mark up and down there.
Now i'm over the twenty hour mark i'm still enjoying it, trying to do everything and find some treads from a robot to bust open a bunker, the lack of stealth to correctly setup an ambush exactly as i want is tough some times, but outside of that complaint game play is balanced and intresting. My knife weilding mexican is effective in meele while my assault rifle weilding Ms Deth may be higher damage the ammo she chews through can be a little short at times this balance feels just about right.
All in all a good rounded RPG that'll probally take 40-60 hours by the end with maybe a second play through, recomended for man, Badger or Robot.

Yargis is a 2D space shooter with short playeble missions that you can play online and offline (right now there are not enogh peaple to play it online but you can co op with a friend)
Level design:
There are a lot of deferent level design's like capture the cows that are floating in space (I know a bit wierd), Find the planets and scan them, Maze, Race, Protect the planet, Survive the attack and much more.
Gameplay:
As i said before, You get a lot of deferent levels to play, Some of them are more fun then others but overall they are mostlly well desinged and fun to play.
Some of the levels in the game require you to play online or in co-op as there are too hard to pass alone.
You can upgrade the ship with a veriaty of wepons that you unlock throu the game by leveling up, The amount of mony you get at each level is really low and not well balanced with the cost of the upgrads so you will need to replay some levels to get more xp and money to buy that usefull shiled and cannon.
Right now the online play is a no go as there are not enogh players there but co-op is a fun option that works with no lag or problem.
Graphic:
The graphics are good for this kind of game with not so many options to change them. The bordars of the map are hard to spot and you bounce off uncontrolebly off them.
Playebillity:
When it came out it was unplayeble, But after a short talk with the devs they fixed the way the ship moves, The fixe came within a day and now it's much more playable and fun, There are still problems with the sliding and controller scham but it is menegable.
The game gets more problematic if you mount more then one wepon, To use the second wepon you press the powerup button and it canceld eachother out and it will randomly activates the buffs you collect.
Overall it's a fun little game that you can play with friends but at that price point I would wait for it to go on sell.

Edit: I put this game down a year later due to some design decisions and frustrating optimization issues. Overall, I still recommend this game, but see below if you plan to play this game long term.
Unlike most games, NS2 is a game where performance WILL affect your gaming experience. The pseudo-client-side hitreg means that if you have low FPS or stutters, you WILL be shot behind walls and miss point blank bites or swipes. While this is not much of an issue at the beginning since you will die a lot anyways, it is very frustrating as you become better because graphically you can still see your shots cause blood splatters and cursor turn red, but realistically you are the one that ends up dead. The performance has improved throughout patches, but as of May 2013 when I quit, you really need a 4.3ghz+ Sandy Bridge to stay above 50fps at all times according to UWE Fraps thread. I have a 4ghz i7-920 and dips down to 20 late game on a 24p server. This game follows the vein of old school twitchy shooters, so fps drops will affect you much more than modern shooters such as BF or CoD.
The second and the most important reason that turned me away from the game is some of the questionable balance and design decisions floating around ever since release and especially after Flayra, the lead designer, stopped working on the title. As you may know, this is a RTS/FPS hybrid. When this game first came out, Khaara, the aliens, had a competitive edge in 6v6 due to what I would call a metagame flaw, aka "the RTS part." In contrast to NS1, they added a commander (Khamm) to the aliens side but didn't really give the Khamm much to do. Sure, you can use drifter units to scout out the place and had to place cysts and structures to spread out the creep (as opposed to marine comm requiring his teammates to build structures), but the structures grew themselves. So Khamm was really in a half baked position where you are only required to jump in once every minutes or so. This created a scenario where the marines were playing man down on the field a lot of times early game in 6v6 comp play.
Instead of fixing the metagame, UWE decided to keep buffing individual marine abilities in order to achieve even winrate. This may have been fine for comp play (though still bad design IMO), but it turned pub play into a complete stompfest in a lot of scenarios. For the longest time, there was no counter to marine shotguns; by the time you get to units that can counter it, marines had Jetpack+Shotguns which truly had no counters for the longest time. The addition of railgun is just icing on the cake.  Even though the winrate is quite balanced during this time, many alien wins came from early rushes or tenacious pushes resulting in horrible, horrible K/D.
Finally realizing the error in their balancing approach, UWE set out to make a series of experiemental changes to remedy this situation, one of which drove me away from the game. In addition to getting an overhaul to the building and tech prerequisites, they made some changes to the fade, an alien lifeform, which can only be called overpowered. The old fade used to employ this technique called double jumping after shadow step to gain you incredible forward moving momentem. You get blink later on which allows you to teleport around to chase down jetpacks. Extensive use of Blink however burns down your stamina very quickly. UWE decided to not only make blink the default fade ability, but they made the speed gain you receive from blinking permenant as long as you hop around. This turned fades into an absolute monster that is able to travel around the map at max speed indefinitely.
This is when I stopped playing NS2. I love playing fade, but it really wasn't fair for the marines or the other lifeforms. Other alien lifeforms still had to deal with the overpowered marine buffs from early on in the game, and marines now have to deal with this ridiculous lifeform which moves at maximum velocity pretty much at all times with a simple right click and space spam.
This turned out to be more or less a rant but I think it is important information for anyone looking into this game long term. Don't get me wrong, this game has a lot of allure at a glance and is indeed very enjoyable as long as you don't take it seriously. This is alien versus marine done right. You will get very intense firefights that plays out like no other FPS out there in the market. Intense small group PvP stories that you'll remember game after game. Stories of how you shut down half of the map before succumbing to the other team's tech advantage or how a coordinated surprise attack turned the game around do happen and happens very often. The RTS snowball effect does frustrate sometimes, but as long as you don't run into ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s that farms you over and over again it can be fun even while losing. The only gripe I have gameplay wise is that it was not as immersive as the original. In NS1, aliens truly jumped out at you, and playing Aliens is genuinely different experience on every level, with completely different resource structure and no commander, but I digress.
tl;dr This is the best Alien vs Marine game you will find on the market today. I would suggest to probably watch the patch notes or some youtube videos as well as watch for optimization on newest builds before dedicating to play it long term.

Alright, let me start off by saying this... Within moments it became one of my new favorite games!
I just recently bought this game, it's appearance and play style can be compared to that of Don't Starve,another game in which that i've played. This is a fairly good sized review but it's worth it if you consider to know more before you buy.
Assuming all possibilities i started it up, you start on a ship, a delivery ship in fact and play as the character Flux, someone whos appearance is like deadpools but in a goofy/ cute kind of style, and you have your robot Juicebox, who believe it or not looks like a robotic juicebox, and you're currently in progress of delivering several packages to it's destination until you are visited by this just plum like floating head alien Hewgodooko, who at first doesn't seem that bad while asking for an energy source until Flux and Juicebox tells him that its on the ship but in order to get it it would result in blowing up the ship. So he then shoots your ship with a giant laser, blows it up and takes what he needed leaving you (flux) and Juicebox to stumble off of the ship, while along your way to get off you learn basic combat knowledge and health maintance which again is similar to that of Don't Starve, but it has its own special touch to it but i'll tell you more about that in a bit.
So you make it into an escape pod and go to the planet below where you "Crashland" *nudge* *nudge* and start to explore, and that's where you learn the collecting/crafting mechanics. Very simple to do and kind of fun, you start getting neccessities to make what you need to survive i.e saws,armors, weapons, etc. All doing so with an infinite and self maintaining inventory system where it'll make crafting super easy. Now on to the enemies, the first actual creature/animal you meet is a cute donkey/cow like creature with one leg by the name of Wompit, one of the many creatures that you'll come to meet and learn about along the way with different appearances and strengths. Now combat system, again I'll relate it back to Don't Starve and how its point,click,attack but what seperates is how the enemies react to it, each creature and being has its own attack, I'll explain the wompit's; it's attack is a stomp creating a circle of splash damage to those within reach, now when an enemy attacks it'll create a blue colored highlight (circle,line,line then circle) and when it goes on the attack that path/highlight will turn red, giving you a chance to dodge that attack and deal damage at the same time which honestly takes a bit to get down especially when no two different animal species attacks are the same, so watch out!
On top of everything else there's quest's and villagers that you can help and work with and complete to get extra stuff.
For my rating of this I would flat out give it a 10/10 for at this point i've only played 5-ish hours but yet have merely scratched the surface of that which is Crashlands. I hope that my review was helpful to all those who eye gaze at this game and like me, choose to give it a shot :) you have my honest word when i say it's worth every penny, enjoy!

Too much talk, not enough death.
Shadow of war had a lot of potential, it is the sequel to the critically acclaimed game Shadow of Mordor released in 2014. Its main feature is the nemesis system which basically aims to create a unique experience to each player of the game.
Shadow of war had a lot of problems, and in this review, I will go through the ones I find to be the most important.
■ The game is very buggy
I have myself encountered a lot of game breaking bugs, I once lost a legendary Captain which I got in my preorder gold crate just randomly after I made him my bodyguard. I made a forum post about this and got a lot of response from others who experienced the same thing.
I have also lost my hard-earned levels. I went from level 49-39, and if you have played at this stage you will know that 10 levels are a lot. I do not know exactly when or how it happened but I know it happened.
There are also reports of other bugs I personally have not encountered:
■ The game is very repetitive
Each fortress is literally the same. Take point A, Take Point B, take point C, take point D and kill the warchiefs and then the overlord. THE LAYOUT IS PRETTY MUCH THE SAME ASWELL. This wouldn't have been that big of an issue if they were optional, but they aint. Stage 4 is a massive grind fest to get the "true ending" where you have to defend your fortress 20 times, and if you lose the defence you will have to recapture it.
The missions are also pretty bland. I don't even remember most of them because they were so similar.
■ The boss fights are reused and or too easy
A big enemy in shadow of war are the Nazguls, and you will be fighting them a lot during the game. The only problem is that every Nazgul fight the same... the only exceptions are the ones you will be fighting in the main campaign. They are the same but with an additional feature.
I thought that monolith explicitly said during an interview (Cannot recall where) that they had no QuickTime event bosses. But Isn't that exactly what the Balrog fight is? Yes, it’s not purely QTE but It’s pretty much there...
I played on nemesis difficulty and I rarely died during boss fights. They were way too predictable and pretty boring IMO. There were a couple of good boss fights in this game, but mainly they weren't exactly up to the standard we should expect.
■ Its still too easy
This problem lies in the combat itself. Every encounter consists of the same moves. You build up your might, you press space to vault over everyone and then you do your execution move. If the captain is immune to executions or has the adaption skill, you just do the same, but replace the execution with your arrows. Nothing is really a challenge if you only know how to counter it.
■ The story is all over the place
Personally, I never got invested in the story. I didn't really find any meaning behind Talion’s actions. During the first game there was a clear goal from the very beginning, but in Shadow of War, it was very unclear.
Probably the most annoying part for me is that it doesn't follow the lore at all. It takes way too many creative shortcuts and make too many changes that I don't even feel like its Lord of the Rings. But this might just be me, so therefore I won't make this point rule my overall score too much.
■ ♥♥♥♥ing loot boxes
Do I really need to say anything here? It’s a bloody single player game. A 60$ Single player game. Yes, I did preorder the game, and yes, I really wish I didn't. I should never have supported their greed AND I NEVER WILL AGAIN.
Shadow of war is however not all negative.
■ The nemesis system is great
There are a lot of new orc personalities to find during your game, and I do actually feel like they have improved it a lot from shadow of Mordor. You can actually create a bond between you and your orcs, or your worst enemy.
The only negative side of the nemesis system for me is that there are way too many blood brothers and way too many cheat death. This might just be my game, but it has happened quite a lot.
■ The new skill system
I really enjoyed the new skill system, it really felt like I was making my own character. Each skill has at least 2 modifiers most have 3, but you can only have 1 active at the time. This really makes you have to decide how you want to play. Do you want to go for a full on heavy attacker or do you prefer stealth?
■ The new loot system is great
I really love the loot system, mainly because I love looking good AF. Adding the whole additional collectables are pure gold for me. It really gives me a motivation to do the challenges. This combined with the skill system really makes your character your own.
The only problem with this however, is that a lot of the armours are reused. The dark set, vengeance set and the ring wraith set are all the same set with different colour palette
TLDR:
Shadow of war has way more cons than pros. Therefore I will not recommend it. Buy it on sale.

Having finished the First Act, I have to say I love this game. I'm not generally a big puzzle game player, but this one really took me in. The watercolor art style is beautiful and really made me feel like I was in a storybook. The music complements the game play well. All of the NPCs have a "soul", for lack of a better term, and feel much more like real people than NPCs in most games. The dialogue trees are also well-constructed so that they flow well and never quite feel out of place even when a few the transitions would otherwise be somewhat of a stretch during a conversation.
The main drawbacks to the game are its length and the simplicity of the puzzles. I blew through the first act in about 5 hours, which was definitely far too short. This is partially because the NPCs don't speak particularly cryptically and attempting to interact with the environment often results in your chosen character giving you solid clues about what you should be doing, which I appreciated, but may bother players looking for a tough challenge. And while there is resolution at the end of the Act, you do feel like the game finishes just at the point where it's really getting going.
This also leads into the puzzle difficulty.  For someone who doens't play a lot of puzzle games, it's nice to be eased into the logical mind frame you need to be in to play it, but the difficulty doesn't really increase over time. Part of the problem is the fact that you can play either story at any time, meaning that the developer has to take each side as though the player is starting from scratch. As a result, as I went along there were really only one or two puzzles that gave me a hard time, and some of that was because of mechanics that hadn't been introduced and, in some cases, were used only once and never again.
However, hese flaws seem minor in a game that is so well-written, well-scored, and well-voiced. Hopefully the second act will bring more difficulty and complexity,

A re-release of the dated, but loveable classic, FSX-SE will once again enchant newcomers to the genre, but may disappoint existing fans.
Do not expect shiny visuals, a modern game engine, bug-free play or anything new: this is a repackaged Flight Simulator X, sold on Steam. The one exception to that is a re-kajiggered Multiplayer system, bringing it up to the standards of convenience that the original probably should've released with. As such,
, given that it is, again, a classic game with many devotees and much attention paid to it over the years. Also because of this legacy, there are thousands of free add-ons online that can still work with this edition, in place of the scant collection of money-grabbing DLC that presently reside in the store. This game being opened up to the Steam Workshop platform would be a suitable godsend, and will likely come as soon as the DLC-money-well runs dry.
The game's price is rather interesting given that this really, really is a re-release, and it wouldn't be hard to find FSX Gold Edition sitting in the back row of a store's PC DVDROM collection for less than $10. Still, the price is not so high as to be unfair.
If you already own FSX, consider carefully whether you want this. Perhaps your flight-sim community is mainly on an FSX-SE server now - although that is unlikely, as the native multiplayer servers are not presently cross-platform with Prepar3D and X-Plane. Perhaps like me you'd rather the convenience of an automatically-repairable installation tied to an account, not a disc. I do not recommend concurrent installations of both - despite using mostly different directories, some registry entries are shared, and many add-ons are not programmed to recognise each separate installation.
If you do not own FSX, ultimately I would have to recommend the game as an educational and, if you're geeky enough, fun experience. Proceed at your own risk, as further involvement may involve countless hours of installing better or more hardcore aircraft, becoming fluent in air traffic control-ese, and looking up real-world charts with which to fly.

Wasteland 1 was out before my time.  I grew up on Fallout 1 and 2.  If you are a fan of classic Fallout, you'll feel right at home in Wasteland 2.
Character customization is very robust.  Even with a crew of 4 personalized rangers, it is hard to build a 100% comprehensive team.  The creative freedom is welcome even if I did restart my first few playthroughs because some of my rangers did not perform as well as I expected.  Without experience or research, you're likely to build sub-optimal team members.
Wasteland really shines when it comes to content.  The world has plenty of subquests and diversions to discover.  The larger quests offer numerous interconnected choices with the potential for wildly varying conclusions and rewards.  The complexity of the quest design did introduce some glitches and inconsistencies during my play throughs.  Every now and then an NPC would incorrectly acknowledge a decision I did or did not actually make earlier in my game, but it was never game breaking.
The combat will feel familiar if you've played XCOM.  The RPG aspects of combat work well.  Weapons are quite diverse even within single categories and deciding which one to use rarely boils down to a single stat.  Healing takes a significant turn investment.  Friendly fire is a consideration when shooting past teammates.  Penalties are applied to your hit rate depending on range and your choice of weapon.  Weapons and ammo get progressively heavier and inventory management becomes progressively more important.  There is surprising variety in enemy archetypes.  All these factors add up to a thoughtful combat system, but it is not without its flaws.  The worst of Wasteland 2's combat can be attrbuted to poor level design.  Combat operates on a grid, but the levels are often built without this in mind.  A diagonal wall is suddenly a much bigger obstacle than it first seemed.  The game does have a cover system that comes highly encouraged, but there are no clear visual rules for what you can and can't use for cover.  Environmental interactivity was supposed to be a big deal and was emphasized during gameplay trailers.  There are destructable crates peppered in most combat scenarios, but that's largely the extent of the dynamic environments.  I don't remember seeing an explosive barrel/pod beyond the first mission.
Overall, Wasteland 2 is a faithful modernization of its source material and there's plenty here to keep you coming back long after the credits roll.

First of all, don't be fooled by the cool cinematics, this game is abysmally different, it's like the devs hired an animation studio to do the cinematics and showed them none of the gameplay. This game is an average hack and slash, a Diablo 2 clone that's anything but memorable although it still manages to be fun if you don't set your standard to Diablo 3 kind of quality. You will beat it in about 5-6h and I don't think it's worth $20 (more like $5-8 IMHO) but if you're a fan of the genre or want a pretty simple hack and slash then you will have fun with the game as you progress.
The game lets you chose between 3 classes: melee warrior, ranged archer or mixed mage. So once I completed the game as a melee warrior I did play it as the other 2 classes and had my fair share of fun with it. A downside are the way the achievements are managed since if you beat the game on a hard difficulty you don't get the previous achievements as if you beat it on the easier difficulties, also there's an achievement for the First Boss that YOU WILL NEVER GET because the dev has stated that they have decided to permanently remove this boss, so bummer there for all the achievement ♥♥♥♥♥s around the world (such as myself).

You hack through a variety of enemies with melee, ranged and magic weapons (you can equip up to 2 at a time) and use mana on your magic powers (you can equip up to 4 at a time, also can invest on passive abilities too). As you level up you can spend some points on improving your character and making it more oriented to melee, ranged and magic to suit your preferences; each avatar is purely cosmetic since you can make your barbarian a warlock, turn the bow girl into a warrior princess or your mystic into a deadly marksman. This game has very simple mechanics and this may give you a good time if you're looking for a beat 'em up with some light mechanics.

Visually this game isn't on par with other games of the genre, that's OK by me although it makes a little bothersome to pay full price for a game that isn't remarkable on gameplay or story either, but we shouldn't be so hard on the game visuals since they aren't THAT bad either as some people have said. The loading screens and cinematics present some nice visual art but you NEVER see those characters ingame, nor you see the armors and weapons depicted in them, which is why I start the review by telling that the developers most likely hired a separate studio for the art that they display.
To be honest the story is just a nonsensical filler, I was really excited after seeing the opening cinematic but then found a pretty bland and uninspired story, quite confusing since I can't even remember the name of the character you are supposed to be playing, at some point I stopped trying to make any sense and thought that characters call you different names on each level as if you are just supposed to represent a different mythological persian character. So yeah... forget about getting an engaging story from this game.
The sounds are ok and the music isn't bad either, I can't complain nor praise the game's musical score, all I can say is that I wasn't bothered by it but wasn't lost in it either.

Life is Strange strips most of the game away to focus on its characters and its narrative, and as a result it does these things so incredibly well. While some characters serve as generalisations of certain groups - geeks, jocks, hipsters, etc. - each of the games characters have amazing depth.
Max is lovable and her development into a strong person following her experiences is heartwarming. Each character minor or major has clearly defined personalities and each of thier actions are justified through a set of airtight characteristics, insofar as I never once said 'this character is unrealistic/no-one would ever do that.' One of the best characterised characters in gaming in my opinion is David, the ex-soldier who we see struggle with coming back to reality, and I as the player went from hating him to loving him so gradually that I didn't notice until it hit me like a frieght train. The fact that the extreme opposite is true for
characters stands as a testiment to this game's excellent characterisation.
Each major decision feels emotionally meaningful even on the rare occasion that they don't matter to the plot. As a result of these decisions Max grows as a person, as I felt myself growing as well. And I spent five minutes looking at the last choice. The friendship and love and hate in this story all feel genuine, to the point where its difficult for me to leave Arcadia Bay behind.
This game will remain an inspiration to me going forward. Absolutely stunning.

I really enjoyed this game. It's visually beautiful, has a compelling storyline, and is overall adorable! My partner said it was like playing a lullaby.

*THE GOOD*
1.) THE ORCS. The already brilliant Nemesis System has been expanded and improved upon MASSIVELY! If you liked the Orcs in Shadow of Mordor, you'll DEFINATELY enjoy the Orcs in Shadow of War! This really is the game's strongest feature in my opinion and it affords the game tremendous replay-ability.
2.) SCALE. Shadow of War is large. Really large. It has more than double the playable areas of Shadow of Mordor, with 5 regions to explore and conquer instead of 2. Shadow of War IS bigger and, more importantly, FEELS, bigger that Shadow of Mordor.
3.) COMBAT. Like Shadow of Mordor, Shadow of War's combat system is quite reminiscent of the Batman: Arkham games but adds its own twist with the addition of the Wraith powers. This was one of Shadow of Mordor's strongest features and Shadow of War seems to improve on it. Combat seems to flow better and feels more dynamic than in Shadow of Mordor.
4.) STORYLINE. Not going to spoil anything but I'll just say that Shadow of War's storyline is awesome! The game makes it clear that Shadow of War is exactly that. War. You and Sauron are waging all-out war in Mordor and the Orcs are your soldiers. Again, not going to spoil anything, but the storyline begins and ends with a BANG. Dynamic characters and strong personalities clashing with one another makes the game's campaign a real blast to experience!
5.) LINKS TO SHADOW OF MORDOR. Shadow of War has a number of rather ingeneous call-backs to Shadow of Mordor that makes it feel like a true sequel while, at the same time, not making you feel as if you've missed-out if you haven't played the first game. For example, early-on in Shadow of War, if you've played Shadow of Mordor's Nemesis Forge mode (and I encourage you to do so BEFORE starting Shadow of War), you'll be confronted by your greatest nemesis from Shadow of Mordor who'll act as the game's first boss. for me, my nemesis was particularly dangerous and, while I found all the bosses challenging, he was by far the hardest to overcome during my playthrough. You'll also meet your greatest follower from Shadow of Mordor and enjoy a few nice little cameos from some of Shadow of Mordor's side-characters that makes the game feel like a continuation of Shadow of Mordor but also it's own self-contained narrative. You don't have to play Shadow of Mordor to understand the plot but you may not experience some of the little call-backs in the Nemesis System if you don't.
6.) AESTHETICS (THE SIGHTS AND SOUNDS). Shadow of Mordor was a good looking game. It looked good and sounded good. Shadow of War is that amped waaaaaay up. If you have a good machine and can risk cranking Shadow of War up to high or ultra, do it because it looks fan-freaking-tastic. Lots of people don't point it out either but Shadow of War SOUNDS great too. The soundtrack is great and so are the sound effects. The flame breath on the drakes is especially awesome! The game sounds crisper, clearer, grittier, and more 'alive' than Shadow of Mordor and this is another of it's strongest points. However, if your machine isn't a total beast, don't be intimidated since Shadow of War still looks good at medium and low. You'll still experience the awesome sounds, though. I HIGHLY recommend playing Shadow of War's cutscenes with a good pair of headphones or earbuds on because it's absolutely fantastic!
*THE BAD*
1.) MICRO-TRANSACTIONS. Everyone brings it up but it's true that Shadow of War's 'Marketplace' feels quite hand-fisted in. At times, the game will FEEL as if it's subtly encouraging you to buy into the loot boxes and it CAN get to you if you're the kind of person that is ardently against these kinds of things in games. Honestly, though, it's NOT AS BAD AS PEOPLE SAY! The Loot Boxes ARE ♥♥♥♥♥♥ and they shouldn't have been in the game...BUT...they AREN'T the worst thing ever and you likely WON'T be absolutely outraged by them. It's definately a negative point but I feel most people are blowing it way out of proportion.
2.) TUTORIAL. Now, this MIGHT just be me being bad at the game or misunderstanding it or just being dense but I'm going to put it in here anyways. I found the tutorial in Shadow of War to be...limited. Does it teach you the fundamentals of the game and its core concepts? Yes it does and it does so aptly. BUT. Shadow of War does not seem to introduce you to the more subtle gameplay concepts that are continued from Shadow of Mordor. Now, it might be because of my playtime in Shadow of Mordor being detected by the game or I may have missed the prompts but, for me, it feels as if Shadow of War expects you to already be familiar with things like Brutalize, Shadow Strike, Wraith Stun, Shadow Mount, Vaulting, and Detonations.
3.) SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS AND/OR BUGS. Now, I haven't experienced any of the crashes, game-breaking bugs, or other problems many have reported. In fact, my experience with Shadow of War, from a technical standpoint, has been overwhelmingly positive and I have absolutely no problems running the game on my machine even for long periods of time. That being said. Instances of frequent crashes, audio glitches, and game-breaking bugs HAVE been reported by some individuals in reviews and on the Steam Discussion page and while I have NOT encountered any of these issues, it is wise to agknowlege that they do seem to exist for some people. The game also seems to have fairly high graphical requirements and, while the game does look very nice, it may be a challenge for lower-end systems to run it. If you had issues running Shadow of Mordor at a reliable 60ish FPS, please be cautious about buying Shadow of War because it is more demanding of your machine. Keep the Steam Refund Policy in-mind if this is a concern for you because that's what it's there for.
Overall, Shadow of War is a great game, in my opinion. While I understand all the outrage over micro-transactions, Loot Boxes, and the Forthog debacle and I believe all of that is terrible and shouldn't have been in the game to begin with, I didn't find them all that disruptive. I'm about 40 hours in and I haven't spend any of my money on anything and I don't feel that I'm gimped or any less powerful for it. You CAN spend Mirian, in-game currency you earn from doing pretty much anything, on so-called 'Silver Loot Boxes' which give Orcs, equipment, and certain boosts and bonuses. They're very convenient if you're pressed for time or just can't be bothered to train-up that one particular class of Orc you need but they are, BY NO MEANS, necessary. You can get by quite well without even entering the Marketplace at all and you won't feel any less powerful. At times, the game DOES feel like it's 'grindiness' is pressuring you into shelling-out for Loot Boxes (which, I'm sure, was deliberate by WB) but if you keep at it you'll find that it really isn't as bad as lots of people make it out to be. A strongly good game with overlookable flaws.

Alan Wake is a great mixture of both storytelling and action horror. You'll feel as if you're in a Stephen King novel with pistol in one hand and a pen in the other, and that's the point. Alan Wake, the protagonist of this story admits several times he was inspired by Stephen King. In a truely bizarre mix of story telling, Alan Wake is everything. He is your narrator, your hero and your player character. He is you trying to survive in a story taken over by unknown forces which use a strong control over the darkness to grow ever stronger and remove you from it's sinister and cruel plan.
With nothing to stop you from being swallowed into a violent, angry and endless void you must run until you can find a means to protect yourself from a world being torn apart in the black of night. Nothing can help you and nothing will help you, except for the light. Dawning a flashlight and the knowledge of how to finally fight back, you become the champion of light. You begin to shape destiny again. You become a hero.
With your new found power and in a desperate race against time, you must find your wife who was inexplicably swallowed by the darkness. You must convince yourself that you're of sane mind, when everyone else is trying to convince you otherwise. You're a hero, who will fight endless legions of the Taken inorder to reclaim the one you love and care for the most. The only question though, is how?
I've found out the answer to this over five times on Xbox 360. Yes, the story is that good. Yes, maybe I should play something else. Yes, yes and yes. Get this game.
