Let me tell you the tale of "Pushkrimp", a lowly grunt that got lucky one fine Mordor day. About how, in the chaos of battle with a undead Ranger, he managed to land the fatal blow. From that day on, he became known as "Pushkrimp Tark Slayer". He was a ferocious Orc, weilding far more damage output than most, a berserker with a gaggle of savages following him around after he murdered his old captain. He was angry at the world for not recognizing his greatness, and he never gave his foes a second chance, if they even got so lucky.
Pushkrimp became the focus of one particular undead Ranger, the lucky blow not going forgotten. So an ambush was arranged to have him assassinated for his insolence. Pushkrimp laughed at the pathetically underprepared Ranger and his crew. Murdering the Rangers thralls quickly, before killing the Ranger in a single blow. A sign of things to come. Now... Pushkrimp had the Ranger in his sights...
For the next few days, Pushkrimp would lie in wait and ambush the Ranger, mercilessly murdering him again and again with his savage blows and inpenetrable armor. Twice, he suceeded in killing the Ranger, and twice the Ranger fled in horror as Pushkrimp gained more power than even the Ranger wielded. But the Orcs savage reign of terror was not to last forever... or was it?
Amonst fiery pits, the very war machine which Pushkrimp guarded, he again ambushed the weary Ranger. An epic battle ensued that climbed the heights of the scaffoding and confused orc workers. Above the pits, Pushkrimp and the Ranger did glorious battle one more time. Clashing and dodging the Orcs vicious blows, the Ranger stabbed where he could, keeping his distance despite his arrows being useless (even though Pushkrimps sole flaw was ranged attacks). Near death, Pushkrimp raged at his fall from flawless victories, and quickly began recovering health, wildly swinging his one-hit-kill axes at the Ranger. His fury was his mistake.
Near death, enraged, and too close to the edge of a bridge, the Ranger saw his moment, his chance at victory. He drop kicked Pushkrimp from the bridge, breathing a sigh of releif as the Orc that caused him no end of suffering plummet to his doom into a pit filled with lava. The Ranger fired arrows into the screaming Orc as he burst into flames, just to be sure the meance was gone forever. It wasn't until the screams died away that the Ranger felt safe again, the top predator in Mordor.
Leaving the fields of lava, the Ranger plotted his next move. Who was to become his new thrall, how he would conquer the looming fortress... then a axe whizzes past his head! Ambush! There... his armor and hair burned away, skin melted, and body charred... stood Pushkrimp! He challenges the Ranger, chastising him for his confidence, before raising his axes declaring he has become "Pushkrimp the Flame of War" as they burst into flames. The Orc cackles maniaclly as he twirls his flaming weapons, the Ranger terrified.
The undying Orc rushes the Ranger, another epic battle ensues, but no lava pits to unexpectedly lend assistance. The Flame of War demonstrates his newfound strength in rapid regeneration as well as enhanced resistances. He has become a true monster, enraged, unkillable, and very lethal. He tackles the evasive Ranger in a fury, and caves his head in with his bare fists. The Ranger dies again, and terrified of the monster lurking in that region, flees to another.
Time passes, the Ranger grows in power, all while avoiding the hunting grounds of the Flame of War. Soon, the Ranger feels he is strong enough at last to defeat the now surely weaker Orc that gave him trouble so long ago. He returns... to desolation...
The captains that once swarmed around the fortress: dead. The Warcheifs that served the Overlord: dead. It was as though the Ranger need not invade the empty land at all... save one Orc standing fiercly at the top of the fortress... There, in command of the land of death, stood... PUSHKRIMP!!! The new lands Overlord had mounted a staggering one Orc assault on the fortress, annihilating all in his path. Worse, forged in war, The Flame had gained still more power than the Ranger by a wide margin. Facing him would surely mean death.
Nevertheless, the fortress defences down, the Ranger trained until he matched the Orc in strength... theoretically at least. Pushkrimp had made the fortress his home, stringing up his old commanders as decorations for his walls. His strength was on full display. He had no need of Warchiefs, so he assigned none even as the Ranger assembled his armies and mustered his power.
The assault on the fortress came as planned, the walls falling quickly, but none of that was the true challenge. Pushing open the metal doors of the keep, the brutality of The Flame was on full display, his piles of bones, and traitors of particular note hung from the walls. There... upon a throne of skulls sat The Flame. He welcomed the Ranger, thanked him for giving him the confidence to rise through the ranks. Then, he asked for one more favor: that the Ranger die once again to solidify his place as top Orc. The cordality of the meeting distracting from the horrific scene the Orc chose for himself.
They clashed, the lesser minions meaning little as they fell quickly from the sparks flying between the two old rivals, none could stand between them. The Flame himself rend his minions if they interfered, their assistance more interference. The battle ascended the steps to the throne, and the duo clashed before the throne of bones long after any battle should last, the Ranger forced to avoid any blow from the wicked fiery axes. Then... the Ranger fell, Pushkrimp catching him on a backswing.
All was lost, The Flame was too strong. Mordor would forever be strangled under his shadow. The game would end. Then, a ray of light as one of the Rangers loyal commanders tackled The Flame before he could land the killing blow. The battle resumed, the weakened Ranger trying his best to protect his friend. "No! He's too strong for you! Retreat!" the Ranger wanted to yell, but he knew his ally was the sole bulwark between him and death. Still, death came. And again, an ally saved the Ranger. So it went, three more times, until the Five Ranger Commanders and the Ranger himself stood before The Flame in glorious battle.
Still, sorrow filled the ensuing melee. The entirely competant fighting force crashed against Pushkrimp like angry waves against a seawall. The furious Orc ducked and dodged, struk and withdrew with the finesse of a seasoned warrior, his health wildly swinging between full and none. Then... the Rangers allies began to fall, one by one. First was the brute Oolog the Ranger relied on as his shield. Then, his archer commander fell. Then his frontline commander lost his head to a flurry of blows... it was looking grim as the unnatural Orc Overlord slew all the Ranger had arrayed against him.
Finally, the Rangers last two allies, another berserker and a heavily armored defender, did the unthinkable. While the berserker at long last broke The Flames will, the Defender threw himself in front of a ferocious spinning assault that would have surely killed the Ranger. Mogzu One-eye... we will never forget your sacrifice. In that moment, The Flame grinned a wicked grin and mocked the Ranger for his weak allies. Even with a price-tag of only $1 I cannot recommend this game. Actually, I don't even think i could even call it a game at all. Calling it a game would suggest some sort of gameplay, some sort of meaningful interaction, something to do... all things this "game" almost entirely lacks. 99% of this "game" consists of just staring at a floating mountain as it slowly rotates. Yeah, that's it. It's about as interesting as it sounds. I've seen a lot of people praising this game as something innovative or something that challenges what a game is. Don't get me wrong, there are some games out there that are doing just that... this is not one of them.
The game starts with you being given a vague subject and you draw out a little picture based on that. As far as I know it goes into seeding the RNG that creates the mountain. It doesn't really matter what you draw but it's probably the most interesting part of the game. After that you are shown your mountain. It just sits there slowly spinning as it changes from day to night and the seasons change. Every little bit some text will pop up and once in a great while some random object will land on you mountain. All you can do is wait, you can zoom in and out or rotate the mountain, you can play musical notes with the keyboard, and you can pick up the objects and drop them back down on the mountain. That's about all there is to it. Sounds like a lot of fun, eh?
Mountain might be somewhat redeemed if it actually looked good. If the graphics were even decent it might make a good screen saver but sadly they are not. The graphics are poor and I have problems with textures flickering and such. It's just not that pretty to look at. The dev also recommends that it's something to leave running while you do other things but it's so poorly optimized that it uses much more resources that in should for what it is... So much more that some people have suggested that it could be a Bitcoin miner in disguise, lol. There's no reason to believe that but the fact is that it's a bit heavy for something that's meant to be running it the background.
If you are looking for something to blow a dollar on there are definitely better things you could get.

Gameplay: Top-Down Shooter that takes place in 1989. Pixelated too makes it kinda cool. You play as Jacket, who kills the Russian mobsters. You can either eliminate them one by one, or go shoot everything up, which is faster-paced and chances of dying are much more.
In Hotline Miami, It's more about surprising your enemies and stuff. The gameplay is fun, yet challenging. It took me about 6 hours to beat the game, yet after I beat it, it's still a fun game to replay.
Soundtrack: OMG the music is addicting. The style gives the game more feel when you play it. What I like is that when you die, the music never gets interrupted. The only time it gets interrupted is when you face a boss (which goes to another soundtrack), get to a cutscene, or complete a map.
Difficulty: The game can be pretty difficult at sometimes, You will die with one swing or a gunshot. However, there are different masks in the games that give you abilities. I challenge you complete it with the standard Richard mask tho haha. Once you get used to the game, you can beat it easier with strategy.
Replay Value: I've played it over again a few times now and then when I run outta games to play. The good thing is you can jump around chapters after you beat teh game. I just pick a random chapter and continue the massacre. ;3
What I liked:
Gameplay,
Replay Value,
The action can keep you on your feet.
Difficulty makes you want to keep trying to beat the game.
What I didn't like:
Sometimes I didn't spot enemies and a random gunshot comes out of nowhere and gives me a jumpscare.
Difficulty can make me frustrated sometimes.
Bosses can be frustrating.
Story can be a bit confusing.
My final thoughts:
Hotline Miami is a really fun game that keeps you on your feet when you do missions. Soundtrack is amazing, Gameplay can be either fast pace shoot up, or eliminate one by one. Ultimately, I think this game has great replay value, although it can be frustrating at times. I would give the game a 9.5/10.

It is difficult to review a game that is only half-finished, but since there is currently no set date for Act II to be released, I suppose there's no harm in at least trying. Lets start with the cons, in order to get them out of the way, shall we? Possibly the most obvious, is the lack of an ending. While I understand the financial issues this title ended up facing, and I can appreciate how the developers decided to solve it, I'm still left feeling a little let down after realizing I would have to wait an undetermined amount of time before seeing a conclusion to this story.
Indeed the story is wonderful, very well told and beautifully written, it simply lacks an ending. Act I is long enough to provide an enjoyable gaming experience, though at times the puzzles can be a bit simplistic. The action is primarily point and click, and puzzles revolve around finding objects to use with others in order to progress the characters. The characters themselves are wonderfully constructed an developed, as is their environment. The humor is witty at times, and a bit dry at others, but the writing holds up in general.
I've heard many comparisons of this game to Monkey Island, however I wouldn't go so far as to agree with them (at least not until this one is finished). That being said, this title is still wonderfully constructed, and I do recommend it to those who are fans of puzzle games with linear stories and emotional rides. Especially if said fans are just slightly more interested in the story side than the puzzle side.
The artwork is as equally impressive as the character development, and makes the game fun to simply look at. The soundtrack is fully orchestral and fits the game very well, helping to augment all the appropriate cutscenes. Character dialogue is provided by an array of very talented voice actors, each offering their stylistic abilities to their characters. This, in turn, creates a wonderful cast of characters for the player to interact with.
All in all, this is a great game...so far. I really hope to hear about the release of the second act soon, but that is unfortunately not something I can recommend paying $25 for. Still, I suggest picking up this title as a daily deal or something. Certainly wouldn't promote the idea of paying more than $10. At least at this stage of development. Perhaps once the second half of the game is released, and it is given a proper ending, it will warrant the higher price tag. As is, however, it falls a bit short of that mark.

This is an intriguing game. You play as Alan Wake, a best-selling author and the main protagonist in a story straight from the imaginings of a horror novel. It's dark, suspenseful and engaging; most of the action takes place at night, with a bias towards shadowy atmospherics and a distinct contrast between light and dark. It breaks "good" and "evil" down to the most basic concept of "light" being "good" and "darkness" being "evil"; the darkness is your enemy and it brings dangers that will kill you, while light usually represents a safe haven. Your greatest weapon is usually your torch (closely followed by a revolver, rifle or shotgun!) - flares and flashbangs are also put to creative use.
The gameplay is relatively simple, being story-led and therefore fairly linear. There is not much scope for exploration/deviation from the given path, but the storyline is immersive enough that it keeps you interested. There are many hidden items to be found throughout the game, though there is not much in the way of problem solivng. Combat is straightforward enough; an interesting concept is having to "burn" the darkness out of an attacker using a torch or light source before using your gun to kill what is left. The weapon selection is very limited, but realistic as the whole game is set within the small mountain town of Bright Falls.
This game stands on its atmospherics. Play it at night with the lights switched off and no distractions and you'll find yourself inexorably drawn into the nightmare Alan Wake finds himself stranded in. Is he crazy or is this stuff real? Sometimes it is hard to tell and you find yourself constantly questioning what is going on. It can be tense, creepy and dreamlike, all at the same time. The story becomes more and more involved the further you get into it, but this does mean that, at times, it gets convoluted or downright confusing. The ending doesn't make a whole lot of sense to be honest, but I'll give the game the benefit of the doubt and say that it probably helps to play it through a second time as it may make more sense when you've fully grasped the concepts of the game.
This game is all about story and atmosphere. There is little in the way of puzzle solving, nor is the combat particularly challenging. There are no "big boss" type fights that can't be beaten easily in the same manner as regular foes. I played it through to the end, and while I enjoyed the game, I was left feeling slightly dissatisfied as it didn't feel like everything had been properly concluded. That may be intentional but it leaves you feeling a little short, with unresolved questions. It was an enjoyable play, however, an easy game to get to grips with and an interesting, if sometimes bemusing, story. This game is one of my favorite's when it comes to story and voice acting. It's interesting, intense, has an amazing sense of humor, and some of the best side characters of all time. Natural Selection 2 combines First-Person Shooter with Real-Time Strategy to create a game that offers a truly unique experience.
[What is it?]
NS2 let's you play from a top-down view as the team's Commander or through the first-person perspective, like a shooter. The game offers two unique sides, the Frontiersmen(Marines) versus the Kharaa(Aliens) which play vastly different.
[Gameplay]
Consisting of territorial control, in which both teams rally to take strategic locations, for resources which allow access to upgrades and special abilities through the Commander's research for the other players. The goal? Eliminate the opposing team by any means necessary.
[But is it worth it?]
NS2 offers a truly fun, rewarding experience that takes communication and teamwork in order to achieve victory. Whether you're playing as a Marine with a jetpack or mech battle-armor, or the flying and teleporting Aliens. I cannot recommend it enough!

9)Different planets have different gravity and amount of atmosphere, prepare for this as well as planets moving and closing transfer windows
10)Use the CoM(Center of Mass), CoL(Center of Lift), and CoT(Center of Thrust) tools

12)Jet engines only work in an atmosphere

Played the demo years ago, and ever since I checked on this game every few weeks. So after my preorder unlocked, Ive been busy playing it on my laptop while on vacation. Yes im sitting here, playing ST while fishing and  what not. Im aware some of those items have been addressed already, however im listing them as they are present in my game currently. So they are all valid.

The good stuff:

- physics are good, if a bit overdone at times. Notice  the insane bending of truck frames, particularly the trailers
- game runs great, even on my IBM laptop which has graphics akin to a pancake. It looks great on low settings too.
- 5 maps to start us off with
- Terrain response is the best ive seen. Terrain memory is impressive.
- proper offroad sim!
- moddable
- great community support
- hasn't crashed yet. so that's good. then again, tech demo also never crashed. hooray for crash free games!

The bad stuff that needs fixed asap, because once the novelty wears off, many will start noticing all this:
- Vehicle choices are very limited. Even the vehicles included are not licensed. Which is ok, but since they didn't license them, more could have been included. No lada niva copy? Come on.
- The maps are biased towards big rigs. car/truck based 4x4 will struggle with just about every turn on most maps. the demo map was rather forgiving. the game maps are not. bypasses are irrational and don't afford smaller vehicles any advantage. Most are dead ends anyway.
- The camera.. I cannot express the frustration the camera system brings me. I spend more time trying to see stuff than driving. a lot has been said about it already, why it wasn't fixed prior to release, i'll leave this to your imagination. It feels way worse than in tech demo.
- The lack of a minimap in the interface (like in GTA). The compass is useless. No it doesn't increase the challenge. It just creates frustration. Replace compass with minimap. I don't want to constantly have to stop what im doing, press F1 and then spend some time trying to rotate the main map to figure out if I should take a left or right.
- Wheel autocenter must be an option. Wheel turn rate (responsiveness) must be an option. Given this is keyboard only game, devs should be ashamed at the lack of control config options. This is the main reason vehicles act wonky at any speed. Wheels turn too slow, then they tend to stick in a position. This results in vehicles drifting. Nice simulation of drunk ivan behind the wheel, but im not ivan...
- I want the ability to freeze time like in the demo. I don't want constant and annoying day/night cycles. Couple this with the camera, it becomes annoying stacked atop annoying. 1 minute an hour is also annoying. It also removes your free will. The game forces some pointless clock on you. why? We get it, it can go from dark to light. Now let us chose when we want to play!
- Damage is too random and lacks common sense. You take damage from the oddest things, and don't from the most obvious ones.
- Rock physics are a little goofy. Rock placement is also dubious at times. Why are there boulders in the middle of the mud with no boulders anywhere else? Where did those come from? I get it they are there to create extra challenge, but its too obvious. See what I mean? Too obvious someone was trying to stage terrain.
- cab view. both 3D modeled cabs and hood view.
- Lack of gauges/data. Speed? RPM? These are basic for any driving game since 1992, why not present in 2014?
- can only save 1 map at a time. Oh the joy!

Things it needs added eventually:
- The lack of weather and elements. not sure if engine can process weather.
- The lack of winter maps. even if not dynamic based on weather, those should be part of any game that involves Russia. because Russia isn't Hawaii............
- The game feels very pointless after a while. It needs some sort of economy to engage you beyond driving slowly over mud and stuff.
- better damage model. Wear to tires, axles, engine overheating etc.
- more truck upgrades! many more. I feel the need to mod my gear.

I've learned at least two things from Spintires: Russian off-road trucks are tough as hell, and the forestry industry is in dire need of development.
The genre of Off-road simulator is not a particularly well populated one, and so it may not say much when Spintires is easily the king of its genre. It is, however, easily the greatest and fullest representation of the thrills and muddy spills enjoyed by many an off-road enthusiast as represented in interactive media thus far.
The intricate work that went in to this game so far is worth immense praise. The mud, the rocking and buckling of the massive trucks, and the creaky bouncing of the heavy-duty suspension is all accurately portrayed in a spectacular physics engine that surpasses those of many AAA titles. Simple tasks like exploring a forest and picking up/dropping off logs are made into a game of timing and strategy. Recognzing a soggy bog in a lush field of tall grass becomes a treasured skill, and knowing just how tightly your truck can turn around on a rocky path can save you from having to drive out and recover yourself with another vehicle... And that's just the single player game! Why not bring a friend? It's always safer to wheel in numbers!
All of this is realized in sharp, immersive graphics that almost has the player smelling the pine in the air. The trucks are rendered with care and attention to detail. Obviously these guys know their Russian off-road trucks.
Again, a spectacular game well worth the money, if for nothing else than to support the creation of truly innovative and unique games by talented developers. There are some rough edges, sure. The sound effects are at times intermittent and there is plenty of clipping and visual artefacts (particularly in heavily deformed mud, which is understandable considering the collosal complexity of developing truly destructable terrain).
The team behind Spinetires should stand among the greats for the work they've done and the standard they've set. I hope this game catches on big.

The first ~2 hours of the game are pretty ♥♥♥♥ing fun, and reminiscient of the first game. Most of what I noticed was after 5-8 hours of play, at which point the issues began to compound.

I found the second world "zone" to be awkward to explore, and some areas felt incredibly lifeless and dead. I ended up backtracking through the exact same boring paths many times, and the game didn't look good enough for me to enjoy it. Sometimes the enemies say funny or interesting things as you walk around, but a lot of the time they just kind of stand there, or walk around aimlessly, in very "videogamey" fashion.

Many portions of the map feel dead or arbitrary. There are lots of awkward staircases, ledges, balconies, and just “things” in the world that don’t really make logical sense from a city planning perspective, and it becomes very noticeable at times as you are moving around. Not a huge deal, but it does get tiresome to cross a massive and boring open expanse of ground just to find some awkwardly placed buildings. Some of the orc fortresses are super ♥♥♥♥ing rad, though, so this kind of goes both ways. Some areas just feel more polished, by far, than others.

A lot of the AI seemed either completely oblivious to anything happening literally 10 feet from their face, or an archer might spot the player from 300 feet away and pelt them with perfectly accurate arrows.

The dialogue, from orc goons and captains, is the best part of the game, and it's phenomenal. I almost kept playing just to see more of the goofy lines they'd say. However you can't skip the dialogue, and some of it is rather long: I was killed by glitches/bugs 3 times in a row on one very difficult war chief guy, and I had to listen to his overtly long speech every ♥♥♥♥ing time he appeared, even if he only saw me 2 minutes ago, and I heard plenty of repeats to the point that I was just annoyed every time I saw him.

The animations are pretty good, if not excellent, and were easily one of my favorite things in the game.

A very annoying part of combat I found was that basic orcs would take 6-10 hits to kill, even with a partially upgraded sword. you can execute them by building Might, or you can execute them if you knock them down. However, enemy orcs will *always* attack you if you try to get someone on the ground, and interrupt your execution. This is understandable, however: the animation of your execution might show your dagger *through an orc's skull* and it might play the "you just carved his throat open* noise, but as soon as you are interrupted he will not only survive, but get up immediately even if he was previously writhing on the ground in pain. I found melee fights, coupled with the amount of orcs you have to kill, tedious and obnoxious because the best way to win them is to ONLY left click or counter, and never execute until you start getting lots of might (or maybe way later in the game after you've grinded all your unlocks and such). Which is a boring way to play.

The unlock system is kind of neat, but a lot of the things you get feel like they should have been freebies or just regular game mechanics. Like something that instantly picks up treasure on the ground; trying to collect the gear that orcs drop is annoying, especially when the same input to pick stuff up is used for other things, and you end up getting killed while trying to get gear because the game does the wrong thing. Combining and crafting jewels is tedious and feels like a forced method of extending gameplay and faking the sense of “progression.” There are tons of things to collect and find, none of which I found interesting or compelling, but I’m sure the lore would be more interesting for some. Though I’m of the opinion that the devs probably wanted people to buy their DLC “start boost” junk, which gives you XP and gear.

The “big cool super ability” in the game, imo, looks stupid. If I recall correctly, in the last game you got to basically stop time and go around chopping everyone in half. It was awesome, and EASILY my favorite part of the game. In this one, you stop time and start shooting arrows, kind of. It looks really awkward if you’re in melee because the animation is so quick that it doesn’t look like anything. It also doesn’t really have any cool “arrow impact” effect or trail. It’s also possible to shoot nothing by accident, or the same orc twice, so you end up spinning and mashing buttons randomly just to try and do the most damage, which doesn’t feel fun. I don’t know if you could upgrade to the older, more fun thing, but I didn’t play long enough to see anything that said you could. Also, the bar for the super ability seems to randomly disappear, even though it takes forever (15-ish minutes of play, approximately) to charge. So it seems like you’re encouraged to use it randomly and wastefully, or just lose it.

If you play with mouse and keyboard, the quicktime “deflect” prompts are ATROCIOUSLY bad at times. Mouse 4 or Mouse 5 literally just have tiny blue text that said “mouse 4” or “mouse 5” so the only difference is the single number character at the end which might also be partially covered by the game’s effects, and if you click wrong OR take too long to try and read the prompt, you do the wrong thing and die. This contributed to the majority of my deaths, and was not fun at all. There are several ways this could have been fixed or improved, too, which only makes it more annoying.

Also on the topic of controls, executing the wrong ♥♥♥♥ing orc is way too common. The game can throw several dozen enemies at you, and your character will often decide to execute the weakest or almost already dead orc instead of the adjacent, nearly dead captain who you’ve been hunting and wailing on. You lose might from any injury, and earning it is a pain, so this can get you killed and it’s not fun. I’ve also had issues with “attacking air” where the character will swing or grab literally nothing, only to be shot to death by an adjacent archer. This is beyond frustrating.

My biggest problem with the game is twofold. One, getting stuck on random damn ledges and invisible walls or map geometry, especially in the middle of a fight or a chase. Watching a fleeing orc captain sprint at 20mph away, only to escape because you got trapped in a 2 inch brick step, is just aggravating. Likewise, diving for cover from an archer only to get shot because your character wouldn’t move is annoying. I don’t know if it’s the very context heavy controls, or poor map design/geo, but this was a very common issue for me.


The second part of the big problem is the enemy captains. Some of them have combinations of attacks that will one shot you, regardless of what you do, if you miss a single prompt or do not dodge in time. Which I would be okay with, except for what I mentioned above: some prompts are horrendously difficult to read, and sometimes you can get stuck in place.

The event that made me uninstall was a 2 hour hunt for one orc captain. He had an assload of health and minions or whatever, and every time I would almost kill him, I’d get stuck in a wall, shot by an archer I couldn’t see, get killed by a prompt I couldn’t read. After killing me he got upgraded with poison weapons, which would kill me (or put me into that last chance thing) in one hit, even if I had full health. I played safe and whittled him down again, and when he had a sliver of health remaining, he just vanished. He didn’t flee or have any prompt or speech, he just disappeared from sight, and reappeared 50 feet away, with full health, and  bodyguards. Then he made me sit through another long monologue, and came to fight me.

If you really REALLY liked the first time, maybe it would be worth picking up on sale, but imo the game is mediocre. It has some great mechanics and some fantastic writing and dialogue, and then lots of frustrating design choices or outright laziness that strongly detracted from my experience.

Where to begin...
(I'll avoid spoilers)
This is a episodic game in the form of a telltale game sorta. Your choices will effect your playthrough and the world around you. However different from Telltale games is that This is set on a original, built from the ground up, World.
It's set around a High school where you play as a Teenage girl named Max. Who comes back to her hometown, Arcadia Bay, Oregon, on a scholarship to Blackwell. A school for talented students. Early on in the game due to events you learn that Max can rewind time. With Max's new power, and some shady♥♥♥♥♥♥goin on around Arcadia Bay. It's up to you and your old childhood best friend Chloe, to figure out whats going on.
Right off the bat, yes. This game has some really cringy dialogue. I get the whole going for the "teen girl talk" effect, But in reality, not alot of teenagers talk like this. But If you can lower your expectations on it like I did after I heard reviews when Ep 1 came out, then it won't bug you so much.
The gameplay like I said is your standard point and click game almost. It's your job as the player to of course decide which choice you wish to go with or how you play. What dialogue options you'll take, What easter eggs and hidden collectibles you'll find. etc... Added with the time rewind thing, you'll also have to take into consideration how to use your power. You can redo a choice that you really didn't like to do, Talk to a character then do a complete rewind and use info they gave you in the past conversation, and use it on them for the new present conversation. The player will have to think carefully with their choices along with what they use there power for. Breaking open this door, will get you inside but if you forget to rewind, that door will remain busted and it WILL effect your playthrough. Just a example of that.
The visual art style and graphics are very Beautiful. From the scenery, to the in game photos, and the Breathtaking End Episode Cinematics.
The emotional impact this game had on Many players and I included. Is massive. The Game starts off strong a first two episodes. I feel like Ep 3-4 kind of start to lose the magic but there still fine and enjoyable episodes. Ep 5 is just a big ol WTF simulator (I mean this whole game does have to do with time travel, what did you expect?) Characters like Chloe and Max, make them very memorable and probably some of my favorite video game characters in recent years.
The Ending feels somewhat very underwhelming and powerful at the same time. It's definitley a strong emotional ending (regardless of which one you choose) But I felt like the episode was almost rushed and not given enough thought to with the Whole Time Travel thing. Some things happen that make no sense in terms of Time Travel sense, and you start to feel like your not accomplishing anything in the episode.
The Soundtrack alone is a 10/10 it picks up at the right moments and the Song choices for each episode are brilliantly done. You'll probably find yourself listening to it, well after you've beaten the game.
In the End Life is Strange is a Beautiful, Emotional, Breathtaking adventure game That is definitley all about Enjoying the Journey, rather than the Destination. The Dialogue is cringy so lower your expectations.Though the Characters, Soundtrack, and world of this game make it a must buy. I look forward to coming back to this title many times in the future and sharing its praise with friends. Bring on Life is Strange 2.

This is the game I felt Fallout 3 should have been...
Now don't get me wrong, Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas were great games, but I was so used to the original Fallout games that switching to first person was a little of fputting for me. But like I said, they were, and still are to this day, great games.
As the sequel to Fallout's predecessor and inspiration, Wasteland 2, doesn't stray too far off from its roots, and shows us what Fallout 3 would have felt like with isometric camera and such.
Story:
I won’t delve into too much of the story… Because I hardly clocked in 10 hours!
So you start off as new recruits to the Desert Rangers, and as new recruits, General Vargas assigns you to finish the mission, which involves strengthening radio signals in 3 different areas to pinpoint a shady radio broadcast that apparently involves your troupe, the Desert Eagles, and investigate as to what caused the death of your Desert Eagle comrade who was originally assigned to the mission. Thus, the game starst… without holding your hand like most of the newer games today. And that is good!
Graphics:
Let's talk about the graphics, sure it isn't as fancy as you'd expect from a 2014 game; not as fancy as Divinity: Original Sin, but this is one those games that I feel that graphics don't really matter.
It is still one good looking game, but not good looking for the standards of 2014...
Gameplay:
Let’s begin with character creation, it is overwhelming, much like Fallout, with all the attributes and skills you can add points to. And most of these attributes/skills are not your convention, run of the mill, RPG attributes/skills… so hovering over them and thinking which would suit your character. As to customizing the appearances, you are limited to that. But I’m guessing this is where future mods/DLC will come into play. I wanted have my character where a nice suit with a cowboy hat and call him “The Guv”… but it ain’t happening… yet.
With the somewhat overwhelming character creation, you’d soon realize that you have to create a team of specialists. You can’t just solo and create an OP character with every skill there is (maybe you can, I don’t know, I haven’t played that far to think it’s possible… probably you can, but you die a lot more often than being in party… but I think… *goes on to mumble to himself*).
Okay, now that I got my train of thought back, that gives emphasis on team play. The importance of a well balance party… and the need of such a party. You start caring for the other character other than your main character (yeah, you create 4 characters, but let’s face it, YOU WILL CREATE ONE CHARACTER AFTER YOURSELF) and carefully place what skill points you can spend on in certain skills based on their specialization. You feel more involved in their growth…
Items here, as expected of a post-apocalyptic game, can be scarce… ammunition, money, and healing items are spread out, sometimes too thin; and if you didn’t build a good character for the early parts of the game, you’d soon realize you are running out of ammo and healing items. The need to regularly check your inventory and to regularly stock up on essentials (if you have the funds for it) is warranted. This gives you another aspect to keep in mind and not just use items lest you really, really need to.
You can interact with your surroundings for the most part; there may be breakable walls (with the proper skill) that you may topple down; there may be a locked gate (again skill dependent) that may lead to more loot or an alternative path… the list goes on. But like I said earlier, this game doesn’t hold your hand. Sometimes you don’t know you can use certain skills on items or people to unlock new interactions, or in my case, finish a quest. Lots of trial and error sometimes.
Interacting with people, like most RPG’s, has a moral depth into it and can change the course of the game or how other people will interact with you. I haven’t played much, thus, never saw the ending yet, but this leads me to believe this can result to multiple endings. Only one way to find out.
For combat…
Now combat is where this game shines. Truth be told, I am not a big fan of Turn Based games, except of course, for the original Fallout games, but in here, it really got to me. If you have played the original Fallout games, you’d get the hang of Wasteland 2’s Turn Based combat system. Never did a turn based game provide me with so much thrill of action (well, maybe XCOM), the joy of victory when a near impossible shot lands on that one last opponent, and the shear frustration when you have a 95% chance of hitting that SOB and still miss. Oh the mixed emotions…
Sound:
The music is what you’d expect from a post-apocalyptic themed game; it can be dreadful, but it adds to the charm and immersion of the game… exploring a cave with such dreadful music, add in the great ambient sounds, and even if this game is topdown isometric, you feel that you are in there with your co Desert Eagles. It does keep you at the edge of your seat.
For voice overs, they have done a great job in casting for the voice overs, but unfortunately, not all dialogue has voice overs. Some of which, the character you are interacting with for the first time would have a voice over, but as the interaction continues, you’re gonna have to read the whole text yourselves.
Replayability:
One thing why I became an RPG gamer is because with most cRPG’s, there are multiple endings based on the way you act and your decisions in the game. This game is no exception, this is heavily morally driven as far as I played it, there are a lot of possible character builds and this will also change and invite new challenges on how you progress thru quests, loots will never be the same, and just like the launch trailer stating that not any 2 players would have the same experience playing this game… well that is true for playing a second, third, fourth, or a million times (okay maybe I am exaggerating there.)
Summary:
I have been a longtime fan of classic cRPG’s like that of Baldur’s Gate, Planescape, Fallout, etc…
I have been on the hunt lately for good RPG’s that can give me the same satisfaction as those games did. Only Dragon Age Origins and The Elder Scrolls series ever gave me such satisfaction.
This game, was like a God send for the RPG fans. I haven’t played a solid RPG as this in a long while. The morale decisions, the interaction with the environment, the confusing yet satisfying character creation, how it emphasizes team play and not just a single OP character, how it teaches you to save on your gear for when you absolutely need it… it has it all. And did it great and well balanced.
I’d play this again once I finish this…
And I will recommend this game over and over again.

All in all the word for  Guns And Robots is 'querky'. It has a lot of ups; and a lot of downs, people tell me graphics are rubbish, nut in the middle of a firefight your not going to be staring at the walls are you? And yes i kinda agree when you tear yourself away from shooting another Robots head off, yes the graphics are a little plastered on. My main problem with Guns And Robots is what im going to call 'class diversity' for example i was in a 5v5 match where 9 people were using the same type of gun, this may not seem so bad for a game like Robocraft but when you look there are over 15 types of gun to chose from its quite depressing. What i like is that you have to keep a constant eye on you health, which is different for every single part of your body and this makes the combat more responsive. In a way this is good because you get to know people and its much easier to make a clan, but you'll be versing the same people again and again.
So if you like community, querky and somewhat reponsive games; I'd recomment Guns And Robots.

There are a few bugs (such as my car being stuck in the ground due to a dodgy spawn or something) and the driving can be improved but then again Mafia series was never much about the driving and the elements of GTA that it is often compared with. The series has always been a bit of an understudy to GTA supported by a Godfather-esque story; this time around with a bit of a twist therefore shying away from repetition which is a bonus.
If you purely expect a 1960s/70s GTA clone, then this will NOT be a game for you. However, if you are looking to play something that is fun and has a fairly lengthy single player storyline, then this certainly should get a look in. More so than any recent AAA competitors in the sandbox openworld games (I'm looking at you Just Cause 3...).
30 fps, of course I would prefer more but for me, I'm maxing out at 30 fps on my PC on High so not seen any major optimization issues.

Yes, this game does have some trial and error to it, but that's what gives it the addiction it needs to make you want to play it more. You get so far, but in the end, you die and you just want to try again and beat your last run. If none of this is making sense, then just understand that this game is something you will probably stick to for a while, it's a long-lasting game that doesn't go out without a fight to the end.

Though the game can in fact be a little addictive, the seemingly simple core gameplay (which is a slither.io clone, or imagine the old school Snake with multiplayer if you've never played slither.io) ends up coming down to who is willing to shell out money for the best gear if you want to genuinely play competitvely. That's not to say it's pay to win, because some good moves and being in the right place at the right time can and will get you places, but it's always going to be a very short lived triumph without the gear to back it up. You CAN earn the ingame currency through playing, but the majority of the daily quests they hand out are for game modes that are veritable ghost towns, so unless you're willing to grind away in this fashion for months on end, you aren't going to get past around mid-tier gear. Couple this with some very questionable hit detection and lag spikes that will cause you to freeze up for a few seconds and then shoot very rapidly in whichever direction you happened to be facing when the lag hit (often directly into a wall or another worm) and I really can't give this game a thumbs up. It's free to play though, so if you're just really bored, no harm in giving it a go, I suppose.

Delta Force - Black Hawk Down is a first person tactical shooter from 2003 where you take upon the role of a Delta Force Operator who served with UNOSOM II (United Nations Operation in Somalia II) in 1993. You lead your team, typically other Delta operators and, sometimes, US Army Rangers through numerous missions aimed at fighting against the Habr Gedr clan under Mohamed Farah Aidid, from humanitarian relief missions in the Somalian countryside to Mogadishu itself, where you take part in the Battle of Mogadishu, the event which sparked a novel and the film "Black Hawk Down."
The game is a timeless classic, and for any fan of classic fps or Delta Force titles, as well as anyone interested in modern US military history, this is a must have. Despite its age, I can play it again and again without ever getting tired of it.
It's expansion Team Sabre is a bit of a mixed bag. While the missions in the regular game get fairly challenging, especially in the end, the missions in Team Sabre can be downright unfair. Where the regular game made great use of hidden enemies, ambushes, and the pesky .50 machine gun emplacements scattered in the most inconvienient place, Team Sabre's missions throw a bunch of people at you at once, and they shove .50 machine guns EVERYWHERE, in which they seemingly have the perfect accuracy of a sniper. While the premise of playing as Delta operators in Colombia and SAS commandos in Iran is promising, Team Sabre is nowhere near as good as the standard game.
FYI: The Multiplayer component of this game is dead, at least in the base experience (and as far as I know). I don't know if there are outside servers or legacy servers of whatever running this game, and I don't know how many people even play it anymore. If that's something you're interested in, you'll have to research it yourself.
Overall -
Regular game: 9/10
Team Sabre: 6/10

Delta Force has always been considered a "light" tactical shooter. Though it had realistic elements, it was never on a par with the likes of Rainbow 6, Swat 4 or Ghost Recon. It walked the line because tactical and action.
Black Hawk down retains elements of the original, weapon loadouts, 1-3 hit kills, lean/crouch/prone, multiple stage objectives and large outdoor levels. Where it differs, is in an increased intensity, a consensus attempt to pump up the action.  Whereas in the originals you would pick off enemies at a distance, here it is largely close quarter combat  with an increased enemy count and tighter, linear scripting with added arcade elements in the form of health and ammo pickup's.
Comparative to what became the standard - Call Of Duty, it still offers a larger amount of freedom. There are no chest high walls tightly funneling the player, no scripted sequences constantly removing control and no glowing objects obnoxiously directing the player. Though linear, with on-the-rails shooting sections, it still affords the player enough of a sandbox to make combat interesting, while remaining focused. It's a better implementation of a now redundant formula Call Of Duty so succefully popularized.
Where the game stumbles is in it's implementation of difficulty. A dichotomy forms between it's realistic intentions and frantic arcade aspirations. The player is barraged with hundreds of enemies to shoot per a level, yet the die almost instantly. This leads to frustrating deaths thanks to a obtuse, bizarre save system.
Instead of simply hitting an F5 key to save, the player is limited dependent on difficulty. Even on easy, the level length and difficulty isn't consistent, ending in multiple instantaneous deaths both at close range and at a distance requiring reload after reload. Arguably this intensifies the gameplay by removing save-scumming to skip through via trail and error, but it also creates frustration that potentially puts those without a strong disposition for tolerence off the game completely. I'd recommend playing on easy, if only for the extra save slots.
Visually the pc version had aged reasonably considering it's age. The steam version however, as is the case with many games, is simply games with no thought of facilitating for the buyer. In my case, changing the graphical settings, at all, means an entire reinstall. The resolution without user made patches means no wide screen. Multilayer is also dead thanks to the insidious NovaWorld. It's a pity, the game is renowned for it's multiplayer, taking no effort to adapt to steam more than smacks of laziness, marring an otherwise excellent game.
Sounds is acceptable though not as good as it could have been, typical rock and roll booming to signify you are the good guy kicking butt coupled with melodic Middle Easten themes to signify this is a bad troubled land. Voice acting largely consists of military jargon being spouted than any attempts character development, depending on your point of view, this is a good thing. The environmental effects do a good job of lighting up passive sequences with eruptions of firefights without ever reaching the obnoxious levels of Call Of Duty - your ear drums are safe.
The game on a whole rather than a cohesive plot is segmented into selectable missions acting as bite sized experiences typical 10-20 minutes long. Whether you enjoy this is subjective, for myself, aside from Brothers In Arms, I've never found them effective enough to care, it's only ever bogged down the gameplay with unwanted narrative. Black Hawk down cuts to the core of the game immediately allowing for bite sized sessions without feeling obligated to consume the entire package.
AI is hit and miss, sometimes the enemy can one hit kill the player from half a mile away, other cases multiple enemies will stand in front of the player looking blankly into space. Vital spots are non existent, vaguely hitting in the direction of an enemy is an instanous kill. Flashbangs can be useful in mitigating the hoards of enemies piled upon the player and sniping rather than close range weapons are preferable, it does the job, but is spotty at best.
Your own team mates have commands but rather than the substance of Rainbow 6, it's novelty. Useless. The friendly AI operates on it's own, occasionally being helpful without the need for player input.
The weapons lack the realistic oomph of something like Arma and he arcade slickness of Call Of Duty, sitting somewhere in-between the two, they are never satisfying as they should be. Again, they do the job.
Mission structure itself is extremely good. The perfect balance between freedom and linearity. Jumping from an on the rails section, immediately to a maze of city streets, always in a changing state to keep the game engaging. It's well thought out and execution puts Call Of Duty's iron-grip handholding to shame.
Overall, coming back to this I liked this game more than expected, given the bombardment of military shooters through the years I expected to drudge through it, instead I found an engaging experience with just the right amount freedom to stop monotony setting in. It's drop in drop out style of design is great for short gaming sessions. If you can tolerate it's flaws both within the game itself and it's lackluster treatment as a sold product, you'll find a rewarding and surprisingly fun experience, even if you are sick of military shooters.

This was a hard review to write.
This game is one of my favorite's when it comes to story and voice acting. It's interesting, intense, has an amazing sense of humor, and some of the best side characters of all time. The atmosphere when you begin to find pages is wonderful, as you read about Alan being attacked by an axe murderer just before you're jumped- a classic, but fabulous thriller trick.
However, at the same time, it was one of my least favorites. Though exploration and early level gameplay is entertaining, the level design starts repeating, until you hit the final chapter which is the worst level design I've ever played. There are some gems in the gameplay, such as the Anderson Farm and the Heart of Darkness- but the gameplay of the game suffers enormously from controls that just seem off.
However, as I said before, this story is one that needs to be told. My personal recommendation is to either watch a youtube game movie of it, or to pick up the game if it's on a major sale. You need to hear this story, but you don't need to play the game.
Overall, even with these enormous game flaws, I left the game feeling satisfied- I'd give the game a 6/10, and I'd give the story a 9/10. I wish the developers were given the chance to give this game the sequel it so obviously needs and deserves.

Ethereal Legends is an action RPG set in a phantasy world. Without bigger introductions or quests you are set to defeat the evil and protect the world from dark forces.
Since there was not intro video, tutorial quest or any kind of other introduction, the only story I got so far was when speaking to an NPC that told me to kill skeletons in the graveyard, so he opens the portal for me to proceed further. Well, as you can imagine, being the Hero that destroys the evil and that sadly without any kind of decent background story is not going to impress anyone. The gameplay consists of some combat and inventory management.
The combat felt absolutely clunky and unresponsive, nothing that you see in the steam product video. The biggest challenge was to actually to find out which keys do what on the keyboard and I can tell for certain, playing with keyboard / mouse is not a way to play this game. Sadly, it has not been adapated for PC peripherals at all, so it is real trouble to handle it. Besides, that inventory management aswell the options menu are real pain to go through aswell. Since the game only suggested to play with a controller and did not state it is an absolute requirement, I rate the game as fully supported keyboard/mouse game, what is definetely is not.
I dont know where the screenshots in steam are coming from, but definetely not from the game in its final state. On my GTX 1080TI on obviously "Epic" settings it looked pretty bad. The effects were clutches of sparkles, the monsters did not have that many details, the map details loaded mostly only when coming really close to some parts of it. The inventory is coming from early 2000s and looking like an oldschool isometric RPG, while the game tries to be modern action.
The progress consisted of killing monster, running to next spot/dungeon/portal and killing some more there. It is fun for the first few hours since you mostly meet new opponents and get some new gear, but becomes really repetative and boring soon.
The audio sadly was not satisfying at all. The effects sounded like straight from '99 and the music was boring so it got turned off few minutes into the game. Sadly, the game did not provide the cool feeling you see on the screenshots where the area looks immersive on top of cool combat, so to tell you in short - immersion is almost non present in this game and you will be counting minutes wasting on this game.
I feel like this game could have been so much better. With decent optimization, with graphics and style like displayed in the screenshots, with decent action combat system that feels responsive and adjusted controls for PC instead of controller, it might have been a small gem. Sadly, non of it is present and it looks like the game was thrown on the market like 6 months too early before getting polished to make quick money grab. Save your money and stay away from it unless you prefer playing boring action RPGs with a controller, I cannot recommend it.
I hope this review helps you making the decision if its worth buying this game. Rate and leave a comment if you enjoyed reading it.

Crashlands gives you a massive, hilarious, and, omg, narratively compelling, lore-rich open world to run around in, digging stuff up and chopping stuff down; bashing enemies over the head, setting them on fire, freezing them, poisoning them, or, my favorite, electrocuting them en masse; stuffing the corpses of your enemies and displaying them for all to see; taming your enemies' babies, bonding with them to get Fancy Battle Powers, and making them slaughter their own kind on your command; and helping a mess of cool NPCs sort out their troubles.  It is
.
I'm a story person, so that's what most impresses me about Crashlands.  Each of the game's biomes has a dominant culture, with its own stories, history and, no lie, values.  You get a few glimpses into the ancient history of civilizations that came before the ones you're helping now, too.  Lest this make you squint with the sudden suspicion that the game is anything less than a total blast, let me return to
.  Crashlands' content is by turns aww-cute funny, terrible-pun funny, creepy funny, what-the-heck-surreal funny, and heaps of regular HA! funny.  You can do as many of the side quests as you want, or ignore all the NPCs' pleas and stay focused only on your main quest; I recomend doing every single side quest.  The whole experience is delightful.
Visuals are wonderful -- nighttime lighting effects are particularly beautiful, and creature design is distinctive, expressive, and again, hilarious.  I want a stuffed slurb, for example, so badly it's probably illegal in most US states.  Slurbs are just the best.  They're bouncy little razor-snails with pointy spikes on their shells and three blinky eyes.  And slurb on slurb carnage -- I can watch my pet slurb bounce the tar out of another one. . . basically forever.  I will never get tired of that.

My video review:
So I received a key for Ethereal Legends, I thought to myself "pretty impressive title" and the screenshots and videos looked pretty good too, so why not?
Cons:
Straight away something seemed a little off, it felt unfinished, and this was just after the title screen! Navigating the options to change the screen size was a problem, but I got there in the end.
The main character attacks slowly, there aren't any combos and in general, the combat feels very unintuitive. There aren't any sounds when the skeletons strike you and you take (some) damage regardless of whether you were blocking or not.
Spells take just forever to cast, I mean like a good 3-5 seconds. You can't pause the game if you're in combat (the combat music is playing) which is a problem if you just picked up some leather gloves and wanted to equip them!
Everything in the world is just too big. I mean, the skeletons could get away with it - they're skeletons of giants or something, but the rest of the world? It sort of feels like at the last moment, the scale of the hero was reduced just so the world would feel bigger and more "epic" but all that's really happened is that you end up finding hilariously huge barrels and wagons.
It takes a long time to "run" anywhere and potions and spells seem pretty expensive for what they are (there's a wizard in the main castle btw).
You *do* get the ability to dash but it uses up mana so after 3 casts you're back to running around slowly again.
Pros:
You can punt chickens!!
There's a recall spell that you can cast when you get glitched into an area that you're not meant to be in and can't escape from (check out towards the end of my video).
Overall:
Ethereal Legends just feels unfinished, like it was rushed out to go on sale. I was genuinely shocked when I saw the price for the game after recording the video (I got a key for free to review). I figured the game was still just a demo and very clearly in alpha, no pre-alpha still.. I didn't expect it to be available to buy yet.. it feels a long way away from that, let alone for it to cost so much!
So no, I don't recommend buying this game yet... perhaps give it a few months *then* it might be finished enough to be worth purchasing!

Ethereal Legends is not by many definitions a good game, but I have to say it's something I enjoyed because of how bad parts of it are.
The game plays in a similar way to Dark Souls, you go through levels fighting enemies and camping at resting places until you defeat the different bosses.
The thing is everything in the game feels extremely clunky and I mean everything.
The attack and blocking animations barely allow you enough time to attack the enemies in the game before they hit you again and there is no feedback when you land a hit. Enemies will often attack you from the wrong direction entirely yet still do full damage, making dodging nearly useless.
Moving around feels as though the character is moving at 70% the proper speed for their animations. Attacks and kicks also feel extremely slow.
The entire world looks like it is roughly twice as big as it should be in comparison to your character. The characters in the game look like they are roughly the size of a hobbit.
The sound assets are really, really bad to the point where they easily could have been taken from a website like FreeSounds.
Despite all this, the game is fun to play from the same standpoint that bad movies can still be fun to watch. Ethereal Legends desperately wants to be a grand Dark Souls style game but it lacks the budget, design and development team to pull that off.
I recognize the game is developed by one person, but there have been many far better games developed by similar team sizes. In the future I would say the developer should focus on making a smaller scale game that can do a couple things very well, rather than many things poorly.
I can't say this gets a recommendation, but it does have a certain charm to it in how innocent it is.

Overall a good game, worth the purchase. Graphically, it does the job decently enough, although there isn't anything worth boasting about. Custom portraits are a nice touch however, and character customization as a whole is good. Soundwise, again, does the job without managing to be exceptionally good. Guns are appropriately loud or quiet depending on caliber and mods, and music fits the tone of the area, but can get somewhat repetitive. Voice acting is anywhere from "competent" to "laughably hammy". Gameplay is where the game shines. Character creation alone is very deep and engaging, and the sheer amount of skills and talents you can use is impressive. Usually if you think to yourself "Can I do that, and will it solve the problem?", the answer is yes, and maybe. The fighting is usually engaging and appropriately stressful, with team members going down, mad dashes to save them, lucky sniper criticals at the right moment, and more. In the writing department, again, excellent work. Most characters have multiple facets, and can be influenced by your actions (or inaction in some cases). The main story does seem to stretch on for quite awhile, and spins it wheels at the start for a bit, but the side characters, quests, and locales make up for it. As a whole, a great game that I would recommend to fans of the genre (post-apocalyptic, turn-based strategy, or fans of X-COM Enemy Unknown, or Divinity Original Sin) for full price. If any of those previous genres interest you but aren't your main domain, consider picking it up at a discount later down the line, it is one of the better examples. NOTE: The game can be somewhat buggy, and some people have reported game breaking bugs. So far, in 48 hours of gameplay, I have not had any gamebreaking bugs, however, there were minor issues and immersion breaking bugs. Bear in mind.

It is now time to land the review for this game after having finished it at 100%.
I know a lot of reviews are talking about the loot boxes and how they should not be there but i wanted to finish the game to see how “needed” the loot boxes are in the game to finish it 100% (online high level play excluded of course)
I will talk about all aspects of the game first and not mention them. In the final chapter of the review i will explain how the loot boxes play a role and how necessary they are.
If you are pretty much familiar with the workings of the game and just want to see the loot box conclusion and the general conclusion of the game scroll down to the bottom. It is a long winded review
Having finished it completely and dabbled in online play I enjoyed the game quite a bit. If you played the first game (Shadow of Mordor) and enjoyed it then you will enjoy this as well. The gameplay is not that much different from the first but with some more polish. Of course with the now newly added content of fortress defending and attacking which will play a major role in the last act of the story. Next to that every area has its own share of collectibles in the form of memories , artifacts, poem verses for items and of course missions of the past (where you play as Calibrimbor)
I shall refrain from any spoilers of course but i can tell that the game offers about 4 to 5 different story lines you can explore that track through different zones. If you are a hard core lord of the rings lore fan you might have some questions about the story decisions they made here in reference to the movies/books but they gave it their own spin. if you don't take the books/movies too serious then the quests are quite entertaining and intriguing.
[h1Combat[/h1]
In contrast to the first game the combat has not had any great significant changes.  If you have never played the first game the feel of the combat can be compared to games like Assassins Creed or the Batman Arkham series.
In this game you get a Large skill tree where you can spend points in that you earn through leveling or completing certain objectives. Skill are divided in different categories like combat , predator , ranged etc where everything has 1 “main skill” and 2 or 3 “flavor skills” which alters the main skill in a way that will fit your play style. Only 1 flavor skill can be active though but once it has been unlocked once you can toggle it on or off or switch to others whenever you want (even in the middle of fighting something).
Besides the skill system this game now also offers a Loot system where you can equip 6 different item slots On higher rarity items a item can have a sort of mini challange to “unlock” some extra buff or power on the item. Its minor enough to be ignored though but a fun little addition to this all.
The biggest Unique point of this game is of course the Nemesis system which they have also expended on.
If you don't know what this is basically all orcs have the potential to become more significant to your world by developing a personality.That random orc that just happens to kill you that one time is now promoted to a captain and you can ambush him or enlist him in your army later on. Every orc has its own personality trait which can be sadistic ( “I just want to rip you apart!”) or silly ( like a bard orc who started to sing to me when he attacked me) or just weird ( an orc who only moans. or repeats a certain word or phrase repeatedly. just weird stuff ) but it makes every orc unique it its own way.
Well these orcs can develop relations to you or with each other. for example if you kill a captain somewhere maybe in the middle of a different fight or quest somewhere you get ambushed by another captain who comes to seek revenge for his fallen blood brother. and many more interactions like that. The orcs are not always bound to what you do but can choose to Ambush or betray you as well. every playthrough different things will happen.
Shadow of war does not know a “real” online multiplayer mode but it is more of a social aspect. There are 2 different ways of going online. “Online Vendetta” and “Online conquest”
Online Vendetta missions are mission to avenge other players in the world. You get send out to kill a captain that killed another player. They are quick and easy and reward “Spoils of war” and a loot chest . I shall expand on this in the lootbox section. but they just contain some gear that is around the level you do them on.
conquest is the fortress online mode of the game where you can attack another player's fortress. It has a ranked version and a friendly version with people on your friends list. Now 2 important things I will put here since the game is a tad vague on it.
The orcs you take along with you on the attacks can permanently die in your game world as well. so be careful on who you take with you. The defending player does NOT lose any orcs. so don't feel bad for killing his precious legendary warlords. they won't loose them. In the friendly mode you will NOT lose your attacking orcs.
I think this is the chapter which kind of ties it all together. Sure there is a long story. lots of collectables and fortress defending and attacking to be done but how necessary is the lootbox system in all this. are you messed over with your gear if you don't buy “legendary” items from the story. or are you doomed to fail in the end if you don't have max level legendary captains on all your fortresses?
There are boxes you can buy and boxes you can earn in game. with all different levels and contends. The boxes you can earn in game are
Vendetta loot box
Conquest loot box
Spoils of war chest
These boxes mostly contain gear for your character. the Spoils of war chest is obtained after earning 1000 spoils of war from playing online and contains orcs  and follower upgrades as well. but these can not be bought in the store.
Store bought chest are chests that contain 3 to 4 orcs at a time where you have the in game currency version off and the premium version off. where the premium version of course gives guarantees on epic and legendary orc drops.

Very impressive game for a game that requires less than 1GB (around 500-600MB). Made a good list about the game that I have been listing since I first played the game.
PRO:
- Terrain can be deform (mud puddles), trail marks
- The exhaust pipes shakes violently and spew thick smoke when gasing the trucks
- Realistic water physics
- The physics on the vehicles (speed, weight, balance, etc.)
- Maps are decent sizes, and each area has its own unique full of challenges
- Small trees can be run over
- 4 Co-op muliplayer
- Suspensions are realisitcs
- Vehicles of all sizes, ranging from the UAZ (Jeep) to the monstrous 8x8 Maz.
- Winching is fun and very useful. You can attach it to both other vehicles and trees if you are ever stuck or need to pull out a player from the ditch.
- Attaching a crane to your truck, to pick up lumber, move rocks out of the way and sometimes to help push the truck up.
- Trucks take damage, and consume fuel. You can install a utility addon for mobile repairs, or a fuel cistern for re-fueling in the field.
CONS:
- Camera need to have different choices for the player to pick
- Maps should be different such as winter, desert, and a village would be nice
- More players to be in the muliplayer (Should have 6-8 players rather than 4, feels lonely in certain areas with other players)
- The only official objective is to bring lumber, could use more different objectives
- Only one map will save your progress at a time (each map should have their own saves)
- Point of veiw distance should be customizable, noticed some areas are blurry even with settings maxed.
- Vehicle should be customizable such as colors, headlights, your own insigna on the doors
- More vehicles, maybe a tank? :D
Overall a great game that I can play on my laptop when I am away from home. :D

Wasteland 2 is a callback to Fallout and Fallout 2.
Everybody says it because it is true.
It can be a lot of fun, but it is also a tough game. It doesn't hold your hand, you are probably going to die, and you will learn very quickly to save often. I had to drop the difficulty after getting kicked around too much, but soon found myself in a good level of challenge.
It is not the prettiest game, but it will be really rare that you'd be close enough to notice if you zoomed out for combat.
It is a little buggy, but after thirty hours I've only had one game breaking bug. And since the game autosaves every time you enter a new area it wasn't a big issue.
The game may be hard, but after a little bit of playing you'll find yourself with explosives, multiple different weapons, and lots of choices. I've gone into a fight that killed me, reloaded, planned out my fight better and came out without anybody being KOed.
I love games where changing tactics can win you a fight.
The biggest flaw, in my opinion, is something that I can't prove. I find this for all games that list the percentages for attack.
I swear I  have managed to miss 90% to hit attacks three times in a row, jammed a gun with 5% repeatedly in a combat and so forth. Of course I don't really pay attention as much when I succeed, so it might just be subjective.
And it's not game breaking, that's for sure, even if I do curse my computer every time I miss an easy shot, or jam at an inoppertune time.
And then I keep playing because I'm still having fun!

It is as the title says....a Mountain, which is a god, a single great entity, and being that is finding a sense for itself and asking the basic questions beings ask themselves...why am I, who am I, am I alone, and so on. While this is happening, weather changes, day and night cycles, and random objects crash into its surface. You can use the keyboard to craft/play songs, many of which unlock various weather and artifact features, thoughts, and so on. I recommend leaving this game open and checking on it every so often to see what it is doing and has done while you were away.
When you grow weary of it, you can destroy your mountain, wipe its surface clean, or whatever.
This is something people should be experiencing. A simple and yet deep experience.

Do you like hurting other people? If you do, please keep it to the game (・ω・)b . I really enjoyed this game for the soundtrack, gameplay, and pure fun haha. Who knew a top-down shooter could be so fun?
Gameplay: Top-Down Shooter that takes place in 1989. Pixelated too makes it kinda cool. You play as Jacket, who kills the Russian mobsters. You can either eliminate them one by one, or go shoot everything up, which is faster-paced and chances of dying are much more.
In Hotline Miami, It's more about surprising your enemies and stuff. The gameplay is fun, yet challenging. It took me about 6 hours to beat the game, yet after I beat it, it's still a fun game to replay.
Soundtrack: OMG the music is addicting. The style gives the game more feel when you play it. What I like is that when you die, the music never gets interrupted. The only time it gets interrupted is when you face a boss (which goes to another soundtrack), get to a cutscene, or complete a map.
Difficulty: The game can be pretty difficult at sometimes, You will die with one swing or a gunshot. However, there are different masks in the games that give you abilities. I challenge you complete it with the standard Richard mask tho haha. Once you get used to the game, you can beat it easier with strategy.
Replay Value: I've played it over again a few times now and then when I run outta games to play. The good thing is you can jump around chapters after you beat teh game. I just pick a random chapter and continue the massacre. ;3
What I liked:
Gameplay,
Replay Value,
The action can keep you on your feet.
Difficulty makes you want to keep trying to beat the game.
What I didn't like:
Sometimes I didn't spot enemies and a random gunshot comes out of nowhere and gives me a jumpscare.
Difficulty can make me frustrated sometimes.
Bosses can be frustrating.
Story can be a bit confusing.
My final thoughts:
Hotline Miami is a really fun game that keeps you on your feet when you do missions. Soundtrack is amazing, Gameplay can be either fast pace shoot up, or eliminate one by one. Ultimately, I think this game has great replay value, although it can be frustrating at times. I would give the game a 9.5/10.
Also, I got it for $2.50 USD on sale, which is 75% off! I recommend waiting for the sale. Cheers!
